on behalf of the efd group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, yemen is not just a new frontier for terrorism, as some have called it, but a country of precarious stability. the lack of control over the territory by the central government and the permeability of the borders allow the development of illicit trafficking, uncontrolled migration, piracy and terrorist activities. the response to the new challenges of al-qaeda in yemen should not be limited to military pressure but should also help to improve the control of the territory by the local authorities. i repeat, local authorities and not just government. the stability of yemen should be achieved through a national and regional ownership approach, without imposing external or pre-packaged solutions that are often foreign to local realities and fail. this would facilitate a greater commitment by the gulf cooperation council itself, whose financial participation in local projects would be crucial. the european union should work together with yemen's partners, the g8 and the gulf countries, with financial and project contributions shared by the yemeni government. i conclude: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.

high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy/vice-president of the commission. – madam president, when we look at iraq today, we see real progress, though the country still faces a multitude of challenges. but i want to focus today on the present and the future of iraq, as a country with great potential and notable achievements over the past months. violence today is at its lowest since 2003. although we have seen terrible attacks targeting government institutions, the total number of civilian deaths in 2009 was less than half of the level of 2008. inter-sectarian violence, a major problem in 2006 and 2007, has been significantly reduced. iraq has a new constitution and has conducted several elections with high participation at great risk. thanks to the courage of the iraqi people, democratic institutions have taken root. provincial elections last year went fairly smoothly all over iraq. crucially, the next general elections, due on 7 march 2010, can be another big step towards consolidating the iraqi democracy. for our part, this means our work to support iraq must continue, and move into new areas as the situation improves. the european union has provided more than eur 1 billion in assistance to iraq since 2003. it has gone towards basic services, human development, refugees, good governance, political process and capacity building – all in accordance with iraqi priorities. our integrated rule of law mission, eujust lex, has been extended several times at iraqi request and is now also training inside iraq. the eu has been playing a leading role in electoral assistance, and we will continue to assist iraq in this and other areas until iraqi institutions can assume full responsibility themselves. as there is good progress, we are focusing more and more on iraqi ownership and long-term sustainability. we are also developing our relations with iraq. we have just signed a memorandum of understanding on energy cooperation, and we will soon sign a partnership and cooperation agreement, the first contractual relationship between the eu and iraq. it will cover issues from political dialogue to trade and regulatory cooperation and development assistance. we want a broader and deeper political dialogue with iraq, which should also cover human rights. parliament has taken a keen interest in iraq, and we expect to see even more cooperation between the european parliament and the iraqi council of representatives in the future. clearly, iraq must deal with the many challenges. the upcoming general elections will be crucial, and should be free and fair. with our international partners, we will be following them very closely. the eu will be deploying an election assessment team to iraq to assess the election and make targeted recommendations. honourable members, iraq is on a positive trajectory. i am confident it will use its new institutions to find the compromises necessary for national reconciliation. for our part, we will continue to stand by iraq and continue our support together with the un and the rest of the international community. i look forward to our debate.

and we would also like your opinion - about the recent decisions of the electoral commission to eliminate numerous candidates and parties closer to the sunnis or christians, thus risking to weaken the already fragile democratic process in iraq. the european union must follow this electoral process through the actions it is taking, as you say, as you have said, but it must also give itself greater ambition in developing its relations with iraq. the eujust lex programme directly involves us in the process of improving iraqi legislation and democratic institutions and as a socialist and democratic group we welcome the fact that the council has decided to extend the mission until 30 august 2010. the union must continue to provide strong support to iraq through its cooperation programmes, with the aim of participating in the process of stabilization and development in the country, strengthening relations between parliaments after the elections. it should be remembered that many member countries are cooperating with iraq, including italy in the important cultural cooperation programme. the political balance in iraq is essential not only for the country but also for the role that iraq can play in the region strategically, with the aim of overcoming the existing conflicts and ensuring peace. in this sense, the improvement of relations with turkey by the kurdistan regional government is a positive step in this direction. but iraq, as we know, remains a country with very serious problems of security, respect for democracy and human rights and also economic insecurity. it is the most vulnerable groups such as refugees - and i close - also by supporting the local and european ngos working in iraq, and women in this respect can also be strategic actors in involving them in overcoming the difficulties of the population.

for example the eu-africa strategic partnership. and it is also one of the priorities of the stabilisation and association agreements between the european union and the western balkans. the important role played by assistance in training and raising awareness of persons who may be in contact with victims, such as border police, police officers and security forces from third countries, in the fight against trafficking in human beings should also be noted. i would like to conclude by saying that the spanish presidency will work in this direction, that it will deal in particular with the issue of children affected by this trade, which is one of the main priorities of the spanish presidency. among other initiatives, we have asked the commission to present, by early 2010, an action plan on unaccompanied minors arriving in the european union. finally, mr president, the spanish presidency intends, during its term of office, during this semester, to have a debate immediately on a directive to combat trafficking in human beings which i am convinced the new commission will present immediately. as soon as this commission proposal is produced, the spanish presidency will begin its discussion in the council and with parliament. that is the expression of our determination to fight against this modern slavery, as the previous speakers have so well defined it.
the commission's vice-president - mr president, the minister has just explained how this trade in human beings was indeed a form of slavery. i am very grateful to mrs hedh and mrs bauer for asking this question. we must achieve a holistic, multidisciplinary approach which does not limit itself to repression but which includes international cooperation involving third countries. this integrated approach was the one adopted by the commission in the proposal for a framework decision published in march 2009. this framework decision builds on the council of europe convention on action against trafficking in human beings of 2005, but goes beyond that. so, of course, as the minister has just said, we will use the new legal basis provided by the lisbon treaty to present, as soon as possible, a proposal for a directive which will take account of the discussions which took place before the entry into force of the lisbon treaty. and we hope that this new proposal for a directive will maintain a high level of ambition. we feel that the european parliament must play a central role and that its commitment is very important in further strengthening the european legal framework for measures to combat trafficking in human beings. i will therefore give you some information in reply to the question. firstly, the sanctions: trafficking in human beings is a very serious offence and must be punished accordingly. the sanctions must be severe and the approximation of maximum sanctions must continue. the penalties vary widely between member states, from three to 20 years for the basic offence and from 10 years to life imprisonment for aggravating circumstances. even if we accept that the way in which sentences are carried out may differ from one member state to another, such a huge gap between the penalties is unjustifiable from a european perspective, and we will therefore provide for very high penalties in the new proposal. i come now to the aid and protection provided to the victims. the assistance, support and protection provided to victims of trafficking, including housing, medical and psychological assistance, counselling, information, interpretation services and legal representation, are all essential. of course, as the spanish presidency wishes, we will also consider specific and more protective measures for children who are victims of trafficking. the legal aid and representation scheme should be free of charge, especially for children. finally, in the course of 2010, the commission will publish its first report on the application of the directive on residence permits for third-country nationals who are victims of trafficking in human beings and who cooperate with the competent authorities. and we shall see, as a result of this report, whether the directive should be amended. as regards measures to discourage demand, the commission intends to include in its future proposal for a directive a provision requiring member states to take initiatives to this end and encouraging member states to criminalise the use of sexual services or labour where the user knows that the person is, and has been, a victim of human trafficking. as regards jurisdiction, the capacity of each member state to prosecute not only its own nationals but also persons habitually resident in its territory who commit acts of trafficking in human beings abroad must be increased. this is essential to combat the phenomenon of the so-called new mafias, that is, criminal organisations composed of individuals of different nationalities, who establish the centre of their criminal interests, and therefore their habitual residence, in a country of the union. then i come to the data collection. the commission has invested heavily in the development of common indicators for data collection. we must provide the european union with reliable, comparable figures. several important projects have been carried out, the results of these initiatives need to be appropriately monitored to develop a common indicator model with eurostat, with the european union agencies, europol, eurojust, frontex, fundamental rights agency. finally, i would like to conclude on prevention. we have a financial programme 'preventing and combating crime' which will include, in 2010, a targeted appeal on the fight against human trafficking. the stockholm programme also provides for specific measures which, in the general guidelines adopted by the justice and home affairs council, concern measures to strengthen cooperation with third countries. the commission has therefore drawn up a more comprehensive policy to combat trafficking in human beings. as i said, the commission will present a draft directive very shortly, and i am pleased that the spanish presidency has announced a debate which will enable you to enrich the commission's proposal, which i believe is timely, as this phenomenon, far from diminishing, is still increasing in our member states. so it is time to react, and to react forcefully.
on behalf of the ppe group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, first of all i would like to thank mr hedh and mr bauer for their initiative. human trafficking, as everyone before me has said, is a very serious crime linked to sexual exploitation and illegal labour. these are crimes committed by unscrupulous persons who recruit victims through the use of violence or even deceit, perhaps through the promise of honest and well-paid work and the threat, not only to the victims, but also to their children or family members. unfortunately, as is often the case, it is women and children who pay the highest price. it is estimated that there are almost three million victims of trafficking in the world, and almost 90% of them are women and children. in 2008, the european parliament, with the first european strategy on children's rights, denounced that child trafficking has several criminal objectives: organ trafficking, illegal adoption, prostitution, illegal labor, forced marriage, exploitation of begging on the street, sex tourism, just to name a few. the document defined trafficking as a real scourge within the european union and therefore the fight against trafficking and exploitation should become a priority for the future agenda of the european union, first of all by adopting all the necessary and urgent legislative measures also to ensure full protection and assistance to victims. the recent stockholm programme also mentioned the trafficking and exploitation of children. in conclusion, therefore, and also in the light of the debate this evening, we hope that the commission and the council will continue their efforts and that the commission will be able to make this new proposal for a directive, which we shall be examining very carefully.

the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the issue of good fiscal governance, although always of great importance, has become even more topical and important since the great economic and financial crisis two years ago. the international, g20 and european summits have discussed and continue to discuss this issue, particularly when dealing with the fight against tax evasion and tax havens. all this is important, it is a sign of commitment and will, but we must not be under the illusion that an announcement is enough. we need a serious and continuous policy. there are still many problems. it is still too easy to buy or open a shell company to evade taxes. just look it up on the internet: there are thousands of websites offering companies to buy in european union countries. often, an e-mail, with a photocopy of the scanned passport attached, is all that is needed to open a company. the practice of creating fictitious legal entities to evade taxation must be brought to an end. the report i am presenting is based on the european commission's communication on good tax governance of 28 april 2009. the report goes in the direction of putting forward concrete proposals and calls for a strong commitment from the european commission and the council to implement these proposals. the fight against tax havens, tax evasion and illicit capital flight must be considered a priority for the european union. hence the principle of good governance, which is based on transparency, exchange of information, cross-border cooperation and fair tax competition. the point is that we need ever greater cooperation and collaboration in taxation in the european union. the general objective we must set ourselves is to achieve an automatic exchange of information on a global and multilateral scale, starting, of course, with the european union. as mrs alvarez has already said, banking secrecy in the countries of the european union must be abolished completely, and the temporary derogation system which allows the application of a withholding tax, often evaded or underestimated, in place of the exchange of information, must be brought to an end without further delay. i do not want to dwell on the specific proposals contained in the report. i would stress that we need a few points in particular: extend the scope of the 2003 savings directive, fight against vat fraud, establish a union public register of persons and companies who have set up companies or opened accounts in tax havens, reconfirm and relaunch tax harmonisation projects, starting with the common consolidated corporate tax base. the european union must also speak a common language at international level and strive to improve the oecd rules, so that automatic exchange of information is replaced by exchange on request. mr kovács, you have heard the other reports, we need a strong commitment from the commission and at this moment we need the new commission to be given these priorities when it is exchanging its duties. as the european parliament, we will hold the council and the commission to account for their work. i thank my colleagues, and especially the shadow rapporteurs, for their contribution to this work, which i hope parliament will approve.

acting president of the council. - first of all, i would like to thank all the honourable members for their speeches, which i have found very useful in helping to shape the common position that the european union will have to take to the next conference of the parties to the cites convention. the vast majority have highlighted the value of the cites convention in helping to conserve endangered species. as i said at the beginning, following the commission's proposal to the council, the council will be able to outline its position on cites with regard to the various items on the agenda of the meeting concerning the main threatened species. here, for example, we have spoken of tigers, we have spoken of elephants - mrs bearder - we have spoken of the polar bear - mrs liotard - but a large majority of the interventions have been on the case of bluefin tuna. and on this question we have heard different opinions based on different arguments. the council is of course aware of the results of the last meeting of the scientific committee of the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat) in october 2009 and also of the recommendations of the independent panel of experts of the fao in december 2009. in this respect, the council is fully aware of the implications of the proposal to include tuna in the cites appendices, not only for the conservation of the species but also for the survival of traditional fishing methods in some fisheries which have proved to be sustainable for the species. the council will therefore carefully assess all the elements before adopting its position. in conclusion, i would like to reiterate to the honourable members the gratitude of the council presidency for its contributions and interventions at this decisive stage in shaping the position of the european union at the next cites conference, and i will be happy to convey to the council the content of its interventions and its keen interest in the issues to be discussed in doha. i would also like to convey to the honourable members the commitment of the spanish presidency to ensure the conservation and sustainable management of endangered species. and we are aware that the council has the full support of this parliament.
member of the commission. − mr president, my first general remark is to say that i really appreciate the contribution of all the speakers concerning all the objectives ahead of discussions at the conference. i can assure you that the commission will be in favour of sustainable trade for the benefits of both biodiversity and the communities which need to live in harmony with the species concerned. now, a few more specific comments in relation to your remarks; first of all, as i explained, the overall position of the commission on bluefin tuna will be adopted very soon. this is an important matter because it relates mainly to the catches by the eu fishing fleets. it has been felt that it is more appropriate that, instead of the outgoing commission, the new commission takes a clear position on this issue because the new commission will be in charge of defending or promoting the eu position at the conference. i am really confident that this proposal will ensure a sustainable future for both this species and the associated fishing industry. this will need to balance short-term and long-term perspectives on this issue. but, on more specific items and the questions raised by the distinguished members of parliament, on the question of support which could potentially be given to the fishermen affected, i think that we should stress that the commission would be ready to assess the possibility of providing such support to the maximum possible extent, but we also need to remember that budgetary reallocations have been decided for many years and that we would also need to assess the financial consequences while we have a rigid financial budget for the perspective 2007-2013. there is one specific issue concerning the proposal to include bluefin tuna in appendix ii and i think it is important to note that there are very specific provisions in cites which would apply in the case of an appendix ii. there would be a lot of legal and technical discussions on what such a listing in appendix ii would actually mean. the practical impact of such a listing would be uncertain. that is why we need to think of what the practical consequences of putting bluefin tuna in appendix ii would be. regarding mrs bearder’s question on elephants, there are procedural weaknesses in the motions of tanzania and zambia but in our legal assessment these flaws cannot be sufficient ground to procedurally reject these motions ex ante. finally i will comment on mr kelly’s question. is the commission happy with scientific evidence on many issues? i think it is difficult for the commission to question scientific evidence because it would mean that the commission has better scientific or research capacity than the research institutes, which is not the case. that is why it is sometimes very difficult to take a position on the scientific evidence.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the debate we are having today on the 15th meeting of the conference of the parties to cites next march is of particular importance for the rational use of wild flora and fauna. the draft resolution seems to be unbalanced in the direction of a ban on the use of many resources. i am referring in particular to the proposal to include mediterranean red coral in annex ii to cites. i would remind you that the scientific community considers that there is no risk of extinction for the species of the corallidae family, given the abundance of this species in all the waters in which they live. the inclusion of the coral in annex ii therefore seems excessive and not supported by scientific data. the trade in red coral is an important source of income in large areas of the mediterranean and inclusion in cites would have significant repercussions on the economies of many countries, including italy, with social alarm points and consequent loss of jobs. for these reasons we oppose the inclusion of this family of species in appendix ii of cites. i also ask the european commission to reconsider its position, which seems to be based more on extreme environmentalist thinking than on sound scientific assessment.
in writing. europe has always been attentive to the problems of over-exploitation of wildlife and illegal trade in wildlife. we believe, however, that the cites convention will have to base its decisions on the results and scientific data provided by the relevant international bodies. two points are particularly sensitive: the proposal to include corallium sgg. and paracorallium sgg. in annex ii and the request to include bluefin tuna in annex i. as regards coral, we feel it is appropriate to reiterate our objection in the light of the negative opinion of the fao scientific assessment panel of mid-december 2009, which found that there was no evidence of species decline to support inclusion in annex ii. this would seriously affect the competitiveness of the artisanal coral processing sector, which is an important economic and employment voice in some italian areas (torre del greco, alghero, trapani in particular). as regards tuna, there are countries such as france and italy which are more interested in fishing for bluefin tuna and therefore in protecting the species for its sustainable use. we can support this proposal, but we would ask that this inclusion be subject to a postponement of the decision for 12 to 18 months and to the provision of compensation for the sector.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the swedish and spanish presidencies have made turkey's accession to the european union a priority, as if it were irreversible. in our view, turkey's accession is neither realistic nor appropriate for a number of reasons. firstly, because turkey is not geographically located in europe; secondly, because turkey is an increasingly islamized state and ankara is in fact a leading member of the world's largest pan-islamic organization, the oic; thirdly, because religious minorities are persecuted and have an inferior status. fourthly, because turkey continues to officially deny the genocide of one and a half million armenian christians and occupies cyprus militarily and politically, in violation of international law. we must also remember that with turkey in the european union we would have countries like iraq, iran and syria on our borders. finally, we must also remember that in 2030, turkey, with 90 million inhabitants, will be the most populous country in the european union. this means that it would have the largest number of meps and the largest share of votes in the european council, so the european balance would certainly be destabilized.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the conclusion of the negotiations with croatia by the end of the year is a possible objective and the swoboda report balancedly emphasizes the progress and the steps still to be taken. now, it is the justice sector that still needs to be reformed. it is not enough to complete the necessary system reforms, pass new laws and cooperate, as necessary, with the criminal tribunal for the former yugoslavia. i insist on the need to create a genuine legal culture and mentality in line with european standards. the independence of the judiciary, which is a central issue, and the training, recruitment and career of judges, i.e. the absence of various types of governmental influence on judges, are becoming crucial. i call on the commission to consider the need for decisive action in this respect during the final phase of the negotiations.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we want to encourage croatia's accession and that is why we are asking the croatian authorities to return to their rightful owners the assets nationalized to italian citizens at the end of the second world war and still owned by state or municipal institutions, also in the light of european law. we want to encourage the accession of the former yugoslav republic of macedonia and that is why we ask that the consensus method, which is part of the history of the european union, be respected and that the european institutions cordially accompany the reflection of all the member states on the reasons which still hinder this process. we want to speak with turkey in the language of truth. the oomen-ruijten report has this merit: the commission's proposal is not to deny the difficulties of the process and does not set out any prejudices, but it does certainly take the copenhagen criteria as a reference point. it is therefore right that parliament should strongly denounce the violations of human rights and the democratic deficit. but it is not in this house that we should look for those who make the path of this application for membership almost paradoxical. they are to be found among the officials of the many governments who promise at every official meeting what they have an interest in denying in the hallways. on the other hand, it is useful to insist on strengthening the instruments of the privileged partnership, on the basis of the oomen-ruijten report, in anticipation of a development which is linked not to prejudice but to the full and responsible acceptance of the contents of the acquis communautaire.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, we are aware of the differences between the different legal frameworks in the individual countries and we also know that at present different interpretations of european and national case law lead to a high level of infringement and litigation within the member states. the lack of a european union policy is not further sustainable in light of the challenges inherent in the cross-border nature of interactive gambling services. moreover, the rapid spread of the internet and electronic commerce in recent years has led to an increase in the supply of online gambling and the consequent emergence of cross-border issues that remain unresolved. i am therefore convinced that the european institutions must respond to common challenges, such as the protection of consumers, in particular minors, and the prevention of crime and fraud, but also those relating to the fight against the illegal and unauthorised provision of services, which national governments alone cannot meet. the commission is therefore responding to parliament's requests and working towards a regulatory framework at european level. do it with the necessary determination. i am not questioning your good will, commissioner, and i would therefore say that the consultation is fine, and the green paper is fine, but only if it serves to identify the right legislative framework and is not an end in itself. the old commission has on many occasions overdrawn its green papers and white papers without taking a decision. i think you realize, commissioner, that we need decisions and not just words.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, first of all i would like to wish commissioner barnier a good job, because we need it. gambling, by its very nature, has psychological implications for individual gamblers and affects the cultural and behavioural aspects of individual societies. given the risks involved, the recent ruling by the european court of justice that each member state is free to set its own rules governing online betting and gambling is wise. the judgment in the portuguese league confirms that the european union is governed by 27 different rules, depending on how much each member state has considered itself to legislate. this condition is contrary to the application of the rule of the internal market tout court, to the gaming sector and to harmonisation at european level. a supply that is not strictly regulated would have a negative impact on the needs and behaviour of individual citizens of the european union, with particular reference to the most vulnerable groups and the young. we ask you, commissioner barnier, to work towards a regulatory framework that clarifies the competences and sets out common principles and a code of conduct for operators to protect all european citizens who have a passion for online gambling.

acting president of the council. - mr president, the presidency also welcomes this debate in the european parliament, as it constitutes an important contribution to the broad consultation process of the green paper, and the european parliament's input should therefore be seriously considered by the commission when it subsequently draws up its legislative proposals. the council will also study all the parliament's views in detail, with a view to examining and subsequently adopting the legislative proposals under the codecision procedure. the green paper of april 2009 addresses several structural weaknesses of the common fisheries policy: overcapacity, unclear objectives, short-term decision-making, lack of sectoral accountability and poor overall enforcement. the green paper also outlined possible ways of tackling these structural weaknesses and addressed such important issues as differentiated regimes for industrial fleets and small and artisanal coastal fleets, discards, relative stability, individual transferable quotas, greater market orientation, the integration of the common fisheries policy into the general context of the maritime policy, public financing and the external dimension of the common fisheries policy. the member states, both individually and jointly in the council, are studying all aspects of the issues raised in detail. the first phase of consultations was completed in december 2009 and the commission has received 1 700 proposals and held over 125 meetings and seminars so far. the second phase, which will begin on 1 september 2010, will focus on analysing the contributions received and discussing the main ideas. in january the commission held seminars on the main aspects of the reform and on management based on fishing rights. a seminar on small-scale fishing is being held today. the impact assessment will be in the month of march. the european fisheries fund and the future financial perspective in april, the external dimension in may and discards and selectivity in june. the conference, organised jointly by the presidency and the commission, will be held in a coruña on 2 and 3 may and will deal with three key elements of the reform, namely governance, stock management and the differentiation between large-scale and small-scale fishing. on 4 and 5 may we will have the ministerial meeting in vigo where the ministers will discuss the outcome of the conference, and it is possible that the june council will include an informal discussion on a working document on the options for amendment as an item on the agenda. in the third phase, as i said earlier, which begins in the second half of 2010, the commission will present a white paper and then four legislative proposals: the basic regulation, the new common fisheries policy, technical measures and the new financing regulation. the aim is for the cfp to enter into force, with the new reform, on 1 january 2013. the council has not yet adopted a position; the council will only take formal decisions on the basis of the legislative proposals it receives from the commission in 2011, and will do so in accordance with the rules of codecision.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the recent railway disasters in europe - belgium today, italy yesterday - require us to reflect on the failures of the system and on the appropriate measures to improve safety performance. for example, it is astonishing to think that the european union developed a dedicated rail traffic monitoring system rtms as early as 2000 and yet, ten years later, very few member states have adopted the system. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the safety of rail transport is not compromised. it is true that the adaptation of railway infrastructure and the rolling stock of the european system involves technical and economic assessments and tasks which must necessarily be carried out by the companies in the sector. however, it must be noted that community legislation does not fix a date for the adaptation of national lines to the rtms system and leaves it to the member states to determine the equipment requirements for vehicles in circulation. it would be better to impose and set dates, to encourage investment and even to take it away from those who do not fit in with infrastructure projects or rolling stock purchases that do not use these systems. the other reasoning is that we must not delay interoperability and the completion of the internal market. today we have an independent national security agency, which should check the adoption of the appropriate security systems. it is important to emphasize that obtaining safety certificates is a precondition for obtaining a licence. i also stress that, with a view to a liberalised common railway market, the powers of the european railway agency in the field of controls must be strengthened at central level.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, following the recent train accident in brussels, which many colleagues have mentioned, the spotlight has once again been on railway safety. directive 2004/49/ec on safety on the railway generally provides that railway undertakings and infrastructure managers are to share responsibility for safety of operation, each for the part of their responsibility. in the specific case of the accident in belgium, it appears to have been a human error. we'll wait for the investigation, of course. however, it appears that the train did not have an automatic braking system. is the commission aware of which networks and how many trains within the member states do not have this safety device? and does it intend to put forward a legislative proposal to equip the entire union network with such a system?
the tragic train accident in belgium draws public attention to rail safety. in addition to safety in signalling technology, the safety of rolling stock must also be improved. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's transport policy is not disrupted by the introduction of new technologies. unfortunately, the eu has done little to date to oblige freight transport operators to maintain their rolling stock at an acceptable safety standard. it is also important to bear in mind that dangerous goods are also transported by rail and that in the event of an accident, this can have devastating consequences. in view of this, i call for higher safety standards in rail transport.

in writing. − the proposal is affected by the emergency situation in gas supplies which emerged in january 2009, when the commission identified the inadequacy of the union's energy infrastructure. the european commission's intention, which parliament fully shared, was to have a constantly updated picture of the energy infrastructure system. there is a great deal of uncertainty about the implementation of investment projects, which has been exacerbated by the economic and financial crisis. i believe that action is needed to remedy the lack of consistent data and information on investment projects, without which it is impossible to analyse the expected evolution of the union's infrastructure and to carry out adequate monitoring from a cross-sectoral perspective. furthermore, regulation 736/96, which this proposal repeals, is no longer applied consistently and is inadequate to the recent developments in the energy sector. the commission has therefore strengthened the existing system by this proposal, considerably improving the comparability of information and at the same time reducing the administrative burden. finally, i would like to emphasise that i voted against amendment no 81 (which was intended to include the whole nuclear energy chain among the infrastructures covered by the regulation), since there are already provisions governing these matters in the euratom treaty.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, these proposals are intended to make it easier for third-country nationals legally resident in a member state to move around the schengen area with a long-stay visa of type d. in essence, the principle of equivalence between a residence permit and a c-type short-stay visa is to be extended - and this is a matter of concern to us - to long-stay visas. consequently, the long-stay visa will have the same effect as the residence permit as regards movement within the schengen area. in other words, it is intended to allow anyone who has a document proving his legal residence in a single member state to move freely within the schengen area for short periods of no more than three months each semester. we point out to the commission and the council the safety problems which may arise from this free movement. it is already very difficult to carry out checks in one member state: the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect.

in writing. − the competition policy report shows how to improve the functioning of markets to the benefit of european consumers and businesses. particular attention was paid to the issues of 'cartels and consumers'. fighting cartels is essential to ensure that the benefits of a competitive regime reach the final consumer. the following are among the most serious infringements of competition law: it allows operators to raise prices, limit production and share markets. the commission's role is to impose sanctions, thereby prohibiting anticompetitive behaviour, and to fine cartel members, thereby discouraging any undertaking from engaging in or continuing to engage in anticompetitive behaviour. during an economic crisis the risk is to increase the level of protectionism. it is therefore necessary to avoid public intervention that would alter the conditions of competition in the internal market, but at the same time to recognise that sometimes the use of state aid is indispensable to deal with the crisis. i am voting in favour of this because an anti-competitive environment encourages the abuse of dominant positions to the detriment of smes and it is therefore essential that europe should work towards greater product guarantee and protection.

challenges. the new powers which have been given to parliament by the entry into force of the treaty mean that parliament is engaged in a frequent, collaborative and efficient dialogue with our first interlocutor, the new vice-president/high representative whom baroness ashton has the honour of representing for the first time. his mandate was subject to our vote of consent in january and on several occasions, as a parliamentary assembly, we were promised continued involvement by the council and the commission in all the most relevant issues of european security and defence. the high representative is therefore invited, as the report itself insists, to appear before the european parliament and to consult it frequently and regularly. with lisbon, the european union's external action takes on a new and important dimension, but to achieve this goal in practice it is also important that it has the necessary budgetary resources. the european parliament has a key role to play in ensuring the democratic legitimacy of external action. the creation of a european external action service will give the european union a diplomatic body and apparatus which could only be relied upon by national representation. of particular relevance and relevance are the following official representatives: the high representative shall be responsible for the appointment. the report also calls for the eu to take action to ensure that the eu's citizens are not left behind in the process of democratization. the hope is that the form of double-hatting will gradually be achieved - except in the case of the special representative, which has a regional scope of action - and that economies of scale will thus be achieved, making the european union's external action more efficient and at the same time less burdensome. the report begins with an introductory and strategic section, and then deals with the subject of european foreign policy by subject and geographical area. the european union must, together with its allies in the international organizations, and above all in the united nations, be the highest guarantor of world security. it must be able to count not only on its seat on the security council but also on the staff and delegations that are the link between the two realities. europe, as the vice-president/high representative is asked to do, wants to become an active, strategic and independent partner of a great ally like the united states in responding to the global challenges of terrorism, finance, and the often difficult relations with industrial giants such as russia, china and japan. the report then proceeds with a geographical analysis of the desirable lines. in the balkans, the enlargement theme is mainly introduced by: the european union is present in kosovo with the eulex mission, but efforts still need to be made to ensure that the accession standards of many neighbouring countries applying for membership are respected. the chapter on cooperation with the east and the black sea regions deals with the security of supply and the european union's energy dependence. the section on russia calls for the signing of a new partnership and cooperation agreement. the european union calls for the establishment of a european union-wide network of information and communication networks, including the european information and communication network, and for the establishment of a european network of information and communication networks. middle east: the israeli-palestinian conflict, where the european union will need to play a stronger political role in order to relaunch the peace process following the council decision of 12 december 2009. union for the mediterranean: settlement of the turkish-cypriot conflict. asia: afghanistan, a critical period for the formation of the new government after the elections; pakistan's key role in the fight against terrorism; concern about the violation of fundamental rights in iran. africa: positive contribution of the somali coastal defence mission. latin america: the need to create a stable and lasting partnership for relations between the european union and latin america. i shall listen with great interest to the comments of my colleagues and reserve the right to reply at the end.
on behalf of the efd group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, mrs ashton, in the context of president albertini's report, which is really excellent, there is a passage which seems to me to be politically important: the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. it is not possible to control migration flows of such enormous dimensions by means of repressive measures and domestic policy measures alone. even the distribution of migrants among all the states of europe would not solve the problem, but would rather encourage new arrivals. a fundamental response to the control of migration is development cooperation policy, which is best coordinated at european level and aimed not only at economic but also at social and democratic progress. migration should be a choice, not a necessity. for this cooperation policy to be effective and reach those who really need it, it is essential to promote good local governance, without which there would be inefficiency, corruption, waste of resources and poor results. ensuring local governance and cooperation between governments is a foreign policy issue and cooperation must become an important instrument of european foreign policy: this is the message i would like to convey to high representative ashton in an area which is very close to my heart, cooperation.

mr president, the joint motion for a resolution on the non-proliferation treaty is a very important one, and the alde group and i are very proud to have contributed to its elaboration. the resolution is holistic because it encompasses all the disarmament matters, from the npt review conference to the issue of nuclear-weapon-free zones. this resolution calls for a middle east free of nuclear weapons and for the withdrawal of all tactical warheads from european soil, in the context of a brotherly dialogue with russia. this resolution also frequently refers to a nuclear-weapon-free world, a target to be achieved through a special convention and within an ‘ambitious’ time-frame – this means a short one. our resolution is the european answer to president obama’s proposal of the abolition of nuclear weapons. this document should be considered, therefore, as a step on the road to the total ban of atomic weapons. it means to end the paradox of the possession of nuclear devices by some countries, which is legal on the one side, and the complete prohibition of chemical and biological arsenals for all countries, on the other side. atomic bombs must be made illegal and their possession should one day be considered a criminal act. i am confident this parliament will continue in this direction with even more drive and more vision.

vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. − mr president, i should like first of all to express my thanks for the contributions that have been made and say how much i thought this was an important and valuable debate in terms of our strategic direction. i want to say at the beginning that i agree completely with all honourable members who spoke of the value and importance of the scrutiny of this house and the role of this house, not only in terms of that scrutiny but also in terms of the expertise that i know exists within it. it is my intention to call upon that expertise and to hope to have as many occasions as possible where we are able to debate and discuss many if not all the important issues that have been raised today. i will be relatively brief at this point but i will just try to talk about a few of the key areas that i think honourable members are most concerned about. i shall begin by saying that i did not say ‘no’ to the barnier report. what i said was, on the basis of lessons learnt from haiti and now the support we are offering in chile, we wanted to look at how much more we could do, how we could operate more effectively, what we should have on standby and whether we should have something on standby. that requires us to consider strategically what we should be doing, and the barnier report provides the backdrop to do that. i am very grateful to michel for the contribution that he has made on that – it is the backdrop. on the non-proliferation treaty: a number of honourable members have raised the importance of the conference that is coming up in may, all of which i agree with. it is very important that we move forward now in terms of what the opportunity of may will afford us. i also agree that security begins with strong political relations. we have to consistently view our approach in the wider world as being about developing those strong political relationships in order to promote security, not only for ourselves but also for third states, for states with whom we are seeking to have that relationship or with whom we are in dialogue because of the concerns that we have. a number of honourable members quite rightly raised the importance of the balkans. i have indicated in my priorities that this is an incredibly important area of work. it is very important in the period building up to the elections in bosnia that we promote the importance of the european union and make sure that national politicians describe to their people the path that they plan to take to get closer ties with europe and ultimately to become part of europe. i agree on the importance of valentin inzko and the work he is doing in the office of the high representative. he and i are working together to think about the strategic approach – again for a future that takes us way beyond the elections to where we need to be in the coming months and years in order to retain the security. i take the point about the importance of stability: not only do we have to have it there, but we need to keep it there. there is concern in the region that we are seen to be moving forward and on occasions i feel we have got a bit stuck in what we need to do next. we need to take that forward. that is particularly true, as a number of honourable members have said, in kosovo, where i have met the government. i have had conversations with the government and with the prime minister in particular, to look at what we would do with them in the future. then there is serbia, which is pushing very hard to become a part of the european union. when i met president tadić and the government members, it was very clear there too that this is something they see as being their future, and they too understand the issues that we are concerned about on that journey. concerning the debate on cuba, i would have been there. it is simply that we have a clash. there is the council of presidents meeting to discuss the external action service and i cannot be in two places at once. that is what the european parliament decided in terms of timing. i must obey and be present at that. however, i think cuba is an important issue and i have no doubt that we will return to that subject. concerning the separate department for peace-building, my response is that it should be in everything we do and i am always nervous about separating out something, as if somehow it is separate from every bit of work we are doing. if you look at how we are going to operate the external action service, it is like an umbrella organisation that takes in clearly the responsibilities under the treaty but also is your servant and the commission’s servant. so when the commission is looking to do things on trade, on climate change, on energy security across the world, the external action service can be its tool as well, directly linking the work of the commission to what happens on the ground. all of that, i would maintain, is about a more secure, more stable world. so for me it is all about how we build in the idea that we are there to support efforts to ensure that we have peace and that we keep peace. on atalanta: i think the points made there are very positive. it is a very important mission, but it is a mission that has to be connected to all the other things we are doing in that region. i also take the point that we need to think about fishing and the strategy on that. that is very much understood. working groups: i think it is a very good idea for parliament to have them. i think senior officials are linking with them well at the moment and we need to continue to do that. on the operational headquarters: it is not that i have changed my position. what i said in january was that i remain to be convinced. we have now been looking at this, because, as i have been in the job a little bit longer, i am more engaged in the work that we are doing in terms of our missions abroad, whether in kosovo, whether in bosnia or whether in discussing what we are doing in atalanta or indeed what we have just been doing in haiti, and so forth. in my speech i said that we need to look at what is necessary and then decide how best to achieve it. there are different views, but those views, i believe, will converge around a common theme, and that is what we ought to do. so it is about being convinced one way or the other as to how we do it. on human rights: i want to describe that as a silver thread. the projection of our values and human rights is essential to everything that we do in the european union and in the wider world. it is about how we make sure that it is a thread that runs all the way through all our actions in terms of support for the work that we are doing across the world to promote the values of the european union. i want to look very carefully at how we do that, so it is not something that just becomes an add-on extra to a dialogue. it becomes an integral part of everything that we do. i agree as well about the strong relationship transatlantically with the united states. they are a strong partner with us on a whole range of things, particularly on crisis management, and it is very important that we build on that. i am also very keen to build on the work that we do with the us in areas of development, for example particularly in africa, where there is a potential – i believe, anyway – to do a lot more, certainly in the light of my experience with aid for trade as the trade commissioner. we also need to think about other big partnerships. i have been talking to the brazilian foreign minister about the potential of again working together on development where the economies of scale and the ability to collaborate enable us to release resources in a much more effective way to certain parts of the world which are in real need. i agree too on the cyber threats. this is a very important issue. it is here now. it is an issue we are going to have to keep looking at because inevitably the threats change all the time. just a little bit on the external action service. the geographical breadth of the european union has to be represented within the external action service. i agree with that completely, but it will take me time to do it. one of the things that i have said to all the foreign ministers and i say to parliament is: please resist the temptation to assume that, because the first four or five appointments i make are not from a member state that you might know best, it does not mean that i will not make appointments in the future from those member states. we simply have to build it stage by stage. remember, as honourable members know, it does not exist at all at the moment. i do not have a team or a staff for the external action service because. until the legal basis is done, we do not have anything. we simply have what we had before, trying to bring it together in a more coherent way. i will appoint on merit and nothing else. there are no favourites here. it is on merit. i want the brightest and the best and that is what i have said to member states and the institutions. i want the delegations on the ground to be an umbrella, able to support the work of the european union in all its different elements, as it is represented to third countries, as it works with third countries. it is essential that it does that as otherwise we will end up fragmented again. the question is how to do it, and that is why we are in dialogue with the council and the commission at the moment. if it were very simple, we would have done it by now. we just have to make sure that we do it properly and effectively. we will work that out in the next few weeks. in terms of resources, i am going to argue for flexibility. i am going to argue that, if you have a crisis in a particular country or if you realise that you need to be able to move resources, we should deal with it, but deal with it within the context of parliamentary scrutiny. and again we need to think about how to make that work, not just now but in the future. we absolutely must avoid duplication; otherwise we will have gained nothing except more bureaucracy, which is not what we want to do. we have to make sure that this is a cohesive service that runs well, operating as an entity within the european union, supporting and being supported by the other institutions. and, as i have said, we must remember that it does not exist yet. let us hope that we can get the work done in the next few weeks. with parliament supporting me i am sure we will, so we can get this into being. we can lay the foundation stones but it will take time to build it, and that is so important that i hope that every honourable member will understand. a couple of final points. on summits: we have lots of different summits. the question that we always have to keep in mind is the value and importance of them. i cannot go to all of them. there are simply too many. i will be at some. we were well represented at the morocco summit because both presidents were there. i honestly believe that if the presidents of the council and the commission are there, we have to start saying that is a strong eu representation at the summit. it does not always require me to be there as well, and they would agree with that. on behalf of the efd group. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, in the debate on the european union's energy choices, there is one certainty: the most important, cheapest and most sustainable energy source available to us is energy saved. for natural, historical, cultural and economic reasons, mountain regions are a model for reducing energy consumption, compatible with the needs of modern life, and lend themselves to large-scale experimentation with the use of low-carbon renewable energy sources. mountain regions produce almost all of europe's hydroelectric power. to give an example, the province from which i come in italy alone produces 12% of the hydroelectric power of the entire country. in addition, there is a long history of experience in energy-efficient building techniques in mountain areas. houses have been built that are completely self-sufficient in both electricity and heating and that even provide more energy than they use, using advanced technology, of course. the mountains are often pilot areas, so they are the ideal setting for experimenting with better use of biomass, solar, geothermal, heat pumps and, above all, renewing energy distribution systems. commissioner, the mountain is full of energy, clean energy: just take it. we therefore ask the commission to involve mountain regions in its strategy, to study their experience and to recognise their right to fair compensation for all the renewable energy already supplied by these regions. article 174 of the lisbon treaty recognises the role of mountains: the commission has already taken a number of initiatives in this area, and we are therefore urgently awaiting an initiative from the commission to implement this article and to implement a european policy on mountains, including in the energy field. i therefore call on the commission to follow the recommendations of the durnwalder report in the committee of the regions and to integrate the energy problems and the productive capacity of mountain regions in terms of renewable energy and passive construction in the evaluation of european territories. mountains, which account for 40% of europe's territory and 90 million inhabitants, the rapporteur. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, with the globalisation of markets and the serious crisis that europe is experiencing in the agricultural sector, one of the answers that the agricultural market can give is to focus on the quality of products. i believe that a good quality policy by the european union can increase competitiveness and add value to the economies of european regions, as it is often the only development option for many disadvantaged rural areas with limited production alternatives. by supporting the niche farming of these disadvantaged areas, we will create an economy and jobs in these areas. furthermore, a future quality policy must also be linked to the considerable potential of a modern, dynamic, rich and diversified agriculture such as the european one, capable of offering not only high-quality food products but also services of fundamental interest to a society in constant evolution. in my report i stressed the importance of keeping the three systems of registration of geographical indications separate, as they represent the link with the regional territorial realities of europe, representing its traditions, history, taste and exclusive knowledge handed down over time. i therefore consider that, by maintaining the two separate pdo and pgi systems, account is taken of the specific differences in the form and intensity of the constraints between the product and the geographical area of production. consumers often confuse the indication of the place where the food was processed with the origin of the agricultural product and are usually unaware of the functioning of the food chain. i therefore consider that only the mandatory indication of the place of production of the primary products can give the consumer real knowledge of the quality of the product he is buying, since it is subject to a production cycle which can strongly influence its characteristics in relation to quality and food safety. let us remember that it is our duty to protect what our citizens produce and eat, who voted for us. the other two points i thought it important to include in my report are: the importance of intensive consumer education and information activities to be carried out by the european union on the various european labels and the guarantee they provide, as well as the inclusion in international registers and the international recognition of the wto system of geographical indications. the latter point is of fundamental importance if we are to protect the counterfeiting of our high-quality products. i would like to thank commissioner cioloş for his presence, and remind him of the importance of adequately protecting the quality systems that are our future, and of the fact that the economy of disadvantaged rural areas can be revived by aid to the agricultural sector, which safeguards all those niche products that are typical of these areas and which keep the population linked to this territory that would otherwise be abandoned. this would support respect for the environment and the landscape and create, where possible, a tourism and food and wine economy linked to the various regional in writing. the commission proposal provides member states with the means to combat crossborder vat fraud effectively by supplementing and amending the current regulation, creating a legal basis for targeted cooperation to combat fraud, namely eurofisc. tax fraud has serious repercussions on national budgets, undermines the principle of fiscal justice and can distort the conditions of competition. we must not forget that the public authorities are obliged to compensate for the resulting loss of revenue by increasing the tax burden on companies that comply with their tax obligations. the fight against tax fraud throughout the eu must be aided by action by the states. the aim of the proposal for a regulation is not only to enable the correct assessment of this tax but also to ensure that it is applied correctly, in particular in community transactions, and to combat vat fraud. the proposal introduces a number of improvements to the exchange of information in general, by better defining the cases in which member states may conduct an administrative enquiry, and by specifying the measures to remedy a refusal to carry out an enquiry.

the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the report which we are debating tonight and voting on tomorrow is part of the great work of implementing the 20/20/20 package, which i believe will remain one of the most far-sighted and significant achievements of the last european legislature. if i were to be told what i have to salvage from the previous five years, i would definitely put the 20/20/20 package at the top of that list. i think it is also important to say that there has been a lot of work on this report, both by the european commission - there is a communication and a recommendation on the basis of this report - and also by the itre committee and others, who have enriched the initial report with many suggestions, additions and amendments that enrich our work. i think there is only one point on which there is still some disagreement in parliament - which i hope will be overcome by tomorrow's vote - and that is the more or less binding nature we want to give to the contents of this report, and i would like to stress the work that has been done with great agreement and unanimity. information and communication technologies (ict or tics) are an important sector, even as a weight in the european economy: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full. they are also very important not only for what they represent but also for the contribution they can make and the significant and essential role they can play in trying to achieve that transition of our economy towards an economy which is still developed but which emits less and emits less carbon and therefore is less polluting for our future and for the future of the new generations, and which can, in short, constitute, not in words but in concrete deeds, the changes which can lead to the way of producing, the way of living, of moving and of consuming in our reality, to that industrial revolution which for many will characterize the very future of social and economic life, not only in our continent but in the whole world. how can icts make such a major contribution to the transformation of our economy? first, by changing the sector itself: the report wants to show how this industry can first look inward, to see how you can make communication devices, microelectronics and so on, consuming less energy, that is, being more efficient inwardly. then they can make a very important contribution in the large sectors, housing and transport, two sectors - i repeat the commission's data - where increased efficiency, according to the european directives and the target data, even from 20/20/20, can lead to a reduction, since today transport consumes 26% of energy in europe, 40% is consumed in homes for heating and cooling, depending on the season, and these emissions are also very high and can lead to very significant efficiency ratios. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. i am thinking of the entire banking sector, the public administration's reporting sector, the entire e-government and all the services, in essence, that can see, by applying these technologies, savings in carbon emissions but also savings in time, with the consequent improvement in the quality of life of citizens and the quality of social life. so a significant point: but i think that this report will be all the more significant if parliament approves it as binding tomorrow. i would like to give just two examples, mr president, if i may. the commission has already proposed a number of measures to improve the quality of the data. just yesterday, in this house, 700 mayors from europe, in the presence of our president and the european commissioner, made a new pact that wants to work on the efficiency of cities, where 70% of european citizens live, which can therefore make a great contribution to efficiency and better economic and social development.
the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, at a time when the treaty of lisbon is making europe's role in the lives of millions of citizens more significant, the challenge of transparency and legality is becoming crucial. the report we are presenting is therefore the result of a strongly united effort. the work was measured first against the scenario outlined by the court of auditors for 2008, in which the financial impact of irregularities decreases from over eur 1 billion in 2007 to eur 783 million in 2008. the decline is in all sectors except direct expenditure and preaccession funds. criticism also remains in the structural funds. but absolute amounts and values alone do not tell us where emergencies are lurking and where the situation is under control. the analysis and meetings held in recent months have led us to give priority to two needs: on the one hand, it is urgent to give member states greater responsibility for detecting fraud and irregularities, and for sharing the information needed to combat fraud, waste and distortion in spending and revenue collection. on the other hand, it is important to put forward proposals and working hypotheses to make the implementation of interventions in the member states more effective, with administrative procedures and management strategies that focus on the quality of projects and their impact on the living and working conditions of european citizens. to achieve these objectives, we propose that parliament should insist on certain priorities: first of all, we propose that olaf draw up 27 files, analysing with due care the strategies followed by each member state in combating fraud and irregularities in the use of european resources, with a precise map of the authorities responsible for controls in each country and data on the quantity and quality of the controls carried out and on their effects. secondly, to reduce irregularities and to improve regulations considerably. we are embarking on a programme of legislative and regulatory simplification: the commission has already taken a number of measures to improve the quality of the information it receives. the fight against corruption, financial crime and distortions in public procurement must also be stepped up. in this year's report we are making progress on this point, which is shared by the whole committee. the commission has also been asked to draw up a report on the implementation of the programme. from the relationship between the eu and tax havens to databases on beneficiaries of eu funds, the report makes a real contribution to increasing the transparency of spending and strengthening anti-fraud and anti-corruption strategies. finally, as regards olaf, it is essential to ensure its full operational independence, the full cooperation of the member states and an adequate human resources strategy, which it desperately needs. the debate and the debate in europe must be kept alive and open in order to give life to a single european prosecutor's office. in conclusion, i believe it is crucial that we fight together for transparency and efficient management of european resources. we must avoid any form of exploitation in this respect: the commission has also been active in the field of the environment, and has recently launched a new initiative to combat pollution. we must instead look with clarity at the problems and distortions which still persist in the various sectors of community finances and make further progress on these issues, with determination, by improving the efficiency and transparency of financial management. i believe that by making this effort the various community institutions will really take a step forward towards building a stronger, more integrated union that is better able to meet the needs of its citizens.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, violence does not solve conflicts but only increases their tragic consequences. violence, even before it is wrong, immoral, unjust, inhuman, is not appropriate: it's not convenient. it is the least effective means of finding a solution to the problems affecting an entire region, because if the element that triggers violence between the christian minority and the muslims is not only religious fundamentalism but the lack of economic development that leads to resentment and tension between different ethnic groups, what the european union, together with the african union and the entire international community, must make clear to a federal government in nigeria, which is responsible in many ways for this situation, is precisely that promoting civil and peaceful coexistence between the different ethnic groups and communities in the country is a factor of convenience for the collective, for the convenience of all the people. in addition to the establishment of an appropriate system of investigations, as many have called for, and the repression of those responsible for the immense bloodshed of the last few months - especially oil - as nigeria, would require better access to resources and a better redistribution of resources, and i believe that the agreement signed on 12 december 2009 between the federal republic of nigeria and the european commission will be able to give a great boost in this regard. security is therefore at the heart of the country's many problems today, and the main threat is not the conflict itself but the reasons that created and generated the conflict: this is where action is needed to guide nigeria towards genuine economic and democratic development.
