the rapporteur. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, representatives of the council, on 4 may last we voted unanimously in committee on the report on european aquaculture, which is essentially aimed at promoting the sustainable development of the sector. i would like to begin by thanking all those who have worked on this report over the past few months and who have given me valuable support. it is a text which has been the result of many months of work, consultation and mutual agreement, and which i hope will indeed constitute the starting point for the serious, concrete and effective promotion of an appropriate policy on aquaculture. i also think that a healthy and sustainable development, with its technological potential and its innovative component, is a very important asset for the european economy. the report also calls for the commission to take a more active role in the fight against fraud and for the commission to be able to take action to combat fraud. they have shown that they are aware of the negative consequences of the absence of a single regulation for aquaculture, the disorientation of operators, complex and excessively bureaucratic procedures, real situations of discrimination, market distortions and the lack of competitiveness of european production. the report argues that the sector needs to be given a boost by establishing a specific fund for aquaculture, either autonomous or part of the european fisheries fund, which would support research and innovation, ensure a virtuous coexistence between sustainability and competitiveness, and maintain a high level of attention to employment issues. the measures to be taken in the short term to deal with and solve all the problems currently affecting this sector are certainly not few and far between. i am referring to an integrated management plan for marine urban planning, which is essential to make freshwater, sub-coastal and offshore aquaculture compatible with tourist areas and those destined for other important economic activities, all within the framework of the rules on respect for environmental protection. i am referring to the drafting of a regulation which takes account of the specificities of the various types of aquaculture farming, to be introduced also and above all with the aim of lowering production costs and ensuring respect for the environment. in this context, i believe that the contribution of both technological innovation and scientific research is crucial. the aim is to set up facilities to reduce the dispersion of feed in water. in this connection, it will be necessary to increase the use of vegetable proteins over animal proteins without altering the nutritional value of the fish. as regards scientific research on feedingstuffs in particular, the emphasis will also have to be on discarding and processing waste to avoid the likely imbalances in the marine system resulting from a dangerous over-harvesting for fish feed. the use of the european quality mark is useful for competing with products imported from third countries and for satisfying the needs and health of consumers. i believe that it is now essential to introduce product certification and a control of the chain to identify the product, with a consequent reformulation of the labelling systems. last but not least, it is necessary to design facilities which are more respectful of the welfare of fish, of the density of farms and of the slaughter systems, all measures which should also be applied to organic products, which in fact result from a smaller production and a lower environmental impact. the employment issue should not be underestimated, as aquaculture can also be the preferred place for the employment of personnel displaced from fishing. a broad vote in this parliament will certainly be the best way for the commission, after its communication and our reasoned opinion, to propose the necessary measures, going beyond the stage of recommendation to the states, to build a community policy and to get out of the situation of being a producer of one million two hundred thousand tonnes of fish and a consumer of over five and a half million tonnes. thank you. sorry for the delay.

in writing. - thank you for the opportunity to explain the reasons why i voted in favour of the bluefin tuna catch documentation programme. i believe there is a general consensus in the european parliament on the need to safeguard species that are in danger of extinction. biodiversity is truly a 'world heritage' and states and the entire international community must do everything possible to protect it. in this sense, the management of bluefin tuna is correct. if the bluefin tuna stock is continuing to decline, finding a way to safeguard it must be a priority for us. the system of documentation of bluefin tuna catches proposed in this report, which implements the one already approved by the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas, therefore seems to me to be a good idea. i believe that this new programme can really help to solve the problem of the reduction of bluefin tuna, although it will create some obstacles for our small-scale european fishermen, who remain one of the categories most affected by the crisis and who need help in other ways.
in writing. the proposal for a european parliament and council regulation amends the existing regulation on the documentation of catches of bluefin tuna (thunnus thynnus). one of the main reasons for a proposal for amendment is the vicissitudes of iccat, the international commission for the conservation of the tunas of the adriatic, which is also responsible for the atlantic bluefin tuna catch. this commission was born as a fighting organisation which sought to fight with alternative measures against wild fishing. it was a matter of imposing trade measures on those countries whose vessels were catching endangered species in disregard of iccat rules. i mentioned that there is already a catch documentation programme for bluefin tuna, the dct, which is probably the most complex documentation programme for a single fish species. however, i very much welcome the proposal to extend and improve this programme by adding new data such as catch, exporter or retailer, transhipment, farming, harvesting and trade information. finally, i am delighted to know that such an initiative, if adopted, would be part of the european union's much-publicized commitment to abolish illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we have already fought in the past to ensure that bluefin tuna is not included in annex i to the cites convention and that fishing and marketing is not prevented. the iccat recommendations confirmed that we were on the right track and that only by managing resources more responsibly can we prevent the depletion of bluefin tuna stocks and at the same time protect our fishermen, who are already facing a difficult crisis. managing resources means fighting illegal fishing, establishing a strict system of quota control, proposing innovative measures for stock management and monitoring trade flows. that is why i voted in favour of these new rules which, by requiring the provision of complete documentation from the time of capture to the time of sale, ensure reliable traceability of every stage of the supply chain. prevention will help to protect bluefin tuna without penalising - and i repeat this - the honest fishermen who, in their own interests, are the first to want this fish species to remain.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the proposal on the rights of passengers travelling by bus is intended to improve and protect passengers, particularly disabled people and those with reduced mobility. this is the first regulation on bus passenger rights and should guarantee passengers, as is the case in the rail and air sectors. the second reading position is intended to establish a set of rights for passengers who decide to travel by bus. i agree with the rapporteur, mr cancian, who i thank for the excellent work he has done, and i think that the scope of the regulation should be changed, excluding regional services when they are integrated with urban and suburban services. it would be right and proper to guarantee the rights of passengers in the event of accidents, cancellations or delays in departure, as parliament had already decided at first reading. equally important is the issue of passenger rights information: it would be useful to provide passengers with information on coincidences with other modes of transport, and this would also ensure dialogue between passenger transport services by bus and those by rail. as regards the disabled and persons with reduced mobility, maximum protection must be guaranteed, and i would propose a 24-hour time limit instead of 48 hours for requesting assistance and greater guarantees for compensation and replacement of the tools which guarantee the mobility of persons with reduced mobility in the event of loss or damage. in addition, taking into account the needs of passengers with reduced mobility, any architectural barriers should be removed and existing infrastructure should be improved to make it accessible. the aim of this regulation is to improve the competitiveness of the bus sector, to promote intermodality and, above all, to improve the travel conditions of passengers.

the next item is the report by dirk sterckx, on behalf of the committee on transport and tourism, on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on reporting formalities for ships arriving in and/or departing from ports of the member states of the community and repealing directive 2002/6/ec (com(2009)0011 – c6-0030/2009 – 2009/0005(cod)) (a7-0064/2010).
i would like to thank the rapporteur, mr sterckx, for his excellent work on this report on extending freedom of movement in the maritime sector for shipping within the european union. i agree with the rapporteur on the purpose of this directive, which is to exempt all maritime transport of goods within the european union from unnecessary administrative formalities. in order to have a european maritime area without frontiers, it is not only important that the various competent authorities cooperate satisfactorily, but also that the various simplification systems be applied at the same time. this is necessary to ensure the smooth functioning of the entire european maritime area without frontiers, to make the transport of goods by sea more attractive and to make optimal use of it. the harmonization of administrative procedures between member states will allow for more fluid shipping between the various ports of the european union and will revive the sea freight traffic, which currently represents less than 10% of the total. to this day, navigation is still hampered by the administrative formalities that are imposed on it. the electronic systems should therefore be put into operation as soon as possible, as they would allow for a faster system of data exchange. interoperability is also important for real administrative simplification, since the initiation of information by e-mail is not entirely efficient and is useless if the information systems are not technically interoperable. as regards language, i believe that the use of a common language would certainly benefit european shipping. this would make the communication quicker, causing less confusion and administrative delays.
vice-president of the commission. − mr president, thank you all very much for your remarks and your unanimous support for this proposal. i am very happy about this proposal. it is an important step forward, but we will have a much bigger step ahead of us in this task of establishing a single maritime area for european shipping, namely customs barriers. there we will see a lot more difficulties. now we are talking about formalities, and this is very important, more important than just an administrative question, but i also ask your support when we come to do the same with customs formalities, which are much more complicated and controversial.

in writing. the function of the paris convention on international exhibitions is to regulate the frequency and quality of the exhibitions themselves. the convention applies to all international exhibitions lasting from three weeks to three months which are not essentially commercial in nature. as the convention covers matters falling within the scope of the customs legislation of the european union, a member state wishing to accede to it must first seek authorisation from the union. the european union cannot accede to the convention as only sovereign states can be parties to it; i do, however, share the aim of the council decision, which is to enable the member states concerned which have not yet acceded to the convention to do so, while respecting the exclusive competences of the european union.

in writing. the proposal for a council decision aims at the signing and conclusion of an agreement between the european community, on the one hand, and the swiss confederation and the principality of liechtenstein, on the other, laying down the arrangements for the participation of these states in the frontex agency. the agency is conceived as a key instrument in the common strategy against illegal immigration. the agency also assists member states in training their national border guard corps and provides them with technical assistance and support in organising joint return operations or border surveillance. the agreement between the european community and switzerland and liechtenstein also defines certain matters such as the limited voting rights of their representatives on the agency's management board, their financial contribution to the agency's budget and the confidentiality of data. i can only welcome the conclusion of this convention, which allows the two countries to help ensure greater coordination between the competent services of the administrations of the participating states in the field of external border control and surveillance. i therefore hope that the member states will endeavour to complete as soon as possible the ratification procedures necessary to associate switzerland and liechtenstein with frontex.

in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of the report on promoting access for young people to the labour market and strengthening the status of trainees and apprentices, because i believe it is essential to promote and support youth employment. unfortunately, we are now in a period of severe financial crisis, which has caused a considerable increase in unemployment, especially among young people. recent statistics show that there are over 5.5 million young people under 25 without a job, or 21.4% of the european youth population, a figure which is twice the rate of unemployment as a whole. in view of this situation, it has become necessary to ask the council and the commission to draw up an employment strategy focusing on the development of policies that can guarantee young europeans targeted access to the world of work, in order to avoid the social and economic costs that youth unemployment entails for our society. the adoption of packages of measures providing a strong incentive for investment in education, research and mobility and facilitating access to financial instruments for young people wishing to pursue entrepreneurial activities is also a priority.

in writing. biodegradable organic waste biodegradable garden, kitchen and food waste represents about one third of urban waste and has a potentially significant impact on the environment. when they are landfilled, they emit methane, a greenhouse gas 23 times more potent than carbon dioxide and one of the main drivers of climate change. while waste management in the european union is governed by a wide body of legislation, there is scope for further improvements in the area of biodegradable organic waste, especially as this waste offers the possibility of being recycled and used as a source of renewable energy. in this sense, a specific directive on the management of organic waste would be a crucial point for the implementation of the principles deriving from the framework directive on waste and from other directives on waste management in general. the only reservation i have is that the directive must be flexible enough to be applied locally, so that the best solution can be chosen from an environmental and economic point of view.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i am in favour of the establishment of the european banking authority because this instrument should be able to fill the regulatory gaps that were revealed during the last financial and economic crisis, a gap which parliament had unfortunately identified long ago. as has been shown in some reports on this subject, coordination between national supervisory authorities, whose jurisdiction is bound up with the borders of their respective states, is not sufficient for the control of those financial institutions which, on the other hand, conceive of the internal market as a genuine area without frontiers. the establishment of this authority could therefore be a significant first step in addressing this type of problem.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the recent financial crisis has given rise to a great deal of debate on the urgent need for action to ensure the sustainability and stability of the financial system. the measures taken so far will entail costs of unprecedented proportions, with negative side effects such as freezing of financial markets, contraction of credit markets, paralysis of enterprises, a surge in the unemployment rate and a decrease in tax revenues. whatever their final cost, it is clear that it will be too much for the taxpayers, growth and employment in europe. the different strategies, methods and instruments used in europe and the us have raised serious concerns about the effectiveness of the overall process, legal uncertainty and distortion of competition. the need for global, coherent solutions through international alignment of regulations and procedures is more urgent than ever, and it is at this moment that the european union is called upon to show its leadership and to play an active part in planning the new financial system, a sound and healthy european single market among 27 members.

in writing. − the objective of the 1996 directive on the integrated prevention and control of pollution (ippc) is to prevent and control emissions to air and soil from european industrial installations. the ippc aims to promote the implementation of best available techniques (bat), i.e. those that are economically and technically sound and that ensure maximum efficiency in achieving a high level of environmental protection: they are defined in the bat reference documents (brefs) developed following an exchange of information between the commission, member state authorities and stakeholders (the 'seville process'). at its plenary session on 10 march 2009, parliament discussed at first reading the commission's proposal to establish the emission limit value directly on the basis of brefs: the commission has also proposed a number of amendments to the directive, including a proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos. i support the proposal to establish union-wide minimum requirements for emission limit values only for activities requiring eu intervention, according to the criteria of environmental impact and state of implementation of bat in the sector concerned.

situation of the country continues to be very fragile and violence could resume. i am pleased that the european union has been active throughout this crisis. we have followed the events closely from strengthening key institutions and supporting inter-ethnic reconciliation and civil society initiatives, as well as social stabilisation. the emergence of a stable and democratic kyrgyzstan in a hitherto authoritarian and unstable part of the world is a goal we are ready to support. as regards the security aspects and possible eu engagement, we are liaising actively with the un and osce together with others. we are looking carefully into initiatives currently on the table, including the osce proposal for a police task force. with respect to security, as for all other areas for eu now, the need for such a policy in the future and the need for a change in this policy. i also note your call for a re-design of the common agricultural policy in line not only with the lisbon treaty which sets clear objectives for the cap, but also with the europe 2020 strategy. i think that this is precisely the opportunity to adapt our common agricultural policy more closely to the current expectations of the citizens, beyond its traditional objectives of ensuring security of supply to the markets. you also advocate measures that help to improve the functioning of the food chain and the balance between the various actors in the chain, as well as the transparency of positions and the bargaining power of agricultural producers. these are elements which will be reflected not only in the reform of the cap but also in other initiatives which the commission will propose. i have also read with great interest your proposals on the future of direct payments as an instrument not only to ensure the stability of farmers' incomes but also to ensure a minimum level of supply of public goods. i think that this is a new approach to direct payments and a new justification for them, linked to the guarantee of a minimum basic income for farmers, but also to the incentive to produce public goods. i also noted the suggestion to review the criteria for the distribution of these direct payments, both on the basis of this new criterion and to ensure a more equitable distribution between the different member states, regions and categories of farmers, also taking into account the specific nature of agriculture in less-favoured regions, in difficult areas. i also note, as george lyon has said, the need to continue the market orientation of the cap, an orientation which must be made in a reasoned way in order to avoid farmers being faced with very chaotic markets. from this point of view, i think that the market orientation is entirely compatible with the improvement of the mechanisms for managing the markets, precisely to ensure that these markets can function properly without affecting, as i said, the achievement of the objectives of maintaining agriculture throughout the european territory and preserving the diversity of our farms. i have a few comments on the amendments which have been proposed and which will be discussed. i think food production is an important objective of the cap. this production is paid for directly by the markets, but public goods, which are not paid for by the markets and must be covered by a public financial contribution, must also be taken into account. in agricultural production, these two aspects can be taken into account: food production and the production of public goods, with aspects that are paid for by the markets, others that are not and that must be supported by the public budget. as regards the structure of the common agricultural policy, i have said on several occasions that in my view the common agricultural policy must have two pillars in order to obtain more clarity as to the achievement of the objectives of the cap, but also to ensure a more efficient management of the instruments at our disposal. there are instruments which have to be applied annually, and the results of which can be measured every year, but there are also certain measures which have to be applied on a multiannual basis, as part of a programming, in which case several years are needed to achieve results. in order to ensure better management of the resources and means at our disposal within the framework of the common agricultural policy, i think we need these two pillars, which must of course be complementary and whose objectives must be better defined. secondly, and most importantly, it is necessary to clarify how the measures covered by them are to be implemented. as regards conditionality, i think it has had a positive effect on direct payments. it also clearly defined the starting point for public goods paid for by public funds. of course, we can simplify the conditionality measures. the content of the directives can be made clearer not only to farmers but also to the national or regional administrations which apply and control them. that said, i think that the ecological conditionality linked to basic direct payments is also a good starting point for defining clearly the other measures that stimulate the production of public goods. as regards market measures, as i said, i think that a market orientation is necessary, but we also need to maintain safety nets and also to study new measures which can enable us to achieve the objectives of a certain price and income stability in the market. as regards the structures of small, medium and large farms, i agree, including small farms, that they must become more efficient, but we must be able to ensure that this change takes place in their specific environment, by making more use of a specific potential. so we can have a restructuring of these farms, which goes hand in hand with a shift towards markets, without going towards a single model of agriculture, so that we can maintain diversity in agriculture. i will listen carefully to your comments and observations and i can assure you, mr lyon, that i will examine very carefully the content of the report voted by parliament and will certainly refer to it in the preparation of the commission's legislative initiatives in the coming months.

in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the cap is one of the most important policies of the european union, and agricultural expenditure accounts for some 43% of the community budget. under article 33 of the treaty establishing the community, the community is to ensure that european consumers receive reasonable prices and farmers are paid fairly. the recent economic and financial crisis has led to a reduction in farmers' income of 12,2% on average between 2008 and 2009, a tightening of credit access conditions and an increase in the unemployment rate in rural areas. the volatility of commodity prices on agricultural markets has increased considerably and is expected to continue to increase. i therefore believe that in the future cap a minimum safety net must be provided to manage market price uncertainty and to provide rapid and effective responses to economic crises in the sector. according to fao estimates, by 2050 the world population is expected to increase from the current 6 to 9 billion and that, by doubling the demand for food, global food production will have to increase accordingly. food security will therefore be the central challenge of the agriculture of the future and the union will have the burden of continuing to guarantee it to the european citizens.

in writing. - it is a certainty that after 11 september 2001 no human being perceives his own safety and physical safety as a trivial fact. the crux of any action to restore public confidence is therefore the protection of personal information, which must not only be guaranteed in terms of privacy but whose processing, especially in financial matters, is a significant tool in the fight against international terrorism. i therefore voted in favour of mr alvaro's report on the agreement which sets out the conditions under which, as from 1 august, the us treasury will be able to access financial data from some 8 000 institutions and banks in 200 countries, managed by the company swift. considering the due protections such as the possibility for a european citizen to make an administrative appeal enjoying reciprocal treatment with the us citizen and the tightening of the information retention times, europe-us cooperation in this case represents the just tribute of globalisation to its perverse effects.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of the agreement negotiated between the european commission and the united states because i consider it a duty and a sign of great responsibility to support it. the transfer of personal data is a highly sensitive issue in europe, where there have been painful experiences of totalitarian regimes making abundant and distorted use of it. the new agreement will allow the transfer of certain banking information to the american authorities, provided that this is done in compliance with the strict rules on the protection of personal data, which we in the european parliament are committed to ensuring. such information may be consulted only if it is considered to be relevant for the purposes of counter-terrorism investigations: such access shall be conditional upon the presentation of appropriate evidence by the united states authorities. the new agreement is a victory for all the european institutions, and for our european parliament in particular: the commission is in fact responding to our calls for greater protection of the privacy of european citizens by offering them a double guarantee: full transparency for data access and use by one party and adequate redress procedures to ensure privacy protection by the other. adequate safeguards so that these two interests, security and protection of privacy, can both be met and protected.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of the alvaro report because i believe that it is important to act against terrorism. terrorism is a threat and must be fought as such. the united states is a key partner in the fight against terrorism, with which we must work together to identify and cut off any funding that is the real fuel of terrorism.
in writing. the final version of the agreement meets most of parliament's requests, protecting both the security and privacy of eu citizens and providing legally binding solutions to the problems under consideration. the agreement also marks a new stage in the evolution of parliament's powers, ensuring european democratic oversight of international agreements. in addition to the improvements contained in the agreement, the council and the commission have made a legally binding commitment to establish the legal and technical framework that will allow data to be extracted from the eu territory. this commitment will ensure that the bulk data transfers to the us authorities will cease in the medium term. the establishment of a european extraction system is a major improvement, as the prolonged transfer of data in bulk is a departure from the principles on which eu legislation and practice are based.
in writing. − the creation of the external action service was unclear and controversial from the outset. we should be concerned about the possible contradictions that could arise between the activities of the future community diplomacy and those traditionally carried out by the member states. will the states lose the freedom to determine their own foreign policy? while this is not a concern for an imminent scenario, it is worth asking what the effects of establishing such a service at european level will be in the medium to long term. let me be clear: if the basic idea is to emulate the american model, where foreign policy is handled directly and exclusively by the federal government over the 50 states, then it would be better to remember that the government in washington is elected by the citizens, and its foreign policy receives every four years a democratic legitimacy that the commission and the council of the eu - and even the future foreign service - do not have. by voting against mr brok's report, i therefore express my preference for an intergovernmental european foreign policy, since, in any case, entrusting the cfsp to the community level would not guarantee the supranational nature of the choices made in such a delicate area.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the common foreign and economic policy is the necessary objective of the process of european integration. it should be remembered that the single currency was also chosen because it was thought to accelerate the process of integration that had been hampered in nice. the way in which the european external action service is organised is likely to be more a paralysing inertia than a virtuous unifying process.
in writing. - the importance of timely coordination of the different areas of the european union's foreign policy by the commission is clear. in this regard, the establishment of the european external action service (eeas) under the high representative for foreign affairs and security policy and vice-president of the commission (hr/vp) can make the european union's external action more effective on the world stage, in particular in order to avoid inconsistencies and duplication of efforts and to ensure long-term coherence in promoting the european union's core values and strategic interests abroad.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, mr lunacek's report highlights the limited progress made by the country and i believe that the problems highlighted make its accession to the eu even less plausible, which would thus accentuate the heterogeneous character that the latest accessions are helping to shape. as i have said on the question of albania's integration into the eu, i believe that we are at a crossroads: europe must choose whether it will be limited to becoming an entity based on mere geographical criteria or whether it will aspire to become more organic, coherent and composed of states which, in their diversity, can nevertheless display common characteristics and are consistent with the european ideal. the fact that five member states do not recognise kosovo's sovereignty remains an obstacle which makes kosovo's accession to europe a paradox at the moment. for these reasons, i do not support mr lunacek's report.
in writing. - this report is a demonstration of what european propaganda can do when it ignores the mistakes of the past; the work of mr chountis does indeed highlight the internal problems of albania, but at the same time it almost seems to tell us that we are obliged to welcome the balkan states into the union, as if this were written in the book of destiny and no one could oppose its unfolding. i don't agree with that at all. albania today has very obvious problems of internal political stability, and a very high level of corruption. its entry would pose additional problems to those which the union itself has had to face and still has to face today following a major enlargement which has almost doubled the number of member states. there is no reason, except the power-hungry and centralistic eu bureaucracies, to continue on the path towards albania's eu membership; the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, once again we are faced with the unfortunate situation where, in discussing a real and serious problem (in this case the fight against hiv), arguments are introduced which, by proposing unfair solutions to the right to life, prevent a vote in favour. the use of the language "sexual and reproductive health" has now become the way to persuade parliaments to promote abortion. we can't let them fool us. everyone, myself first, must promote sexual and reproductive health, but when the words indicate a different and even opposite reality (the killing of a human being understood as a woman's right to freedom) it becomes necessary to unmask the deception. abortion is a real tragedy in the world and in our europe too! my vote against the resolution is not to oppose the all-out effort to combat aids, but to oppose the method and content i have indicated.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the common agricultural policy (cap) is one of the most important policies of the european union and, following the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, the reform of the cap, like any new agricultural legislation, cannot be adopted without parliament's agreement. farmers produce goods for the benefit of society as a whole, but the common agricultural policy is not just about farmers, because there is a link between agriculture, the environment, biodiversity, climate change and the sustainable management of natural resources such as water and land. there is also a clear link between agriculture and the proper economic and social development of the eu's vast rural areas; it also provides the food we need to live. this first resolution on the future of the cap is the contribution of us meps to the debate on how to reform the cap in conjunction with the new multiannual budget starting in 2013 and on how to establish the fundamental principles that should guide the process of building a new common agricultural policy. with this vote, parliament put the spotlight on how to tackle new challenges such as the fight against climate change, food security, food quality, the competitiveness of businesses and farmers' incomes.
in writing. − after the 2007-2013 programming period, the new common agricultural policy will have to face a very important challenge for our farmers: the commission has also proposed that the member states should be able to use the same financial resources as in the past, by distributing them equally between the old and new member states on the basis not only of the number of hectares but also of other objective evaluation criteria. i voted in favour of mr lyon's report because i fully support his intention to regionalise and maintain coupled aid for vulnerable agricultural areas and sectors. i also believe in the importance of the policy of promoting geographical indications, simplification, compliance with community standards by imports from third countries and strengthening the position of the various actors in the food chain.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i believe that european agriculture needs a common policy that continues to be such in order to avoid the inevitable disparities between the member states and to ensure that the cap is fairly financed entirely from the european budget. i therefore voted against the renationalisation of the cap, as the new common agricultural policy will need adequate funding in order to be able to better support this policy in line with the main challenges that this sector, which is crucial for the eu's food security, will have to face in the coming years. food safety is a consumer right which must be protected alongside the protection of 'second generation' public goods such as the environment, land use planning and animal welfare.
in writing. − the 2009 crisis showed the weakness of the system of measures to support the agricultural sector. the effects were felt on farmers' incomes, which were reduced by 12% on revenues that normally already amount to around 50% of the average revenues of the european union. the importance of the sector, which employs some 30 million people, must be matched by strategic action for the period after 2013, starting with the strengthening of the common policy, an appropriate budgetary policy and maintaining the budget, taking into account the many beneficial effects of agriculture on the environment, health and climate change. it is important to ensure that consumers receive fair prices and that farmers receive a fair income through targeted aid. agriculture must play a greater role in the 2020 strategy and define actions for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. market instability increases with the increase in product safety and sustainability assurance because this puts eu producers at a competitive disadvantage compared to imports. it is becoming difficult to ensure reasonable prices for consumers and fair remuneration if stricter rules are not introduced to ensure that the principle of community preference is respected.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i agree with the approach and the structure of mr lyon's report. this own-initiative report is an important basis for the guidelines which the european parliament intends to follow for future agriculture, pending the commission's communication which is due at the end of the year. for the first time, parliament has therefore agreed on a way forward for a constructive dialogue on the content and priorities of the competitiveness of agri-food production and the sustainable development of rural areas. the challenges facing european agriculture are numerous and have a significant impact on the economies of many member states, but they are also the subject of debate, in terms of the budget to be allocated to the european union, in order to make these very challenges an opportunity for growth in the agricultural sector and development for many european agricultural entrepreneurs.
in writing. - mr president, the fisheries sector is a strategic resource within the eu for supplying the population and is also a major contributor to local development, employment and the preservation of the cultural traditions of coastal communities. unfortunately, we have seen a gradual decline in production in recent years, partly as a result of certain community measures to protect the marine ecosystem, such as the mediterranean regulation which aims to make fishing more sustainable, but which has actually brought the whole sector to its knees. our fishermen are obliged to fish less, but demand is increasing and so are imports from third countries. to avoid unfair competition and to protect consumers, imported products must comply with the same rules as community products. imports often offer products at lower prices, but also of lower quality and with elements of uncertainty in terms of safety. it is therefore important to strengthen fair, transparent and sustainable trade in the sector, including the need to introduce strict certification and labelling criteria in relation to the quality and traceability of fishery and aquaculture products.
in writing. - i shall be voting in favour of the report by mr codec. at a historical moment such as the quota period, i consider the question of the import regime for fishery and aquaculture products to be crucial, that is, the problem of defining the conditions under which products from outside the eu are allowed into the single market. given that 60% of domestic demand is now met by exports and that this is expected to increase sharply by 2030, europe needs to provide answers to the questions and legitimate concerns of industry. i therefore agree with the view of mr cadec: it is necessary to investigate and monitor the evolution of community policy in this field so that it does not lead to disparities in treatment between producers in the member states and those in third countries.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, time to make up for past undervaluations and delays. fisheries are a key sector of our economic and social system and must be treated as such. in view of the reform of the common fisheries policy, we have a duty to make firm decisions to guarantee incomes, stability of the markets and better marketing of products, including aquaculture. and to protect consumers by paying greater attention to food safety aspects. that is why i voted for this resolution which, in view of the negative impact of market liberalisation on local economies, stresses the strategic importance of reasonable customs protection. we must put a stop to competition from low-cost imports from outside the eu, which often do not meet environmental, social, health and quality standards. we also need to introduce strict certification and labelling criteria in relation to the traceability of products, in order to inform consumers about the geographical origin, the production conditions, the catch and, above all, the quality of the products on sale. finally, i would like to stress that in a market which is largely dependent on imports, withdrawals from the market aimed at destroying the product are no longer justifiable. the resulting savings could be made available to the programmes of producer organisations.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i supported the resolution on the import regime for fishery and aquaculture products into the eu with a view to reforming the cfp, as i believe that it is essential to have a framework adapted to the needs of the sector. the european union is the world's largest market for fishery products and it is well known that production is not sufficient to meet domestic demand on its own. it is therefore a priority to ensure that imports from third countries meet the environmental, health, social and quality standards imposed by the eu, in order to avoid unfair competition from importing countries through lower-priced and lower-quality products. the report approved by this house today also calls for stricter and more transparent criteria to be applied to the quality, traceability and labelling of fishery products.
in writing. − the issue of the import regime for fishery and aquaculture products (fap), and in particular the conditions under which products from outside the eu are allowed to enter the union as a complement to, or in competition with, products from european fisheries and aquaculture, is undoubtedly a priority issue, essential in any analysis of these specific sectors of the european economy. the regulation of this matter is essential in a context where the rate of consumption coverage through community production is today very low, with a rate of dependence on imports of over 60%.

mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the report on fair incomes for farmers, adopted by the committee on agriculture and rural development on 28 june, is an important step towards promoting a better functioning of the agri-food chain in europe. this report is therefore an important step forward in view of the serious crisis which has affected various sectors of the agricultural sector for some time and which is now putting thousands of businesses at risk. the report also points to the need for rapid action to ensure price transparency, fair competition on the markets, and strong action to eliminate abuses of power in the purchasing and bargaining phases and global speculation in raw materials. i believe that not only is it necessary to reorganise the supply chain, with the agricultural producer at its centre, to whom a proper role must be given in connection with the innovation of new forms of agricultural product markets, but also to rationalise the food chain in order to reduce the environmental impact of food transport and to promote the knowledge and marketing of products with high territorial value. i personally fully agree with what the committee on agriculture and rural development of the european parliament has approved and i will also vote in accordance with what the committee has voted, as some of my colleagues have already announced. i would like to stress two points which the report highlights. the first concerns the revision of the competition rules for the benefit of producers of products with a high territorial value. the second is an invitation to the commission to propose instruments to support and promote food chains run by farmers, in order to reduce intermediaries and to give producers an advantage in marketing their products.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we support this report because it contains proposals already put forward by the lega nord, in particular on price transparency linked to the recognition of fair payment of products to farmers, the creation of zero-kilometre food chains, promoting the maintenance of the diversity of territorial products and the quality of products, and increasing the development of the local economy. the indication of the cost of the product at the origin would make the consumer aware of the impact of the change of hands on the final price and would encourage him to choose the short chain, thus favouring local producers. to combat the volatility of the agricultural market, it is essential to prohibit the sale of agricultural products below the purchase price and to increase controls on products entering the european market, as it is often - unfortunately - that european farmers comply with community rules and non-european farmers do not follow them at all. the cost of this is always borne by our farmers.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the first objective of the cap has always been to guarantee fair incomes for farmers and i believe that we must continue along this path. the commission's examination has revealed discrepancies with the initial principle which we cannot ignore. our farmers are convinced that their work is economically undervalued. the transition from the first to the second stage of the supply chain in which they are now active is no longer considered to be a determining factor in determining the final price. it is necessary to control fluctuations in the prices of primary goods which would only and exclusively harm the consumer. i think it is useful to provide for a review of the way the chain is passed through in order to avoid an increase in the price of the good, which is not consistent with a correct distribution of the cost of the work done. we must ensure that the asymmetrical level between the cost of the product in the first and the last stage is rising, thus creating a detriment for the consumer. the market would be at risk of selling more expensive products which would not reflect an increase in quality.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, in recent days many representatives of civil society, political leaders, intellectuals, ngos and the catholic church have been mobilizing for the release of sakineh, a 42-year-old iranian mother sentenced to death by stoning for adultery. this conviction was based on a confession extracted after a punishment of 99 lashes. the death penalty of stoning can be considered a form of torture in that the victim must be buried so that only the head is raised from the ground. the stones that can be thrown at her must be sharp and cutting, but not such as to be capable of instantaneous death, and the torture in the pre-agonized, conscious state must not be less than 20 minutes. in recent years hundreds of women of all ages have been stoned to death in iran for the crime of adultery, and at least 40 more women are currently imprisoned awaiting the same fate. i think it is essential that the european parliament should make its voice heard against this barbarism.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, defending sakineh means defending life, the right to life, and therefore to live. the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, and indeed all the constitutional charters of our countries, include among their principles the inviolable rights of the individual, first and foremost the right to dignity and life. our fight must not be for one individual, but for all human beings who are deprived of their lives in every part of the world for whatever reason. no reason, tradition, religion, law or authority can dispose and i say dispose of an individual's life. we need to take strong, but also decisive action against countries which authorise and apply the death penalty, as well as all serious violations of human rights. europe must be decisive in this, it must take a firm stand, it must insist that these rights be respected in its diplomatic and commercial relations. sakineh wouldn't be the first victim. that's enough, that's enough.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, this debate is necessary today so that our assembly can join the great international mobilization under way to stop the executions in iran, in particular the stoning of the young sakineh. as is often the case, however, debates of this kind always come to a head, just in time to avoid executions or other cases of serious human rights violations. instead, we should think about what kind of actions we can take to eliminate the root causes of human rights violations in the world, causes that are called dictatorships, theocracies, islamic radicalism, totalitarianisms. as regards the case of iran in particular, i hope that none of us will be under the illusion that our action, the action of the european parliament in the field of relations with iran, can be limited to the resolutions we vote for, however just and acceptable they may be. we cannot tolerate theocrats in tehran and the fanatics who rule that country coming to this parliament, as happened a couple of months ago, to give us lessons in democracy. our action must be an incentive for the eu to deal with the issue of relations with tehran with firmness, without ambiguity and indecision.
member of the commission. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, first of all i would like to congratulate the rapporteur, mr portas, on behalf of the commission, for the excellent work he has done in drawing up this very comprehensive report and for his collaboration with the rapporteurs of the other committees responsible for delivering opinions. this report is timely because it can be easily integrated into the work the commission is now undertaking to meet two deadlines. first, the so-called crisis derogation allowing the globalisation adjustment fund to provide support to workers made redundant as a result of the global financial and economic crisis and to provide 65% co-financing expires at the end of 2011. we must consider whether it is necessary to extend this derogation or to return to a 50% co-financing rate for trade-related redundancies. the second deadline is the end of 2013, when the egf regulation will have to be revised. in this respect, one of the key issues will be whether or not this fund should be integrated into the next multiannual financial framework. we are pleased to note that mr portas' report supports the reasons for the creation of this fund and stresses the need to maintain this instrument. the report actually proposes that a permanent instrument be one of the options envisaged for the future and asks the commission to submit a proposal to that effect. mr portas proposes that the mid-term review planned for 2011 be brought forward and completed by 30 june 2011. this is a problem in the light of the amended egf regulation, as reports on the first cases approved after the adoption of the amended regulation will only be available at the beginning of november 2011. we have, of course, an earlier final report which we can use to review the unchanged criteria of the regulation, such as the success rate of the actions under the fund, a comparative analysis of these measures, the procedures for consulting the social partners and the analysis of the impact of the fund on the beneficiaries. the report notes that implementation has been rather modest to date. financial contribution was approved for only 27 cases and very few sectors are represented. nine member states did not submit any applications. only 80 million euros have been used out of the 1.5 billion that could be mobilised. the commission requested reimbursement of almost 40% of the amounts in respect of the first eleven applications. i would like to stress, as the report does, that these figures relate only to applications approved under the original regulation and that, as the report rightly points out, the amendment of the regulation has led to a considerable increase in the number of applications for assistance to this fund, both in terms of targeted workers and budget. the report rightly calls for improvements, in particular reducing the time between redundancies and the date of payment of the contribution to the fund. the commission is committed to speeding up and simplifying these procedures, but some of these improvements will require better organisation by all the actors involved: the commission, the member states and the budgetary authority. close coordination between the commission and the european parliament, particularly on timetable matters, should help to reduce some of these delays. member states should be encouraged to submit applications as soon as redundancies are announced. the commission, for its part, should provide more information and advice to the member states and set itself a deadline of three to four months for its own evaluation. we take note of the request to draw up a proposal to extend the crisis derogation until the end of the multiannual financial framework. i agree that, for the period after 2013, the issue of the european globalisation adjustment fund should be considered in the general context of the negotiations on the next financial and multiannual framework and that the establishment of a permanent fund should be one of the options to be considered. the report is rich in ideas and suggestions and will make a useful contribution to the preparation of the new regulation. the commission has also planned a series of consultation meetings with member states and other stakeholders. i am sure that the rapporteur, as well as the other members of the european parliament, will contribute to these consultations, the aim being that the fund may be improved and made even more effective in the future as an instrument which shows european solidarity towards workers who are made redundant.
in writing. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, globalisation is an important opportunity for us and our children, but it is also a scary one, creating distributions of wealth that are harder to control and manage fairly. moving beyond our borders and putting our identities at stake requires the building of stronger cultures within which to continue to foster mutual respect and genuine understanding. the first objects of our understanding must include the interests of those families who have suddenly found themselves without an income because of increasingly difficult economic conditions. the european globalisation adjustment fund must be a response to these households and an effective instrument for the future economic development of the union. in the midst of the economic crisis we cannot afford to be too rigid in the instruments of implementation, which our citizens, even before our policies, would inevitably suffer. the very fact that we still have a large stock of projects submitted and never implemented should make us reflect on the extent to which our programmes and our permanent funds can be self-sufficient and therefore seriously consider whether the european globalisation adjustment fund should be added to the european social fund as a permanent instrument for european intervention in the field of employment.
member of the commission. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the interconnection of trade registers is a useful project to increase the transparency of economic actors, restore confidence and promote access for smes to the single market. i congratulate mr lechner and the committee on legal affairs on this report. our views are broadly in agreement. the commission will present legislative proposals no later than early 2001 which will no doubt take account of your conclusions. the financial and economic crisis has highlighted the importance of transparency in financial markets and beyond. for citizens to have confidence, they need access to reliable and up-to-date official information on companies. trade registers play a key role in this respect by recording information on companies and making it available to the public. however, while it is easy to access this information in the member states where a company is registered, it is often very difficult, for technical or linguistic reasons, to access the same information from another member state. the interconnection of trade registers will therefore provide small and medium-sized enterprises, consumers and employees with a supplementary and necessary information tool. the following are some thoughts on some aspects of mr lechner's report. i note your concern about the additional administrative burden that might result from the interconnection of these registers. i can assure you that we are not planning to impose any new costs, direct or indirect, on businesses. i also share your wish that the participation of all member states in the cooperation mechanism should be made compulsory. such a mechanism will only make sense if it is supported by all the member states. as regards cooperation in the context of regular updating of information on foreign subsidiaries, the commission intends to propose such a mechanism in the form of legislation, in which the member states would be obliged to participate. this is probably a missing link in the internal market. you also recommend that a single point of access to information be set up. we share the objective of accessibility to data provided by the national registers. consumers, workers, small and mediumsized enterprises and national administrations in other member states must be able to access these services without any obstacles. in the same spirit of accessibility, we want to offer information in all the official languages of the union. this is a prerequisite for achieving our objective of bringing the internal market closer to the citizens. in addition, users of registers should be clearly informed of the scope and the different consequences of the national information contained in the register, which may vary considerably from one country to another. as regards data quality, it is clear that the information provided in the context of interconnection must be reliable, up-to-date and accessible. that is a strong message from you and one which is welcomed by the commission. i can assure you that any initiative by the commission will respect the protection of personal and commercial data. ladies and gentlemen, the lechner report demonstrates the level of commitment of parliament to help implement better interconnection of business registers for the benefit of consumers, businesses and their workers. this project will strengthen the internal market. the commission welcomes this and looks forward to the adoption of the report in plenary.
in writing. the interconnection of business registers is an essential prerequisite for promoting the integration of the economic area within the eu and for strengthening legal certainty for businesses and consumers. the report by mr lechner makes a full statement on the priority actions which are essential to increase legal certainty and transparency in crossborder economic activities. first, it is essential that the interconnection of registers and access to data take place in a single context. to this end, it will be necessary to strengthen and develop the potential offered by the brite interconnection project, so as to allow the establishment of a single portal, which will allow all citizens to access information from european companies. secondly, it will be essential to ensure that all member states participate as soon as possible, taking into account the integration of business registers which will be compulsory for all member states. this is because the success of any project aimed at the harmonious development of the internal market requires the participation of all the parties concerned, so that it can be made binding as soon as the technical criteria have been refined.

in writing. - mr president, i voted in favour of mr portas' report on the interconnection of business registers because, in order to remove the existing obstacles to business mobility in the eu, it is appropriate to consider the mandatory integration of european business registers for all member states. the introduction of a single european portal for access to business registers, a valid and accessible portal in the 27 member states that allows all citizens to access information on european companies, is certainly a tool to make it easier and more convenient for businesses to develop within the union.

in writing. - mr president, on 23 april 2007 the council authorised the commission to open negotiations with the republic of korea with a view to concluding an eu-korea free trade agreement. the agreement was signed on 15 october 2009. the agreement contains a bilateral safeguard clause providing for the possibility of re-application of the gnp rate if, as a result of the liberalisation of trade, imports are made in such increased quantities, in absolute terms or relative to domestic production, and are made under conditions such as to cause or threaten to cause serious injury to the union industry producing like or directly competing products. in order for the measures to be effective, this safeguard clause needs to be incorporated into eu law, not only for the procedural aspects of its application, but also because the rights of the parties concerned need to be specified. this proposal for a european parliament and council regulation is the legal instrument for implementing the safeguard clause of the eu-south korea free trade agreement.

in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the first objective of the cap has always been to guarantee fair incomes for farmers. the commission's examination has revealed discrepancies with the initial principle which we cannot ignore. our farmers are convinced that their work is economically undervalued. the transition from the first to the second stage of the supply chain, in which they are the main players, is no longer considered a determining factor in determining the final price, which then falls on the consumer. it is necessary to control fluctuations in the prices of primary goods which would only and exclusively harm the consumer. i think it is useful to provide for a review of the way the chain is passed through in order to avoid an increase in the price of the good which is not consistent with the correct distribution of the cost of the work done. it is necessary to check that the asymmetrical level between the cost of the product in the first and the last stage is rising, thus creating a detriment for the consumer. the market would be at risk of selling more expensive products which would not reflect an increase in quality. consumers must be the protagonists in order to guarantee a fair return for all operators in the production chain.

vice-president of the commission. − madam president, it is clear that the right to free movement and residence of eu citizens and their family members is one of the cornerstones of the eu. it is not only a fundamental right but also a personal right. article 21 of the treaty is very clear and gives effect to that right. the ban on discrimination, including discrimination at the level of sexual orientation, is a cornerstone of the eu and is also recognised in another article 21, but this time of the charter of fundamental rights. the directive has brought a very significant improvement for same-sex couples. i would like to thank parliament, because it was parliament which really pushed this through. eu law has provided, for the first time, for the right of both same-sex and different sex couples to move and reside freely within the european union. that said, it is implicit that if you are allowed to move freely and to reside freely, then you must also have the same rights at your second place of residence as you do at your first place of residence. it is for the member states, as has been said, to decide whether or not they provide for registered partnerships or for a legal order, but what we are gradually seeing is more and more member states moving in the direction of either recognising or allowing same-sex marriages. the directive is very modern in that respect because it does not distinguish between same-sex couples and couples of the opposite sex. actually, the directive is neutral on this. it allows such situations to happen and for couples to express themselves and to have this right. in that sense it is not necessary to amend the directive. how this directive is implemented in practical terms is another matter. the directive in itself is not the problem, but rather the interpretation of the directive. for the commission it is very clear that the directive must be applied with full respect for the principle of the prohibition of discrimination on the grounds of sexual orientation. the commission has to ensure the correct application of eu law. this means the commission has to monitor whether, in applying the directive, member states respect fundamental rights, including the prohibition of discrimination on the grounds of sexual orientation – the well-known article 21 of the charter. the commission attaches great importance to eliminating any obstacle restricting the right of free movement and residence, and will continue to work with member states to make sure that the directive is applied correctly. you will know that the commission has adopted guidelines on better transposition of the directive. the guidelines are from july 2009, so we are now looking at the way member states are applying those guidelines in practical terms. the commission welcomes the report on homophobia and discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation issued by the fundamental rights agency. that report (which was drawn up at parliament’s request) provides comprehensive and important data on the human rights of gays, lesbians, bisexuals, transsexuals and trans-gender persons. this data is needed, and i have asked the agency to deepen research in this area – as i declared publicly during the international day against homophobia on 18 may – because we need to know what is going on in practice in the member states. the forthcoming annual report on the application of the charter, which is due in november, will deal with discrimination and homophobia. you can count on my determination to act within the framework of the powers that the treaty has entrusted to the commission. i am sure you understand that this is, for some member states, a very delicate political and social question, because the way of looking at things is not the same all across europe. however, the fact that more and more member states are either recognising or applying marriages, irrespective of the sexual orientation of the partners, is a very good sign. we have to advance step by step. we must, most of all on the basis of our guidelines, bring the member states to accept these rules. for many this is very new and very unusual. for some it is very shocking. we have to advance cautiously, because what we do not want – and i believe all those who have spoken here of their experiences, from their hearts, understand this too – is not to be too harsh. in saying this i am not speaking about the basic values, which are not in question, but we have to bring resisting member states, step by step, to accept the general rules. what we do not want is to have people starting to oppose same-sex marriages, the recognition of rights and non-discrimination. let us see, in the report, the details of how, in the different member states and in different regions of the member states, things are being applied. i do not want there to be any doubts about the fundamentals, about the rights of free movement, irrespective of sexual orientation or ethnicity. these we are going to apply step by step. we will come back to this. some members have given a very personal insight, and i wish to thank them. it is very important for me to grasp the sensitive nature of this issue, which is not only a matter of principle but also a matter of human beings living their personal lives. thank you for that. i am sure that together we will manage to change the situation in the coming months and years.

vice-president of the commission. − madam president, for me it is easy, because the law is very clear. it is about non-discrimination, the right to free movement and mutual recognition. let me stress this. if you live in a legally-recognised same-sex partnership, or marriage, in country a, you have the right – and this is a fundamental right – to take this status and that of your partner to country b. if not, it is a violation of eu law, so there is no discussion about this. this is absolutely clear, and we do not have to hesitate on this. this is the law today, and you can count on me to help you to enforce this. but wait, that is the law. the reality sur le terrain – in real terms – might be different, and we have to change this reality. this is the reason why i have said that we have these bilateral meetings at technical level with member states in order to see how we can change their way of applying something which is very clear in legal terms. permit me here to disagree with baroness ludford. we normally do agree in our analysis, but here, we do not. the directive on free movement does not give the member states discretion to discriminate – no eu directive does. we should not allow a mythology to be developed saying that, actually, it is possible to discriminate. we have to be very firm on the principles. i think here we agree again, do we not? so for me there can be no discussion about the basis of what our legal system is and how it has to be interpreted. we will try to have this applied everywhere in the same way as it is written down, and here you find me on your side. there was a question: when is this going to happen? now! not in five or 10 years. i do not know about a change of mentality in the different member states. i can just tell you about the experience which i have as a politician over so many decades. sometimes governments are more cautious than their populations, and this has been said from personal experience in this chamber. sometimes the population react in a very natural, relaxed way, and the government thinks that there is a very big problem. what i try to do is to bring the governments to understand this. if there is no understanding, then more harsh measures have to be applied.

member of the commission. − madam president, honourable members, let me start by repeating what has been said at the beginning of the discussion about the diversity of europe. we have 27 member states with different social conditions and material conditions and this is the main reason why the commission is now working on a quality framework, not something stronger in terms of legislation. we believe this is now the right concept and we should see how it works together with parliament, with which we have discussed these issues repeatedly in the recent period. one key point where i think we can draw strong conclusions is how long-term care connects with our jobs agenda, how we see a strong capacity for job creation, but it also sets us the task of including this into our skills agenda and finding out how we can do more to train and develop a larger pool of carers who can provide professional services in this area. it is indeed an open question how far we have to formalise these services because, as has been said, much of the work that is being done is informal. it is done, or can be done, by relatives and within families. regulating issues, raising standards or demanding certain conditions within the framework of families and relatives is clearly something which would be highly problematic. meanwhile formalising these services and this work would add to costs and raise taxation issues, and we would easily find ourselves in a dead end in a different direction. so there is no easy answer, while there are indeed compelling grounds to improve the conditions of those who need these services and are dependent on long-term care, but also to recognise those who provide this work. what we certainly can do is collect and disseminate best practices, for example by using the open method of coordination. i can say, at this late hour, that in a few hours’ time i will meet some ministers from the belgian government in liège at a conference on pensions. this will be a good opportunity to convey the words of parliament on this question and connect it with our work on pensions, because these subjects are clearly interlinked in terms of both social security in general and an adequate income for the elderly. we have a longer-term plan to follow up our work on pensions with a serious effort on demography. the forthcoming hungarian and polish presidencies are equally interested in this subject, and we are exploring the right framework for the deliverables involved. this work will be followed by the european year on active ageing, which is not only about employment – and definitely not simply about extending the pensionable age – but is also about doing more to preserve health and to upgrade lifelong learning, lifelong teaching, capacities and institutions in order to improve the quality of life. so this is fundamentally a framework in which we can, i think, continue our work. it is full of challenges, but with the ethical commitment we all share, i think we can produce results.
