on behalf of the efd group. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, it is important and necessary to strike a balance between the need to carry out scientific research and the need to protect animal welfare. at present, there is a lack of protection for animals used in scientific procedures. new scientific knowledge can be used to promote alternatives to replace or reduce the use of animals. methods or procedures should be used that cause as little pain and suffering as possible, but without hindering scientific experimentation in the fight against disease. it is therefore right to review european legislation on the protection of animals in order to achieve satisfactory results while preserving the needs of the research industry, given the need to continue scientific research for the benefit of human health and at the same time protecting the welfare of animals still needed for scientific purposes.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, after a year and a half of difficult negotiations between parliament, the council and the commission, we have finally reached a compromise text on the sensitive issue of animal testing. it was a difficult job and i would like to thank our rapporteur, mrs elizabeth jeggle, and our shadow rapporteurs for conducting such an intense negotiation. the text was approved in the committee on agriculture and rural development, which i have the honour of chairing, with no votes against and only four abstentions. it is a good balance between the need to improve the welfare of animals used in experiments and the need to allow progress in medical research. the proposal aims to analyse and improve the 1986 directive, which is now obsolete, and to harmonise european rules in this area. we all have a particular concern about animal testing, and so does the public, but i can say with conviction, ladies and gentlemen, that we are about to vote on a reasonable text, the result of serious and rigorous work, which represents an advance on existing legislation in terms of animal protection, but which at the same time does not lose sight of the moral responsibility we have to advance medical research.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the rapporteur and those who have worked with her have certainly done a difficult job for which we thank them. i cannot hide from you that i, and certain members of the italian government with whom i identify, are perplexed by a problem which, after 24 years, still seems to us to have not been solved in the right way. some colleagues have pointed out that animals have different sensitivities than humans. in fact, no animal would ever do what is happening in iran, which has already happened and will happen again. animals do not generally torture, stone and tell those lies that are so typical even of our political world. we have the right to ask these animals to be useful for better scientific research and for the improvement of human health, but we have no right to ask that they continue to be used for useless, repetitive experiments, which only serve to pocket money for some pseudo-researchers. we know very well that in vitro experiments or computer simulations of human metabolism can now achieve more certain results than those obtained by animal experiments, because it is often not possible to transfer the result of the experiment from one species to another, nor in the animal world, nor from animal to man. for these reasons we would like to see this provision revised to be more in keeping with modernity and mutual respect.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i thank the rapporteur and the shadow rapporteurs for the result achieved. i believe that we have achieved the best possible compromise between the needs of research and ensuring the welfare of animals used for scientific purposes. unfortunately, animal research is still fundamental, there are no alternatives. computer simulations and cell cultures are not enough, say not politicians but researchers. so i would like to remind you that some very serious diseases have been defeated because of tests carried out on living species. i would remind you that 98% of these species are rodents and therefore only a small proportion of the larger species are used. i would also like to remind you that thanks to these tests, we now have treatments for leukemia, diabetes and certain types of cancer. finally, i would like to remind you that researchers are the first to want to avoid unnecessary suffering and i think that all you have to do is visit them at work to confirm this. it is true that there are still some parts which are worrying. i would like to mention one that has not yet been mentioned: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the animal welfare committees are not merely a means of ensuring that animals are protected, but also a means of ensuring that animals are protected. this raises some alarm amongst those who work in the field, because many laboratories already have ethics committees and others are being set up. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.

the next item is the oral question to the council on arms exports by mr arturs krišjānis kariņš, mr tunne kelam, mr vytautas landsbergis, mr gunnar hökmark, mr bendt bendtsen, mr jacek saryusz-wolski, mr ville itälä, mrs sandra kalniete, mr inese vaidere, mr michael gahler, mr josé ignacio salafranca sánchez-neyra and mrs laima liucija andrikienė, on behalf of the group of the european people's party (o-0076/2010 - b7-0320/2010).
president of the council. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i can only welcome the opportunity this afternoon to look at arms export controls. the high representative, mrs ashton, was unable to be present at this part-session and has asked the presidency to take her place for this debate and i will therefore try to answer a number of questions which have come to us on this subject. as you know, the european union has for many years played a leading role in the control of arms exports, both at regional and international level, and the objective is clear: we want to prevent the export of military technology that could be used for undesirable purposes such as internal repression or international aggression. more than a decade ago, the council adopted a european union code of conduct on arms exports which set out a set of criteria for the export of conventional arms. the code was replaced in 2008 by a common position which introduces a number of new elements, making the eu the most comprehensive international arms export control regime in the world. the legally binding provisions of the common position help to ensure that member states export arms in a responsible and transparent manner. the common position aims to coordinate effectively national policies on arms export controls, in particular through an information and consultation mechanism for refusals. and under this mechanism, when a member state is considering granting an export authorization for a transaction identical to a transaction that has been previously refused by another member state, it must consult the latter and inform all member states of its final decision. in other words, a member state which grants an authorisation for a transaction which has been refused by another member state must justify its decision to all member states. so, in answering questions about consultations, the situation is clear: the common position provides for systematic consultation only, of course, in cases where an identical transaction has previously been refused authorization. in general, the delegations of the member states within the relevant council structures also exchange information frequently and regularly on arms control and in particular on so-called 'sensitive' destinations. member states often seek the opinion of other members of the council on any destination which might be a cause for concern or about which there would be doubts. this regular exchange of information is a central element of the european union's arms export control policy. during 2009, consultations between member states covered, for information purposes, a total of 14 third countries of destination. the member states then provided information on the grounds on which they decided to grant or refuse export authorisations to these destinations. that is the way we proceed, mr president, in terms of information, control and interaction between member states to see how we are authorizing arms exports. i shall be glad to take up in a reply any other point you may wish to raise in the course of the discussion this afternoon.
the strengthening of the industrial and technological base of european defence is an essential dimension of the construction of a common defence. but it needs common rules and a coordinated approach to strengthen the development and competitiveness of the european defence industry and, at the same time, to make this development consistent with europe's international principles and commitments. the common position of december 2008, which sets out procedures and criteria for military exports to third countries, is therefore an important step forward, together with the internal defence market directive. as is well known, there is no general consultation mechanism in these procedures. however, the common position makes a very appropriate reference to the need to strengthen cooperation and convergence in this field within the framework of the cfsp. until the desirable progress on this front and on the creation of a common defence makes it possible to adopt even more binding mechanisms, it would be appropriate for the cooperation and convergence provided for in article 7 not to remain on paper only and for the annual report on military exports to be made known to parliament. of course, the question put by the members of the house seems implicitly - now it has been made explicit - not to be limited to general questions. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the common position is respected. on the contrary, such exports can strengthen and make more binding the euro-russian bond and cooperation in the field of security, which should however go beyond the bilateral sphere and be addressed, discussed and carried out to the full in a european dimension.
president of the council. - mr president, this was a very interesting debate and i should like to return to two concepts and make a number of clarifications. first, i would like to reframe the notion of responsibility. article 4 (2) of the common position provides that the decision to transfer or refuse to transfer military technology or equipment is left to the national discretion of each member state. this responsibility therefore lies first and foremost at national level and the common position does not of course remove this responsibility from the member states but it introduces a wide range of provisions to ensure effective coordination and exchange of information between them. the second concept i want to come back to is the concept of transparency. the common position provides that member states are to draw up a report on their arms exports each year. an eu report based on the national reports shall be published annually and shall provide information on the financial value of authorisations granted, broken down by destination and by category of military equipment, as well as on the number of authorisations refused and any subsequent consultations by member states. in addition to the annual report of the european union, the common position provides for member states to publish national reports on exports of military technology and equipment. the objective of transparency set out in the common position therefore applies both at the level of the european union and at the national level, and the european union must, of course, lead by example in this respect. i should also like to say that the common position is - and some of you have already said this - a considerable step forward in relation to the code of conduct. it was adopted in december 2008, less than two years ago. it is reasonable to allow the new provisions introduced by the common position to have their effect before any revision of a new system such as this is undertaken, even though - i have heard you, and even understood you - making it more binding or combining it with a system of sanctions may seem attractive. the commission's proposal for a regulation on the common position of the council on the conclusion of the interim agreement on trade in textile products between the european community and the republic of korea, which was adopted by the council on 14 june, is a very good one.
thank you, mr ries. i am glad that you have reiterated what i said at the beginning of the sitting when i announced this news. we are continuing this fight for the review of the process and in general for the affirmation of human rights throughout the world. the debate is closed.

member of the commission. − madam president, honourable members, pakistan has indeed been very much in the limelight in the last month, and of course we all deplored the horrible loss of life and the many displaced persons. as you know, both the commission and the council are very much engaged in trying to alleviate the situation by finding ways to increase trade, as well as ways of rebuilding the country and helping it to prevent further disasters. this was also discussed at the council meeting last week. turning to today’s item, i want to thank the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs (libe) and the rapporteur, mr sógor, for their very constructive work on this, and for the support given to the commission when your adopted your opinion in july. the readmission agreement has been for many years now an important tool in managing migration flows, and the lisbon treaty explicitly mentions readmission agreements. if we want migration and asylum policy to be credible to european citizens, it must be based on the principle that those who do not have a legal right to remain in the territory are returned. this is where readmission agreements come in. they facilitate the return of persons staying irregularly in the country of origin or transit and they are agreements between administrations stipulating the procedures to be followed. over the course of time, admission agreements have also become linked to visa policy. in a series of readmission agreements they have become an indispensable element when negotiating a visa facilitation agreement. the commission is committed to pursuing these negotiations under current or future mandates. let me address a few of the concerns raised by speakers in the form of oral questions. the commission is committed to giving full effect to its obligation under article 218 in the treaty to immediately and fully inform parliament at all stages of the negotiations and of the conclusion of eu readmission agreements. we will implement these obligations, taking full account of parliament’s role in the adoption procedure, namely the requirement that it give its consent to the conclusion of future readmission agreements. we will provide all the necessary information, subject to measures ensuring confidentiality in the case of ongoing negotiations, and in accordance with precise arrangements within the future framework of relations between parliament and the commission. in the meantime, the director-general, mr manservici, has already given you, in camera with the libe committee on 12 july, the first general update on the ongoing negotiations. mrs griesbeck also mentioned the declaration made by the commission, and of course we will follow that very closely and report to you accordingly. we should also explore together how to further optimise this cooperation. turning to agreements with countries not signatories of the geneva convention, we would of course like pakistan to sign this, and we are heavily involved in trying to convince them and in trying to pursue these negotiations, because the commission is — as are you all — very attached to the values of international instruments on human rights and international protection, and a proper application of those instruments must be at the core of eu policy. for this reason we have developed the european union acquis on international protection – the qualification and asylum procedures directives – which also includes human rights safeguards in its return policy, namely the returns directive. in addition, all member states of the european union are bound by the geneva convention relating to the status of refugees and the european convention on human rights. these standards guarantee that no person may be removed from any member state, or subjected to readmission procedures, before the risk that, once returned, that person may be subject to persecution, or torture, or inhumane or degrading punishment, has been fully evaluated and excluded. in particular the eu’s asylum instrument requires that member states assess each application for asylum individually, guaranteeing that the applicant remain on the territory until the authorities have taken a decision on the said application, and then they must provide for an effective remedy before a court or a tribunal. these standards are vital for the respect of the non-refoulement principle and are by no means limited by any readmission agreement, which is a very, very important point. all eu readmission agreements contain the non-affection clause explicitly requiring that these standards be respected. we should also not forget that these readmission agreements can play an important role in undermining the activities of migrant-smuggling networks. a report earlier this year from the united nations office on drugs and crime, assessing criminal assisted migration from pakistan, estimated that the annual revenue of this so-called industry amounted to 1.25 billion dollars. the report recommended, inter alia, that pakistan initiate operation and cooperation agreements with key partners, including general agreements for mutual legal assistance and extradition. with regard to visa facilitation agreements, no list of prerequisite criteria for deciding to open such negotiations exists, but the european union takes into account the conclusion of, or active negotiations on, readmission agreements, external relations objectives, implementation records of existing bilateral agreements and progress on related areas in the field of justice and home affairs — including fundamental rights. it should be noted that, for all countries with which the eu has concluded visa facilitation agreements, the commission has presented a draft negotiating mandate to the council as a follow-up to council conclusions which envisage the promotion of people-to-people contact with the country concerned. readmission agreements are monitored by the joint readmission committees. these are set up under each agreement. furthermore, we gather any relevant information about the implementation of the agreements in force. so far, no major problems have been reported, not even by ngos who are active in these fields, despite the fact that some of the countries where such agreements are fully operational have been very sensitive. in any case, under a readmission agreement, no-one shall be returned if this would entail the risk that the person concerned would be subject to persecution, torture or inhumane or degrading punishment. should that happen, this is not a consequence of the readmission agreement, but of an illegal decision taken by the member state concerned, which should be subject to judicial review by mr president, ladies and gentlemen, biodiversity is a measure of the variety of animal and plant species in the biosphere: it is the result of long evolutionary processes. evolution is the mechanism that has enabled life to adapt to the changing conditions on earth for over three billion years and that must continue to operate if this earth is to be a home for life in the future. it must be understood not only as the result of evolutionary processes but also as the reservoir from which evolution draws to implement all the genetic and morphological modifications that originate new living species. biodiversity is the life insurance of our planet, so its conservation must be pursued without limits, since it is a universal heritage that can offer immediate benefits to man, such as the maintenance of climate balances, both at local and planetary scales, as a source of study material that allows fundamental knowledge to be gained also to understand similar biological mechanisms in man, such as the sustainable use of flora and fauna for food and medicinal purposes. its conservation is rightly one of the european objectives for the post-2010 year of biodiversity.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by my colleague because i consider it to be a major step forward in this field. the proposal for a regulation on the investigation and prevention of accidents in civil aviation aims to increase the transparency of information made available by national civil aviation authorities. it also represents a necessary modernisation of the rules currently applied, which date back to 1994. the measures for the creation of an efficient communication system between national authorities, with the aim of facilitating coordination and greater sharing of the data collected, are noteworthy. access to sensitive information shall be regulated in order to enable the competent authorities to rely on the cooperation of all parties involved in accidents.
in writing. − air traffic has been increasing steadily for several years, but despite considerable improvements in safety, this growth has only increased the risk of air accidents. in such a situation, it is essential that accidents are subject to independent investigations which can determine with certainty the safety deficiencies and allow for corrective action. at present, the european legislation on accident investigation consists of a single directive of 1994: since then, air traffic has evolved, become more complex and new actors have emerged, such as the european aviation safety agency (easa), which have highlighted discrepancies in the investigative capacities of member states and have necessitated new and more satisfactory legislation. in order to reduce disparities in the investigation capabilities of the european union, it would be appropriate to establish a network of national investigation offices which could also increase the quality of the investigations themselves and provide a legal framework for cooperation between national authorities. i believe that such action could make a real contribution to improving aviation safety.

in writing. we are all aware of the recent environmental disaster in pakistan, the enormous damage to the land, the loss of crops, the more than ten million displaced people and the thousands of deaths. our commitment is to help this country and to develop solidarity and coordination initiatives to facilitate a speedy recovery. but we must not lose sight of the need to make the european area a safe place, which has unfortunately been compromised by years of continuous flows of illegal immigration and trafficking. the agreement on readmission procedures, reached after eight years of negotiations between the european commission and pakistan, sets out a clearer framework for cooperation, co-responsibility and is seen as a deterrent to human trafficking and illicit trafficking. such an agreement would avoid those situations of return without eu supervision. first of all, member states will have to comply with obligations arising from international law, such as the principle of non-refoulement, which will therefore have procedural implications since the member states will be required to carry out an assessment of the risk of ill-treatment in the country of origin. we will also ensure our long-term cooperation with pakistan and encourage programmes of technical assistance and economic and social development and the fight against unemployment and social exclusion.
in writing. - the conclusion of an agreement with pakistan is a positive step which europe must take in the direction of a policy of decisive action against illegal immigration. the citizens of europe today are asking for greater security and a policy of strict control of the migratory flows that flow into our countries. any text such as this, which facilitates the procedures for the return of those who are not legally entitled to remain in the community, is to be welcomed as europe's collective response to the demands of our citizens. as regards the concerns raised by some colleagues about the living conditions that returnees to pakistan might encounter, i believe that these are important arguments which should not prevent the conclusion of an agreement which would nevertheless include a commitment by the eu that pakistan will in future provide the minimum guarantees needed in the field of human rights and the treatment of refugees. europe must direct its diplomatic and political efforts in this direction, but not without doing what the people are asking for at home: security and respect for the law. i therefore vote in favour of the report.
in writing. - we support the report on the conclusion of the eu-pakistan agreement on the readmission of persons residing without authorisation. this agreement helps to strengthen the fight against illegal immigration to the eu by facilitating the process of deportation of irregular pakistani nationals and their readmission to their countries of origin. it should be possible to extend the same type of agreement to the other countries from which illegal immigrants usually come. in the temporary residence centres, time is often wasted in order to obtain permission to return from the country of origin, once the irregular person's nationality has been identified, thus exceeding the maximum periods of detention. with agreements such as the one we are approving today, waiting times are reduced and it is therefore easier and cheaper to manage the return of irregular immigrants.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, this measure is intended to strengthen and rationalise the pharmacovigilance system in the european union. these are the ambitious objectives set out in the mcavan reports, amending regulation (ec) no 726/2004 and directive 2001/83/ec respectively. the council and parliament, and the relevant parliamentary committees, have worked together closely and efficiently to discuss a proposal aimed at improving the community pharmacovigilance system and perfecting the european union's extensive work in this field, which has been going on for more than a decade. simplification, transparency and rationalisation can be seen as the key points of these two reports which propose measures to ensure the best possible protection of public health, based on harmonised standards across europe. the report covers a wide range of interventions, ranging from a better definition of the roles and responsibilities of the main national and supranational stakeholders, to a new and more consciously active involvement of the patient, who is recognised as a key player in the system, to the strengthening of the transparency of information on the safety of medicines, to the simplification of communication, registration and assessment of suspected adverse side effects. the current pharmacovigilance system needs to be improved, including through closer cooperation at european, national and regional levels. effective participation at all three levels will ensure a fruitful exchange of information on adverse reactions to medicinal products. the new pharmacovigilance system, therefore, reorganised as a network, including via web-based support, will be able to ensure a high level of shared and secure information for the benefit of patients, national authorities and healthcare professionals.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner tajani, the primary objective of this proposal for a regulation is to verify the safety of medicinal products once they have been authorized for public use. the controls and evaluations of positive or negative effects are never excessive. it is estimated that the side effects of medicines cause 197 000 deaths in the european union every year. clinical trials can often detect side effects if they occur infrequently, after prolonged use of the drug, or if they result from interactions with other medicines. monitoring the use of medicines and reporting their side effects is, and must remain, a priority of european public health policy. a good pharmacovigilance system must be able to enable healthcare professionals, companies and patients themselves to report side effects of medicines and to detect signs of potential problems. once these signs are identified, action should be taken, for example by changing the way the medicine is prescribed, improving information on the use of the medicine or by completely withdrawing the product in case of particularly severe side effects. the proposal to strengthen cooperation on pharmacovigilance will have many advantages, as it will make it possible to deal with a greater number of reports, so that even the rarest cases can be detected more quickly. this will make it possible to withdraw dangerous medicines from the market more quickly if they are needed. all states will have to continue to be the main actors in the pharmacovigilance system in the european union. i would like to conclude, mr president, by stressing the importance of allowing patients to report directly on the side effects of these medicines. unfortunately, today only a limited number of states accept direct reporting and i would like to stress that in the countries where it is used it does not impose any additional workload on the competent authority.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to thank you for your work. i think it is important that we should discuss this subject here, and i would like to draw attention to one particular issue, namely the multilingualism of information and, in particular, the package insert. i am a member of a linguistic minority and live in one of the most touristic regions of our european union. in each state, the medicines are accompanied by a package insert in the language of the state. this is why, in my region, for example, a significant proportion of people simply do not understand the package insert. it's not only unpleasant, it's dangerous. we must now get this directive to the point where information on package inserts is available from home on the internet and also in the pharmacy. if we can then also present this information in a concise and summary form, then it can also be printed on the package insert itself in several languages without having to attach entire leaflets to the medicines.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we support the rapporteur's approach, as it emphasizes the importance of checking the safety of medicines and improving the transparency of pharmacovigilance activities. the northern league has focused on a few aspects: allow direct access by the patient to the community database of reports of suspected adverse reactions; allow the introduction of fees, at the discretion of the member states, to be charged for pharmacovigilance assessments; and define the composition and mandate of the risk assessment committee in order to give an appropriate role to member states, healthcare professionals and patients. unfortunately, in a europe which is increasingly concerned with health and quality of life, it is easy to abuse medicines. negative interactions between products used for health, medical, plant protection purposes are possible and this can lead in sensitive individuals from the simplest cases of allergic reactions to actual diseases that debilitate people. one of these, which is not yet fully understood and which unfortunately is not easily solvable, is the multiple chemical syndrome: people who are affected can no longer live a normal life because they can no longer tolerate any chemical. it is therefore important that the european union takes action to inform and train citizens in the conscious use of the drug.
in writing. medicinal products make an essential contribution to the health of citizens in the european union. however, they can also have serious side effects, which the commission estimates are responsible for about 5% of hospital admissions and deaths. in recent years there have been cases of medicinal products which, although they were placed on the market after the planned monitoring procedure, have shown significant side effects in patients. this context underlines the need for the union to have an effective pharmacovigilance policy to protect the health of european citizens. i believe that an efficient pharmacovigilance system should enable the competent authorities to be informed promptly of the side effects of medicinal products and, above all, to withdraw dangerous medicinal products from the market rapidly if necessary. i also share the proposals in this report to improve cooperation between member states in the field of pharmacovigilance and to strengthen the criteria for granting marketing authorizations for new medicinal products. finally, i ask the commission to consider revising the composition of the package leaflet for medicinal products in order to improve information on the use of a medicinal product.
in writing. many diseases can now be treated without hospitalisation, and even in oncology there are drug treatments that make home treatment possible. the control of the pharmaceutical chain therefore requires rational and clear procedures which improve the flow of information and transparency in content by clearly defining the roles and responsibilities of the main parties involved. i fully support the creation of a centralised data collection and evaluation system which can complement national pharmacovigilance networks while maintaining consistency of information. the filter of national networks, the only instrument capable of ensuring the objectivity of the validation, the quality of the data encoding, the causal link and the relationship with the reporting persons, could not be excluded. this is all the more necessary now that we are opening up an additional channel of direct information to the patient and to healthcare professionals who will also now have the opportunity to quickly send a valuable feedback message to the surveillance system. in this connection, i would point out the need for training measures for health workers and an information campaign for patients to make more effective use of this tool.
the commission's vice-president - mr president, i would like to thank the european parliament, and in particular the rapporteur, mrs klass, the non-attached rapporteurs and the members of the committee on the environment, public health and food safety, for their considerable work. the 330 amendments adopted by the committee on the environment and the overall compromise adopted last week are a testament to their commitment and interest in this matter. these amendments support the general thrust of the commission's proposal. let me dwell on what we consider to be the most important outstanding issues. firstly, the extension of the union's authorization system and the procedures relating to it. in order to reach agreement on this issue, it is essential to reach a compromise on the study of the union authorisation system and related procedures, and in particular on the role of the european chemicals agency. while the commission can in principle support the extension of the union authorisation system to a wider group of biocidal products, this support can only be given under two conditions. first, echa and the commission must have adequate resources to handle the additional workload. the absence of sufficient means will result in delays that will undermine the benefits of the union authorisation system. secondly, we must devise an appropriate mechanism for the gradual extension of the scope of the system, for example by spreading the introduction of product types over time or by using horizontal criteria such as similar conditions of use. as regards the procedures related to union authorisation, the role of echa will be essential in the functioning of the system. we need to ensure that echa's resources are used for tasks which add value in terms of harmonisation, or which cannot be carried out more effectively by the member states. i would add that the procedures must be designed to cope with the extension of the scope of the union's authorization system. secondly, the derogations from the exclusion criteria. on the thorny issue of derogations from the exclusion criteria, i note that the compromise amendment strikes a reasonable balance between the objective of ensuring a high level of protection of the environment and human health and the need to provide for some flexibility in the event that no alternative solution exists. thirdly, national derogations in the context of mutual recognition. while we recognize that national derogations under mutual recognition may be justified in certain circumstances, we believe that these derogations should be examined on a case-by-case basis by the commission. the authorization of these derogations without provision for supervision by the commission risks jeopardizing the internal market for biocidal products, which the regulation is intended to promote. the fourth question is the definition of low-risk products. as regards the definition of low-risk products, we must strive to establish a pragmatic definition, which is a prerequisite for an effective policy on these products. efforts are still needed before the criteria for low-risk products can be clearly defined. question no 5: what are the items covered? as far as the articles are concerned, we support the amendments to extend the controls to the active substances. as regards the labelling of these articles, we support the general approach of imposing different rules depending on whether the articles have an internal or external effect, for example, whether there is intentional disposal of the product or whether it comes into contact with humans or the environment. question no 6: opportunities in the field of transport while we support the compromise amendment on opportunities, we have serious concerns about some other amendments relating to the concept of inclusion by company. the seventh question is about nanomaterials. on the question of nanomaterials, the commission, in keeping with its policy of decision-making based on scientific evidence and its desire to improve knowledge of these materials, agrees with the need for a definition of nanomaterials and, where appropriate, the principle of separate evaluation of nanomaterials. finally, the animal tests. while the commission supports the objective of reducing the use of animal testing, it believes that this should not be done at the expense of a high level of protection of the environment and human health. i shall now follow your debate on the proposal and the proposed amendments closely and i shall be able to provide further clarification on these and other points in my closing remarks.

on behalf of the efd group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the term 'biocidal' refers to active substances and preparations containing one or more active substances, in the form in which they are supplied to the user, which are intended to destroy, eliminate, render harmless, prevent the action of, or otherwise exert a controlling effect on, any harmful organism by chemical or biological means. so, basically, almost all the fruits and vegetables that come to our table are processed. although these products are now indispensable, since most of the animal or plant pests are increasingly resistant to their action, they must be kept under control because they are often harmful to man. for example, some of them, when applied to foodstuffs, have a specific shelf life, so they must be used at specific times of the year and in specific qualities. failure to comply with these deadlines has serious consequences for the human being taking the treated product: from immediate allergic reactions to those related to prolonged use over time which can be and lead to serious health conditions. biocides also include actual poisons, such as rodenticides, which are freely available for domestic use. unfortunately, although there are risks in allowing these products to be sold, we cannot think of banning their use at a time when we are witnessing a considerable increase in the number of rodent and pest colonies in european cities. the use of different types of biocides, whether or not authorized in the various member states, and even more so the entry of goods from third countries where they are not yet controlled, must also be given special attention, precisely for the free movement of goods within the european union. we must ensure that the european union takes the use of these products seriously and that the expiry dates for their toxicity are strictly observed.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner tajani, the proposal for a regulation on biocidal products which we are examining will be designed to simplify the authorization and renewal procedures for the placing of biocidal products on the market. this simplification will lead to a reduction in costs and administrative burden for businesses, especially small and medium-sized enterprises, without reducing the protection of the environment and human and animal health. it has been very difficult to strike a balance between these two aspects, but i think that some of the compromise amendments reached between the rapporteur and the shadow rapporteurs, whom i thank for their hard work, have been an important step forward. in order to remain consistent with the call for simplification, i believe that the comparative evaluation procedure should not be required for those biocides for which a safe use has been demonstrated and not as it is now required for any biocide. i hope that the amendment tabled in this way in the plenary will be accepted by the house.

member of the commission. − madam president, draft amending budget no 7 is a follow-up to the decision to establish the european financial stabilisation mechanism, which is in turn the response to the dramatic developments of march, april and may in the financial markets. therefore, the european financial stabilisation mechanism – up to eur 60 billion – has been established in addition to the already existing balance of payments facility, with more or less the same philosophy. in response to the question from lászló surján, under the normal desired circumstances, even if a european financial stabilisation mechanism is mobilised, this should not have an impact on the eu budget. under normal circumstances, that is, where the beneficiary state taking the loans repays the loans. it is activated as a guarantee but without a financial impact upon the budget. in the highly unlikely scenario – not zero probability, unfortunately, but very unlikely scenario – that a member state defaults on its obligations, we have to ensure that the european union is ready in time to fulfil its legal obligations towards the lenders. so we should be ready for this unlikely bad scenario. put simply, that is, in a sense, what is behind draft budget no 7. therefore, as with the balance of payments facility, we proposed creating a structure for the new budget item on the expenditure side of the budget and a corresponding new budget article on the revenue side of the budget. these are token entries – as happened with the balance of payments facilities – and have the same logic behind them. the philosophy behind this is that we should be ready in case. i am therefore happy that draft amending budget no 7 has been discussed and has already been formally adopted by the council on 13 september. now we hope for the same decision from parliament.
the amendment to the budget we are discussing today and which we will be voting on in the coming days is an important document, it marks the last step in the implementation of the financial stabilisation mechanism, the mechanism which was so much needed last may to stem the serious storm that hit the euro and thus the union. out of this storm came a certainty: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full. the european union has succeeded in giving a united response, it has found the courage and the strength to give, and that is what we are discussing today. this new budget line marks a clear boundary, it is the first step towards a new shared vision of the financial and in future also economic policies of the member states in relation to the european budget. it is the first step towards that integrated six-month period in which the budgetary choices of individual countries and the community budget will be more closely compared. the budget thus returns to the centre stage the instrument which has always been the key to implementing the union's policies and is also a key instrument for building post-lisbon europe. it is a question of the need to ensure that the european union is able to take full advantage of the opportunities offered by the single market.

in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, medicinal products make a vital contribution to the health of european citizens. however, they can have adverse effects, which, according to the european commission, account for about 5% of all hospital admissions. pharmacovigilance is the process and science of monitoring the safety of medicinal products, including the collection and management of safety data, the evaluation of data to identify safety concerns, the actions to be taken, and the evaluation of the procedure followed and the results obtained. the commission wants to improve the current system of pharmacovigilance by simplifying procedures, increasing transparency, and better defining the roles and participation of stakeholders. however, i believe that there is room for further changes, particularly as regards consumer and data protection: for example, consumers and healthcare professionals should have full access to the european eudravigilance database to prevent the recurrence of adverse reactions to medicinal products, should be able to use not only a web-based reporting format but also other tools such as e-mail, fax or telephone; i also believe that the financing of surveillance systems should continue to be public so that the authorities can be held accountable.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of this proposal because the need to provide patients with correct information has been evident for too long. death from the side effects of medicines is the fifth leading cause of death in the eu in recent years, which is why action such as that advocated by this parliament could no longer be extended. i have therefore chosen to guarantee quality of life for the patient, to give certainty about the possible occurrence of adverse reactions in the patient, to make the drug a real ally of the sufferer, and finally to allow a drug to be promptly withdrawn from the market in the event of problems. in our europe, the creation of a single web portal in all languages is a great innovation and a great support for all european patients who can thus define themselves, in their own right, as united in protecting their health.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the text which has been adopted is a considerable improvement on the original proposal and i congratulate mrs klass on her successful mediation. i welcome the achievement of the objectives of a higher level of data protection for industry and the gradual introduction of a centralised authorisation procedure at european level for the placing of these products on the market. the identification of more stringent labelling requirements will also help the consumer to make a more informed and safer choice. in short, we are moving in the right direction, but there are still some steps to be taken: the regulatory framework on research and development is not consistent with other advanced sectoral regulations such as the reach directive. the financial allocation required for the european chemicals agency to carry out its new evaluation task has also not yet been communicated. i expect the commission to make this clear in the near future, also in view of the workload already imposed on this body by the reach directive.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the role of biocides has always been a matter of some controversy, probably because of the difficulty of identifying and defining them. but the fact remains that biocides have many applications in our daily lives and it is therefore necessary to know their real impact on the safety and health of all of us. for these reasons i voted for the simplification and harmonization of the rules for european industry but also for the member states which will have new regulations adapted to new civil requirements. the introduction of a harmonised system of approval criteria will help to avoid double risk assessments of products already authorised: the commission has already taken a number of important steps in this direction.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, biocides are an integral part of our civilisation and are indispensable to meet our high hygiene and health requirements; biocidal products must be effective in preventing disease and infection, but may, at the same time, be highly dangerous: this requires optimal management of the substances themselves. the new regulation on the use of biocidal products must ensure that producers, i.e. medium-sized enterprises, can comply with the provisions adopted at the production stage without encountering competitive disadvantages. it is also important that both consumers and producers of materials containing biocides can rely on minimum standards that are valid in all eu countries. in my view, the regulation proposed by the commission needs substantial changes and improvements in order to achieve its objectives, including addressing the shortcomings of the current directive, improving the authorisation procedure and streamlining the decision-making process, while maintaining a high level of protection. the new regulation will have to pay particular attention to three key areas: environmental protection, consumer safety and safe, practice-oriented application of the rules by producers. the new regulation will also provide for a simplified authorisation procedure to avoid unnecessary costs and excessive fees.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the european financial system is to be maintained by careful risk management and a careful assessment of the structural stability of the whole sector. a new supervisory authority means that the union institutions will take a stronger responsibility for crisis prevention by discouraging free riding and monitoring behaviour and attitudes. in view of the growing integration of national markets, with the inevitable lowering of defensive barriers, concerted action is needed to make threats, whether internal or external, immune.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing the european insurance and occupational pensions authority because i believe that it is necessary to close the gaps that exist today in terms of coordination, the uniform application of eu law and trust between national supervisory authorities. the recent financial crisis has in fact highlighted the inefficiency of some national supervisory models, which have failed to deal effectively with the problematic situations that have been created in the reality of european financial markets. i can therefore only welcome and support the choice to strengthen the supervisory framework, based on an intervention aimed at identifying instruments capable of preventing the occurrence of risks to the stability of the financial system in the future. the new system of financial supervision is therefore intended to fill the gaps in the sector, to improve the functioning of the internal market and, finally, to ensure a high and uniform level of regulation and supervision, taking account of the needs of the individual member states.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, most economists believe that forecasts are almost never reasonably certain, so the only remedy is to be vigilant and to be immune. the european parliament, together with the council of ministers of economy and finance and the commissioners responsible, has done a very good job. let us not be fooled into thinking that this is enough, nor that the past can be erased, but we can once again have confidence in the banking and financial sector in the future, since macroprudential supervision is entrusted to a body whose task is to monitor the entire european market, the entire euro area, and not its fragmentation, which is no longer valid today. moreover, the protection of this authority extends from european countries to all those whose currency is in any way linked to the euro, and thus to our companies and all those who do business with them.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i fully support the report and the rules introduced which aim to bring greater stability to the market. the report was necessary to safeguard the unity of the internal market. the protection of the internal market is essential! however, i have doubts about the supervision that will be the responsibility of the european central bank, several times in the past the central banks, which should have been supervising, have not done so and much of this crisis is their fault. i would have preferred a different control organ. that is why i voted in favour of the text but abstained in the vote on the legislative resolution.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, since the launch of the financial services action plan parliament has played a central role in building the single market for financial services, promoting not only harmonisation, transparency and fair competition but also ensuring the protection of investors and consumers. long before the financial crisis, parliament has on several occasions called for the strengthening of effective european level playing field for all stakeholders, pointing out major shortcomings on the part of europe in the surveillance of increasingly integrated financial markets. in all its reports parliament has called on the commission to examine how to move towards a more integrated supervisory structure. the need for effective surveillance of the systemic and prudential risks of the main market players was also noted. in order to move towards a more integrated supervisory structure, the commission has published legislative proposals to establish a new network of european supervisory authorities focusing on three pillars: the first for banking, the second for insurance and occupational pensions, the third for financial instruments and markets. finally, a european systemic risk board should be established to monitor and assess potential threats to financial stability.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the establishment of one or more authorities is necessary but not sufficient to detect signs of anomalies and prevent problems arising in the financial markets. the second step is to calibrate these authorities so that they are given non-redundant, concrete, and achievable functions and tasks. the new institutions are not there to discharge responsibility, to identify the guilty and punish them, but to study the markets and to point out the critical points, to highlight the wrong trends and attitudes, to propose solutions. the aim must not be punishment, because no financial punishment can ever restore trust; the aim must be to prevent problems, to solve them early, to identify those indicators which, more than others, anticipate the emergence of possible problems. this report analyses the following critical issues and attempts to address them by designing a mechanism which, ex ante and with our knowledge of financial mechanisms, has a very high probability of working well.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i congratulate the rapporteur on his year-long work and the comprehensive results achieved. it is now well known that the financial crisis first and the economic crisis second have highlighted how crucial it is for europe to have a single voice: in the face of a global economic crisis, the eu cannot be divided. we have seen that european financial regulation was inadequate and that the supervisory mechanisms proved to be ineffective. the report therefore attempts to remedy these shortcomings: the attempt to establish a genuine european authority with clear responsibilities is entirely to be welcomed. the effort to establish a mechanism for resolving future crises is also commendable. our task is first and foremost to protect the interests of citizens and savers, who in some cases have seen their savings go up in smoke: the commission has therefore decided to set up an eu fund, pre-financed by the financial institutions, to protect depositors as provided for in amendment no 137. i therefore consider the report to be balanced in its intentions, even when it identifies a very specific role for smes (see amendments 169-170), which are still paying the highest price of this crisis. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the banking system, which performs its crucial social and economic function, has the characteristic of pursuing multiple objectives and often causing undesirable effects. while the main purpose of shareholders is wealth creation, the main purpose of some stakeholders may be to support a cash-strapped business system or to create wealth through financial instruments that facilitate savings. while the objectives of each are sacred, the impact of management decisions in these enterprises on the surrounding economic and social fabric cannot be overlooked. it is therefore the duty of politics to safeguard the interests of the various actors, while demanding that no one should shirk his moral and social duties. it is therefore europe's task to ensure that everyone can achieve his goals without clashing with the other actors involved. and we must applaud the establishment of an authority which will be able to carry out this mission.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the present financial crisis has brought to light a problem which the european parliament had denounced many years ago, namely the inadequacy of financial regulation and the weakness of market surveillance mechanisms. parliament warned that in order to avoid a systemic crisis three objectives would be necessary: the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the reforms and will continue to monitor the implementation of the reforms. to address regulatory gaps and to mitigate and correct the fragility of supervisory systems, the commission recommends the establishment of a network of national supervisory authorities and the introduction of a single set of rules to protect depositors, investors and consumers in the european union. the european solution would involve giving colleges of supervisors the power to impose binding rules if the national supervisors cannot reach an agreement. the report also proposes the creation of a european fund pre-financed by financial institutions to protect depositors and to help institutions in the event of their failure to do so, which could cause damage to the system as a whole. the ultimate aim of this report is to establish a future crisis resolution mechanism that reduces the chances of the european taxpayer having to deal with the consequences of a collapse of the financial system.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, in a time of economic and financial crisis the european union should take strong measures at european level by increasing control over banking institutions and financial markets. the creation of four new control bodies could be a viable alternative, ensuring close cooperation with the national supervisory bodies. these would not be bodies responsible for monitoring the whole of their area of competence, but specific financial institutions composed of the highest-level representatives of the national supervisory authorities who will help to harmonise standards and regulation across eu states. in particular, the european banking authority will assess access to, availability of and costs of credit for consumers and small and medium-sized enterprises. at the end of the g20 the idea of taxing the banks, strongly supported by both president barroso and van rompuy, was not even considered. in a europe still exposed to the crisis, joint action is needed to establish common rules at european level.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the european central bank has so far shown that it is a good bank. the fight against inflation has been taken seriously in frankfurt and since the introduction of the euro there has never been a systematic increase in prices above the target. this is due to the high level of professionalism of the ecb's technical staff, as well as the constant exchange with the financial and academic worlds, for effective policy monitoring and the certainty of being always up to date with the state of the art. in addition, the reputation acquired by eurotower, also thanks to the impressive legacy of the bundesbank, has made it possible to contain the extent of the crisis in europe, and to become aware of some signals on which, however, no one had jurisdiction until now. the european central bank is therefore the best candidate to assume a key role in the new european supervisory system. while not exceeding expectations, good work can be expected from those who have so far demonstrated their skills, competence and knowledge.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the eu is creating a framework for safeguarding financial stability. to avert the risk of new and serious financial crises, europe needs an institutional framework to resolve the insolvency of systemically important financial institutions. a new macro-prudential supervisory authority, the european systemic risk board (esrb), and a new micro-prudential supervisory authority, the european system of financial supervision (esfs), will be created, the efficiency of which is guaranteed by the ecb's prestige, as the new esfs will not be able to impose measures or sanctions on member states or financial institutions and its reports will not be binding. consequently, their effectiveness depends on the considerable reputation of the ecb and the recognised competence of its staff. the main purpose of the supervisory architecture is to prevent future dramatic situations such as the crisis we are currently experiencing, as well as to ensure financial stability. the core of the success of the new policy for the regulation and supervision of financial markets will be the interconnection between micro and macro supervision. in this way, the esrb secretariat will play an important role in ensuring an efficient and rapid exchange of the data involved.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the vote in favour is the result of satisfaction with the agreement reached with the council. the creation of a european authority for financial instruments and markets is a very important achievement for the european parliament, it has made a qualitative and competent contribution to the regulation, but it is an achievement of which the ppe group is particularly proud. we have always struggled to close the large regulatory gaps in this area and to correct the fragility of the supervisory systems. the integration of the european systemic risk board with the european supervisory authorities and the allocation of more powers to the new authorities was very important. this will make a decisive contribution to giving these instruments the right community dimension.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the structure of the european production system and its international competitive advantage are closely linked to innovation and human capital in the broad sense. the research and development of new solutions, or new processes for solving problems, is the basis for the well-being and prosperity of european countries in the decades to come. it is not raw materials or low labour costs that are currently making the eu a wealth importer, but the production of ideas, the training of service providers and the ability to be the first to bring useful innovations to the market. it is therefore essential, for our continued presence on the international scene, to stimulate the creation of intellectual property through fair remuneration, secured by a temporary exclusive exploitation right. in particular, this report rightly points the finger at counterfeiting and piracy, proposing measures to combat these two scourges. at the same time, i am in favour of ad hoc measures for the internet and the cultural sector, so as to avoid mass phenomena that are difficult to counteract while promoting virtuous behaviour.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the vote on the gallo report on intellectual property rights in the internal market took account of two complementary rights: the right to intellectual property is a right which is specific to the author and/or publisher of the created good and is more general in that it is a right to knowledge by those to whom the good is intended. the european union cannot be just an internal market, where businesses operate and protect the goods and services they produce, but also a common space of citizenship and freedom, where citizens can express themselves and inform each other, including each other. the creation of an excessive and unjustified and unfair limitation on the free circulation of intellectual creations, which would bend everything to private interests, could compress the common space where the expression of thought takes on the importance of the public good. it is therefore important that intellectual creations be protected, but it is equally important that the means of protecting them should not be excessive, in order to make them fully available in ways and times reasonably short for the benefit of the whole community, starting with the internet.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the gallo report on the protection of intellectual property rights in the internal market broadly incorporates what has already been said in the european commission's previous communication, confirming the need for a two-pronged protection of these rights, on the one hand, and of consumers, on the other. this is an important report, especially for small and mediumsized enterprises, which are very common in my region and are often helpless in the face of infringements of intellectual property rights. i also share the protection that has been sought for the private user, considering 'private copying' as an exception to infringement and supporting information campaigns directed at consumers on the legality or otherwise of products purchased either physically or via the web. in view of the contents and the excellent work done by mrs gallo, i shall vote in favour of this report.

in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i fully support the gallo report on strengthening the enforcement of intellectual property rights and i share the call on the commission to work urgently on a revision of the laws for the protection of ipr applicable to both the internal and external markets. in the age of the digitalisation of our society, it is essential to find legislative and non-legislative measures that ensure a lasting balance between free access to the internet and the fight against counterfeiting and piracy. only in this way can we facilitate the access of european industries to the digital market, without geographical borders, solving those problems of multi-territorial licences that today block both the possibility of our products being sold legally and our consumers in accessing the information necessary for a safe purchase. i fully share the importance, as expressed in the gallo report, of the role of european customs, which must now be able to take concrete action to block goods suspected of infringing ipr, and i therefore ask the commission to work on a customs policy which includes problems relating to property rights and to intensify the debate and negotiations on the acta anti-counterfeiting trade agreements.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, in a global world where the internet is flourishing without control and protection, counterfeiting and piracy are the masters. failure to value intellectual property, a vital asset for businesses, means failing to encourage innovation and growth by ensuring fair remuneration for work done. a separate chapter is counterfeiting of trade marks, which, in addition to harming businesses economically, can also be harmful from the point of view of consumer safety. another good thing is that you can download it for personal use and legally from the internet. it's still a crime to do it for profit. we therefore vote in favour.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of the resolution on the european strategy for the development of mountain, island and sparsely populated regions because i believe it is important to re-launch the theme of territorial cohesion and the harmonious development of all the geographical areas that make up the european union. i believe that only greater coordination and closer cooperation between the european institutions, the member states and local authorities can make geographically or demographically disadvantaged areas truly competitive. it is also necessary to take account of the specificities of each region in order to redistribute resources for regional development in a fair and efficient manner. in particular, the european union must take care of the situation of islands in order to lift them out of the marginal conditions often linked to insularity. to this end, cohesion policy should also make use of other policies which can have a significant impact on the future of these territories: i am referring, for example, to instruments for regulating migration flows which, in islands such as sicily, have a significant impact on the socioeconomic growth of the region.

in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that a specific european strategy for the development of mountain and island areas is needed at eu level. a strategy that takes account of aspects such as the promotion of the economy and of structures, employment policy, the safeguarding of the natural heritage, civil protection, environmental and energy policy. the principle of territorial cohesion is one of the key objectives of the european union introduced by the treaty of lisbon, with the aim of reducing regional disparities and removing natural or geographical obstacles. this requires concrete action and specific development strategies. equal opportunities must be created between these territories and the rest of the european union; one of these could be to promote tourism in mountain regions in a sustainable way, thus creating an important livelihood for the inhabitants of these areas. the madrid declaration of european ministers of 15 april 2010 also stresses the need for more effective coordination of measures implemented in the field of tourism policy and the promotion of a more innovative, sustainable and social tourism in europe.

passivity. the council has repeatedly warned against premature withdrawal of monusco, in order to avoid a vacuum and a possible further deterioration of security in the areas affected by the conflicts. overall, beyond the abuses committed, we can only applaud the way in which the united nations has handled the question of extending the mandate of the un mission in the drc. as you know, when the new mandate was being discussed at the united nations, the drc government insisted on a partial withdrawal, and the security council agreed to reduce the 2,000 peacekeepers in the mission by 30 june 2010, from 21,500 to 19,500 soldiers on the ground, but resisted pressure from kinshasa, which wanted a commitment to further reductions. so in the specific case of today's debate, we believe in which monusco is working and, more than likely, advocate better coordination between the drc authorities and the un. we believe that to end monusco at this time would significantly aggravate the the fight against the illegal exploitation of natural resources, but it is clear that this measure can only be analysed in the light of the effects it has had not only on the financing of rebel troops but also on the recovery of effective control by the authorities or on the socioeconomic well-being of the population.

for the commission, - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, as the president has just said, it is on behalf of the high representative, lady ashton, that i am speaking to your assembly on the european day against the death penalty. as you know, the application of the death penalty in the world presents a picture that is still mixed. for one thing, the vast majority of states are now abolitionist in law or in practice, and it is encouraging to see that the number of states is continuing to grow. we are seeing a very strong trend towards the abolition and restriction of the use of the death penalty in most countries. on the other hand, the number of executions and the way in which the death penalty is applied around the world unfortunately remains alarming: the 5 679 executions reported in 2009 are 5 679 executions too many. and with 58 countries and territories retaining the death penalty, our work is far from over. moreover, we all know that where the death penalty is still in force, there are serious problems with respect to international norms and standards, in particular in limiting the death penalty to the most serious crimes, excluding juvenile offenders from its scope or guaranteeing a fair trial. the conclusion is clear: there is no room for complacency in this matter. that is why we must use all available means, diplomatic and public awareness, in pursuing our objective and why the high representative has made european union action to abolish the death penalty a personal priority. what does that mean in practice? the future european external action service will of course be able to build on the fact that the european union is already the leading institutional actor in support of the fight against the death penalty, but the service will also represent and be an opportunity to better realise our potential. it will strengthen our capacity to speak with one voice, which will give us the opportunity to better mobilise and interconnect all the instruments available at european level in the fight against the death penalty. the european union also continues to strengthen its cooperation with other international organisations and multilateral bodies active in promoting the abolition of the death penalty. the resolution calling for a moratorium on the use of the death penalty, scheduled for the 65th un general assembly this autumn, should reflect progress towards universal abolition. the aim is to reinforce and amplify the trend towards abolition which is being observed in all regions of the world. the close cooperation between the european union and the council of europe is another asset in our fight against the death penalty. in this context, and in a very concrete way, we will join our efforts to encourage belarus to abolish the death penalty, for example by organising joint events in minsk on this world day. ladies and gentlemen, since we fundamentally believe that the abolition of the death penalty is essential to protect human dignity and respect human rights, we oppose the use of the death penalty in all cases and under all circumstances and will continue to call for its universal abolition. universal abolition is and will remain one of the priority objectives of our external action on human rights and i therefore reaffirm here on behalf of lady ashton our determination that the european union will remain at the forefront of the fight for universal abolition of the death penalty.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the cop 10 on biodiversity will be held in japan from 18 to 29 october, and it is important for parliament to know what the council intends to propose in order to protect and guarantee biodiversity. one study found that of 4,000 plants examined, as many as 22 percent were classified as endangered. this means that one in five plants is at risk of extinction and - another worrying fact - many plants that are not yet discovered will also disappear. the same can be said of many animal species. with them, active ingredients in plants, which are essential for industry, which is studying new preparations that may be useful in combating diseases that are currently incurable, risk disappearing. as for animals, with their disappearance, important features for our planet are lost. the european parliament recently approved the union's legislation on this subject in september with a clear vote, which cannot but commit the council to the same line. we must not forget that the fight against poverty and therefore against hunger is also a fight to preserve the wealth of a natural heritage, of a priceless flora and fauna, a wealth which we cannot afford to lose and which we must do everything we can to preserve.
madam president, in 2002 the representatives of governments around the world committed themselves to significantly reducing biodiversity loss by 2010. this objective, although it has been repeated and reiterated in various international fora, has unfortunately not been achieved. the rate of this loss on the planet has accelerated at least 100 times faster than natural cycles and has reached unprecedented levels in the last 50 years. in europe, one in six mammals is at risk of extinction, and when one species disappears, it can create a domino effect on all the others. in the last 30 years, at least 30 percent of all animal and plant species on the planet have been lost. without ambitious targets to be adopted immediately, biodiversity loss - as has been said many times - will cost europe €1.1 trillion by 2050, as the wwf also states. so, as pointed out in the question by mrs striffler, the protection of biodiversity is an important element of the millennium development goals and the europe 2020 strategy. fostering biodiversity is like raising the arrows of our bow in the fight against extreme poverty and hunger, by implementing environmental sustainability policies that keep our planet rich and fertile. we need a new strategic vision and new targets that take account of the constant loss of species and reflect the importance we attach to this problem.
