in writing. i believe that the recent financial and economic crisis, the biggest recession since the great depression, has highlighted the need for a major overhaul of the current basel ii regulatory framework. i would remind you that the basle ii agreement defines the criteria for access to credit, encouraging banks to assess objectively the creditworthiness of a firm, taking into account the risks associated with their possible insolvency, guarantees and exposure at the time of bankruptcy. these criteria, although aimed at improving the competitiveness of enterprises and strengthening the soundness of the financial system, are excessively punitive towards small and medium-sized enterprises, the engine of the union's economy. in practice, the application of the agreement, because of the lower financial strength of european firms, often results in less access to credit and higher interest rates. while i welcome the efforts made by the basle committee to update the overall regulatory framework, i am deeply concerned about the shortcomings that have emerged in the negotiation process and therefore agree that parliament should be more closely involved in the negotiations in order to make the necessary changes so that european industry and the european economy are not disadvantaged.
in writing. a new stability pact for europe necessarily passes through the banking system, which is the other end of the spectrum of the use of those own resources which are the beating heart of the european economy. in other words, the debt that the member states of the european union accumulate over time to produce national wealth and distribute it to their citizens is financed and managed by the banks, which should then be able to make a profit from it. while it is true that the member states will still need a long time to adjust to the standardisation of their financial laws and to achieve an appropriate level of uniformity within their tax systems, the establishment of adequate liquidity margins and the requirement of reliable leverage effects to guarantee the amount of savings and its development over time is necessary to ensure that a proper response to the crisis can be found in the short term. the own resources which the european union will have increasingly at its disposal will ensure that the management of the union's resources is less and less geared to containing systemic risks and more and more to creating a set of incentives for the benefit of national economies, not only jealously guarded within their own borders but integrated to optimise the use of their comparative advantages.

in writing. the recent disaster in the gulf of mexico, which caused the spill of millions of barrels of oil, has brought the world's attention back to a key issue for the european union. the experience has shown that in offshore oil production, strict measures must be taken to ensure that the environment is adequately protected. however, europe must remain competitive in this sector and continue to explore for gas to diversify its energy needs. i therefore support the adoption of new safety principles and the application of strict and rigorous common standards and the establishment of solidarity funds to compensate victims in the event of any damage. the urgency of these measures is also dictated by the geomorphological nature of some of our seas, such as the mediterranean sea and the current drilling operations on its libyan and egyptian coasts. if oil were to leak, we would be faced with an environmental disaster that would be difficult to repair, with very serious consequences for the economy and the environment of many european countries. finally, i do not support the proposal for a moratorium because i believe that agreements with third countries and their oil companies are more effective. this would make it easier to export safety standards and to invest in prevention and technological research.

the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, lady ashton, on the financial regulation applicable to the european external action service, or on the basic principles and rules governing the community budget of the new diplomatic service created by the treaty of lisbon and which will include officials from the council, the commission and the national diplomatic services, with the task of representing the european union in all foreign policy matters, i think that a very good job has been done. the service, as originally structured, however, presented a number of dangers which were attributable to its decentralised and complex structure, with branches all over the world. in particular, the responsibility of financial actors managing budgets of hundreds of millions of euros was unclear and risked contributing to the increase in fraud and corruption affecting the community budget. although the treaty of lisbon greatly extends the powers of the european parliament and identifies it as the only institution representing the european citizens, the debate on the establishment of the new external action service was initially monopolized by the commission and the council, which tried in every way to structure it according to an intergovernmental logic and contrary to the community method. after lengthy consultations with the belgian presidency and the european commission, an agreement was reached which, despite the initial approach, sees the role of parliament strengthened and rightly put it at the centre of the european debate. the main points are: the commission will provide, in a working document attached to the draft budget, a comprehensive presentation including all operational administrative expenditure relating to the union's external action, including the common foreign and security policy and the european security and defence policy; article 1, which lists all the institutions of the european union, the responsibility reports are annexed to the annual activity reports of the director-general of the commission; the presence of the head of delegation at meetings of the relevant parliamentary committees accompanied by the director-general; the presence of a common auditor and accountant for the office and the european commission, with an audit clause in 2013; the commitment of the member states to fully support the union in pursuing all responsibilities of temporary staff of the european external action service. we must then discuss some important matters which will be taken up again when the financial regulation is revised every three years. these are the discharge to the institutions and the integration of the european social fund into the general budget. the negotiations have been a success, especially for parliament, whose central role has been highly valued. the fact that we have listed all the institutions which means that discharge for the other institutions is only a matter of time and the fact that we have a single auditor and accountant for both institutions is a good thing. i thank you all for your work.
the rapporteur. - mr president, lady ashton, commissioners, ladies and gentlemen, parliament approves the establishment of a new section of the budget devoted to the eeas and the allocation of additional resources for staff. this position is dictated by the desire to allow the creation of the office, which europe needs and urgently needs, but it does not of course imply a renunciation of the role of the budgetary authority in the debate on the nature of the structure that will deal with crisis management and the priorities of staff policy, as demonstrated by the reservation we established in the 2011 budget. the regulations we are going to adopt reinforce the results of the madrid agreement, in some cases by making further progress, for which i would like to thank my colleagues rapkay, grässle and rivellini. i also thank them for their availability and openness to the debate between catherine ashton and paul christophersen. the staff regulations ensure that all officials of the office have the same rights and duties, regardless of their origin, and commit the high representative to ensuring geographical and gender balance. this is a binding wording, which parliament will ensure is respected, and which at the same time avoids the use of quotas which would be inapplicable and wrong. the financial regulation ensures a sound system of controls and brings the office closer to the commission. let me say with satisfaction that the success of the establishment of specific budget lines for the main csdp missions is a major step forward in parliament's ability to exercise control over the common foreign and security policy. the vote tomorrow will therefore result in a stronger, more community-wide external action service, subject to greater parliamentary scrutiny. we will exercise this scrutiny rigorously and demandingly, but with responsibility and a constructive spirit, determined to help the high representative in his titanic effort to equip europe with a genuine foreign policy in the service of its values and interests.
on behalf of the efd group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, in defining the structure of the new diplomatic service, we must not repeat the mistakes of the past but aim at a lean, inexpensive and above all efficient staff. an instrument of european policy - i repeat, european - must not select its officials on the basis of their geographical origin or gender but on the basis of their quality. i agree that the member states should be represented in the new service and that a large female component would be appropriate. but this cannot be done at the expense of the criteria of merit and professional excellence. what we must do instead is to ensure a rigorous and equal access to careers for all, without discrimination. for training, there are structures, such as the european university institute in florence, which have the expertise to ensure excellent training. it seems to me therefore inappropriate and costly to think of building a european diplomatic academy from scratch.
mr president, after the adoption of the council decision on the organisation and functioning of the european external action service, we are called upon today to put that same determination into practice by amending the financial regulation and the staff regulations of officials of the union. i would like to draw attention to one aspect of the report which has involved difficult negotiations: the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. some of my colleagues would have preferred different criteria for the selection of officials, based on origin and nationality. these proposals were avoided by balanced compromise amendments which took account of the geographical and gender balance without imposing selective criteria on a national basis. the choice of quotas on a national basis would not have been a suitable and desirable solution. after more than 50 years of european integration, the first real diplomatic corps of the union is now being created, a diplomatic corps which must be able to develop a common foreign policy and serve the union's interests on an international scale. in order to fulfil this task, it is essential that officials represent the union and not the member states of which they are nationals or have been diplomatic officials. that is the line taken yesterday in the legal affairs committee in adopting the rapkay report and it is the line i hope will continue to be followed in the vote in plenary.
high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy/vice-president of the commission. − madam president, very briefly from the other side of the chamber – and i hope i have sat for the right number of minutes – i would again like to thank the honourable members very much for a debate which i have listened to with great interest. i take away with me the strength of feeling on geographical and gender balance within the context of a service that is truly european, appointed on merit. i take away with me the need for people to see our working crisis management enhanced and to see it properly reflected in the european service. i take away with me what i have described as a ‘silver thread’ of human rights that must run through everything that we do in the service; and i take away, again, the reminder of the economic backdrop against which i am pulling this service together, and the desire that honourable members have to see an efficient service that uses resources properly and effectively. most of all, after what has been a long journey of many months, i take away the desire of this house to see the service come into being, to reflect the needs of the constituents you represent and to be a service that will serve them well. it is my promise to you to try and reflect that in everything that the service does.

in writing. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation establishing a control and enforcement framework applicable in the area of the convention on future multilateral cooperation in the north-east atlantic fisheries, to which the european union is a contracting party, because i believe that it is necessary to transpose this regime into eu law. in 2006, neafc adopted a new regime to improve the monitoring and implementation of its recommendations, and both the eu and the european parliament subsequently expressed their full support for the adoption of the recommendations. in particular, strong support was given to the new provisions for a system of control by the port state, which allows european ports to be closed to landings and transhipments of frozen fish whose legality has not been verified by the authorities of the same state. finally, these are a series of recommendations which adapt the existing system to the present needs and which i therefore believe should be transposed quickly.

in writing. − this proposal updates the eu rules implementing the control and enforcement regime adopted by the commission for fisheries in the northwest atlantic a new procedure is adopted with the aim of improving the monitoring and implementation of fisheries recommendations and, above all, promoting compliance by non-contracting parties' vessels. in addition, a new port state control system is introduced, allowing european ports to be closed to landings of frozen fish whose legality has not been verified by the flag state of the foreign vessel. new measures are introduced to control vessels engaged in illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing. my vote in favour is mainly motivated by the need to prevent, deter and eliminate illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing.

in writing. - madam president, the europe 2020 strategy proposes to raise the employment rate of people aged 20-64 to 75% and to reduce the number of people at risk of poverty. to achieve these objectives, action should also be taken on all forms of precarious employment which include unwritten employment contracts, working hours of less than 10 hours per week and short-term fixed-term contracts. this is not to mention jobs where the minimum health and safety requirements are ignored, resulting in a high rate of accidents and a greater risk of exposure to diseases and various hazards. these forms of contract, as well as all the risks attached to them, are often aimed at women, penalized on the basis of their sex, age, having a family or being immigrants. the european union should take legislative action to ensure gender equality and reduce gender segregation in the labour market. the member states should in turn increase checks in order to reduce the number of abuses against women, combat undeclared work and take deterrent action against employers.
in writing. - i congratulate the rapporteur on drawing attention to an aspect of the world of work which still causes too many gender differences. the economic and financial crisis has undoubtedly worsened the situation of precarious workers, especially women, who bear the brunt of the burden of precariousness. this is confirmed by recent figures, which show that in 55% of firms only women have a parttime contract. it is also estimated that 31.5% of women have part-time work compared to 8.3% of men and that precarious work leads to a higher rate of accidents and a higher risk of illness and exposure to risks. in short, a situation of inequality which the european union cannot ignore. i voted in favour because i share the need to combat this phenomenon and to urge the member states and the social partners to bring legislation and contractual rules into substantial alignment. i also hope that the commission and the member states will carry out more checks on the minimum health and safety requirements at the workplace. there is still a lot to be done to ensure women's fair access to the world of work.
in writing. - within the european union, a purely descriptive term such as 'precarious workers' still contains two forms of discrimination, both very serious. the first concerns the problem of women's work, which was also tackled in this session from a modern and sustainable perspective in another dossier. the second concerns the dualism in the labour market of many member states between workers enjoying rights and protections on the one hand and workers who are at the mercy of phenomena usually beyond their control on the other. objectively looking at the data, it seems increasingly clear that in the future, wage labour will also involve greater risk taking than has been the case so far. however, this development must be managed to avoid speculation to the detriment of the weaker parties to the contract, and in particular those who are in a disadvantaged situation. the european institutions have a duty to avoid discrimination and to allow everyone to pursue his or her professional goals freely, in accordance with his or her abilities, attitudes and inclinations. the committee takes this opportunity to recall that further research on the precarious position of women would be useful in planning interventions aimed at removing obstacles without being too invasive.

madam president, mr council representative, mr commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i would first of all like to thank my colleague, mrs sidonia elżbieta jdrzejewska, and the other members for the excellent work they have done in recent months, which has led to the establishment of the position on the 2011 budget, first by the committee and then by parliament. in my view, the starting point on which european budgetary action should be based is the concept of european added value, according to which - as is well known - european spending must generate clear and visible benefits for the union and its citizens. it is in this context that it should be stressed that the introduction of new policies and the strengthening of the union's already recognised powers, such as the results of the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, have made the need for an adequate budget more evident than ever. i therefore believe that the european budget must be kept at a size which is suitable for achieving results which cannot be achieved by any other expenditure at national or local level. this is particularly true at a time of crisis such as the present, when the member states are engaged in the difficult task of controlling expenditure and balancing their budgets, and when the committee on budgets has given full proof of a careful and responsible policy by respecting the limits of the multiannual financial framework for the first time in 20 years. the european parliament decided to align itself in many respects with the commission's initial position, and also provided for some increases to finance its priorities proposed since march 2010 such as youth, mobility, research and innovation. the council's proposed cuts, often indiscriminate, and in key budget lines, such as clearance of accounts, were therefore eliminated, making it clear that there were no clear and reasoned policy choices behind the proposal. i also believe that the cap budget should be maintained at its current level, especially in view of the forthcoming revision of the common agricultural policy after 2013, which will require an appropriate level of funding and therefore in line with the current budget.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the outcome of this budgetary procedure is of great importance, not only because it is the first budget of lisbon, with a new procedure and new tasks for the eu, but also because it comes at a crucial moment for the future of europe, which is in a state of serious crisis. many governments, faced with the crisis, are thinking of a model of economic governance based entirely on stability mechanisms, and therefore on cuts, in national budgets and perhaps even in the european budget. we believe, on the contrary, that a stronger european budget, backed by own resources and also by a financial transaction tax, is a prerequisite for effective european economic governance and for greater rigour at the level of national budgets. we must therefore decide which way to go, and that is why the amendments which the council representative has found inappropriate are of great importance. but of course the bigger game is played on numbers: i would urge the council to take a decision on this, because it cannot demand strict respect for the margins and at the same time expect parliament not to give priority to its own priorities. the treaty of lisbon is clear: the council has primacy over the amount of spending, parliament has the final say over the quality of spending. i am thinking of heading 4, we are not against an increase in resources for the cfsp or for the ici+, but we do not want this to be at the expense of our priorities, first of all palestine and development cooperation. the council therefore has three options: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, parliament is about to vote on the first budget of the lisbon era. this powerful instrument which the treaty puts at our disposal is at odds with the worst economic situation the european continent has experienced since 1929. we must ensure that this serious economic crisis does not turn into an even more serious political crisis. if the trilogue fails and the 2011 budget becomes twelve-tenths of the 2010 budget, the distribution and operation of the structural funds would be very difficult, as would the european external action service, which might not even be able to start. all of this should make us think. we welcome the important work of the rapporteur, mrs jędrzejewska, whom we thank also for her efforts to focus the resources of the european union on young people, research and innovation. but we must never forget how important it is that we, as the first, set an example of sound and moderate management of our finances, avoiding as much waste as possible and perhaps even structural duplication, which our citizens would not understand and which would certainly not be to the advantage of the future of europe.

member of the commission. − mr president, to answer mr kelly first, i would like to say that, in general, for countries which have a better system for controlling compliance and have all the instruments at their disposal, it is easier to absorb the money. this is a general rule. generally speaking, i have to admit that mediterranean countries – the countries of the south – have bigger problems. greece has a special problem. we have to be very sure that we can help everybody in order to have better absorption. it is our plan to make an effort to simplify the rules for absorption. that is why we will have a funding line in the framework of our cfp reform which will be much easier for the member states to absorb. referring to mr tsoukalas’s question about the mediterranean regulation, we have decided that this mediterranean regulation has to be implemented. we have had to implement this regulation since 1 june, and there is no way back. if we were to amend this regulation, we would need two or three years without any control and compliance system, so we are going to implement this regulation. i have already cooperated with the greek authorities. i have explained to them that they have to implement this regulation without any further delay. that means of course that all the provisions about special types of gear that are very heavy for the environment have to be met. it also means that we are going to exhaust the margins from our fund possibilities to give them funding in order to compensate them. this is something i would like to say referring to boat seines, to trawlers and to all types of gear: they have to give us a good example of compliance. we will do our best in order to exhaust our funding margins to make it possible for them to have better gear and to improve the selectivity of their gear.

interests are protected. this is a phenomenon which places small and mediumsized enterprises in extreme difficulty, often at risk of closing down their activities because they cannot survive because the union's economy. when the legislation we are about to adopt is fully in force, some eur 180 billion will be put back into circulation, which will mean encouraging growth and innovation initiatives for small and mediumsized enterprises. as you know, access to credit is the key to the development and growth of the competitiveness of our enterprises. i therefore believe that to support this the treasuries of the companies. these rules will also have the effect of giving public authorities that pay late a strong incentive to update their management methods as well. in fact, when a public body purchases goods or services, it has already entered in the budget the appropriations for that expenditure. so it should not be difficult to pay creditors on time. it should also be noted that shorter payment terms will result in savings for public administrations. another important element of the agreement is that the companies themselves will have to pay their invoices unless different agreements between the parties are reached which are not unfair to the creditor within 60 days. in conclusion, let me remind you that member states remain free to maintain or adopt provisions more favourable to creditors than those necessary to comply with the directive. consequently, this legislation does not prevent member states from adopting shorter payment periods or more severe penalties. member of the commission. − madam president, i should like to thank very much those who spoke. you gave a good coverage of all the issues that we are facing. before i get into answers, just let me say the following. when i arrived in the villages affected yesterday, the thought i had in my mind was: thank god it happened during the day, because if that accident had happened during the night many more people would have died. actually from a distance the houses look like somebody has painted half of them in red. obviously this goes above the level where there are beds in which women, men, kids, elderly people sleep. when we are faced with something like this, it is really appropriate to have a thoughtful discussion and to make sure that we draw lessons from it. then we can have a feedback into preparedness, prevention and response in the case of any future disaster. so i take the comments that have been made here in this chamber in this respect very seriously. let me try to respond to them. first, on the question of legislation and the role of the commission. my exact wording was that, from the first analysis we have carried out, it does appear that we have the appropriate legislation in place and that, where we are still lacking sufficient action, this lies in the implementation of that legislation. i am emphasising the words ‘first analysis’ and in my conclusion i did stress that we would look into whether we have gaps in the legislation. again, based on what we have in front of us in this case and in many others, the focus really has to be on implementing the legislation we have rather than on saying: ‘oh well, let us go out and write another piece of paper and stick it on top of many other pieces of paper’, when we know that the critical issue is implementation. when we talk about what we might specifically be looking into from a legislative point of view, there are two specific issues at this point, though there may be more when we finish taking stock. the first one is on the question of classification of the red mud as hazardous or not. we do not say that in every case when we have red mud it is not hazardous. it may be hazardous if there is a high content of heavy metals, and if specific technical qualifications are met. in other words there could be cases when red mud is classified as hazardous. at this moment of time, on the basis of the information that was provided by the hungarian authorities, we can say that, on the basis of their information, this red mud is not hazardous, but obviously we need to carry out a more thorough analysis. then the question would be how we deal with an issue like this and whether there is a need to tighten up the definition of hazardous waste. that i cannot answer today, but i can assure you that it will be looked into. the second legislative issue that is very important is the question of liability that has been raised by a number of speakers. do we have in the liability directive enough teeth to bite when it comes down to the implementation of the ‘polluter pays’ principle? i said at the very beginning that this is an area where the commission is already initiating work to assess whether there is a need for tighter regulation of how companies act in terms of having the means to meet their obligations as polluters. that again would be work we will follow up very thoroughly. the second set of questions concerns financing. what can we do? hungary has dedicated structural funds and rural development funds at its disposal. we know from experience that, in the process of implementing programmes, there is always some room for manoeuvre. basically no country has ever achieved 100% utilisation of structural funds, and priorities shift over time. therefore it is possible for hungary, if the government judges this a very high priority, to use structural funds or rural development funds for environmental monitoring for treatment facilities, for the rehabilitation of damaged infrastructures and the rehabilitation of agricultural land. they can also be used for changing land use, because it may not be possible for the land i saw to be quickly rehabilitated for its conventional agricultural use, but it may be possible to use it for energy crops which do not need to meet the same test in terms of dangerous materials. we also had quite different views on the solidarity fund. i would say two things here. one is that i agree that it is the responsibility of the polluter to pay, but at the same time, when communities are hit by a disaster of this nature, it is a matter of european solidarity and compassion to be able to give them a hand at this moment, because by the time that the liabilities of the company are met, months and months will have passed. i find myself in an awkward situation, as commissioner in charge of humanitarian aid and disaster response, when i can help the victims of the floods in pakistan quickly, but there is nothing in my hands as an instrument to help the victims of this disaster. this summer when we had floods in romania and moldova, i could very quickly provide funding to moldova, but i could not do anything for the victims of the floods in romania – and i am talking not just about myself, i am talking about us as european citizens. this is a question to be looked into to see whether indeed, with the increase in disasters both at home and abroad, we should have in our hands an instrument that allows us to show compassion to our citizens. and by the way, our citizens are perplexed as to why we can help pakistan when we cannot help ajka. there have been questions that were directed to the role of the commission. let me make this very clear. the inspections and the monitoring are a member state responsibility. we do not have a mandate in the commission to do it. what we do try to do – through training activities, awareness raising, lessons learnt – is to bring all member states up to speed in terms of their capacity to monitor and inspect. one of the speakers here said there are clearly institutional shortages in this area. we can help with training, but we do not have a mandate to be inspectors and to substitute for national authorities. i do not mean that we should never have this mandate, but we do not have it today and, frankly, i think it is much more important for the national authorities to be better equipped to perform their duties than for more and more layers of inspection to be built up. make sure that the people who do the job are equipped to do that job. there have been questions relating to the recycling of red sludge. the directive does provide for incentives for research, and our environmental legislation encourages the transition to the best available technology. specifically for this installation, it should be in compliance with the highest standards by 2012. of course, it is terrible that the disaster happened in 2010. obviously – and i will finish with this point because i am well over my time – we have to learn from this case and raise our alert level as regards other places in europe that could potentially be a source of danger in the future. for a hazard not to turn into a catastrophe, the key is in monitoring, preparedness and prevention, and i could not agree more with those speakers who have hammered on this point. we do have a policy on preparedness and prevention and again, as is the case with the legislation we discussed, the critical issue is for this policy to be turned into reality in our member states. for our part, we will bring you a proposal, a communication to strengthen the eu’s disaster response capacity, and we will come back to you with the lessons learnt from this disaster.

in writing. − in any democratic system, parliamentary scrutiny of the work of the executive is a fundamental point, as is close communication between the government and the representatives of the citizens. this interinstitutional agreement between parliament and the commission satisfies, as far as possible for a complex and constantly evolving system such as the community system, certain legitimate demands of our assembly to the european commission. it is therefore right that the control of our assembly should be facilitated in relation to the commission, a technical body which cannot be the political brain of an entire continent and which must be held to account as much as possible for the content, reasons and methods of its action. it is also positive that efforts are being made to emphasise the need for an even greater presence of the commission in parliament's proceedings, particularly in plenary sessions, in order to respond to the requests of the representatives of the european citizens and to report promptly on the commission's position on topical political, economic, social and international issues. it is clear that if the eu is to move towards a democratic set-up, unlike today, the relationship between the commission and parliament will have to be further intensified and improved. my vote on mr rangel's report is in favour.
in writing. − the eu's constitutional architecture is increasingly taking the form of a nation state. the european union is not a political union, but a political union of the peoples of europe. it is from this that, in my view, the relationship between the commission and parliament is shaped, in the way that has already been tried and tested for decades, if not centuries, in each of the member states. in particular, the parliament's monitoring and investigation role is to be appreciated, as it is aimed at reducing the so-called democratic deficit and making relations between citizens and the commission more transparent.
in writing. − before the treaty of lisbon and the new legal basis of article 295 tfeu, the treaties did not explicitly encourage the institutions of the european union to conclude interinstitutional agreements. such agreements cannot alter the provisions of primary law but often clarify them. i am convinced that this project strictly reflects the institutional balance established by the lisbon treaty. i give my consent because this agreement represents a clear and significant improvement in relations with the commission. as with all agreements, the final text tends to be a compromise between the two parties; however, this final compromise is a balanced approach and a reasonable and consistent application of the treaty of lisbon.
in writing. - with this agreement, parliament has become 'better' and stronger and the democratisation of the european union has been strengthened. the adoption of this report is a strong signal of the desire to consolidate the principle of the separation of powers. the framework agreement is of great importance, since it defines the relations between parliament and the commission at a time when parliament has acquired greater powers, especially in the legislative process, being at the same level as the council. in fact, despite the treaties and the additional and implementing protocols, supplementary legislation was needed to specify and define certain matters better. in particular, i welcome the fact that the framework agreement clarifies the points relating to the political responsibility of both institutions, the circulation of information, external relations, enlargement and international agreements, the implementation of the budget, the commission's political and legislative programme and the union's multiannual programme, the commission's legislative competence and the implementation of specific powers, the monitoring of the application of community law and the commission's participation in parliamentary work.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of the report by mr gräßle and mr rivellini, on the financial regulation applicable to the general budget of the european communities, concerning the european external action service (eeas), because i believe that the promotion of financial integrity is important in ensuring fairness and transparency in the management of the institutions. the creation of this new diplomatic service, provided for by the lisbon treaty, is a major step forward for the european union, which will finally have a single diplomatic corps, with the task of facilitating action to make the union's external relations more coherent, secure and efficient. finally, i would like to stress that the european external action service will manage its own administrative budget autonomously and will also be responsible for those parts of the operational budget which fall within its mandate.
in writing. − the european external action service (eeas) will manage its own administrative budget autonomously and be responsible for it. in fact, when the new service is created and, in particular, when the financial provisions applicable to it are established, it is necessary to provide for the appropriate economic guarantees from the outset. to promote the financial integrity of the union, it is therefore important to ensure that the various services responsible for the supervision of monetary aspects, especially at delegation level, can easily interact with each other. by strengthening these guarantees, it is hoped that the confidence of european citizens in the union's institutions will be increased. the structural improvements presented in the proposal are therefore intended to assert the financial integrity necessary to ensure that the eeas can be trusted to operate in a correct and unimpaired manner.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the european parliament's motion for a resolution on the council's position on draft amending budget no 3/2010 of the european union for the financial year 2010, section iii - commission, allocates new resources to finance the accompanying measures in the banana sector for the acp countries (africa, caribbean and pacific). the commission proposal, which was drawn up without involving any branch of the budgetary authority, provides for eur 75 million in commitment appropriations to be entered in the reserve pending the adoption of the regulatory amendments to the regulation. i would point out that parliament and the council have not reached agreement on this. parliament had thought of using the flexibility instrument, which is ideal for dealing with similar situations, since these are funds that are ready to be mobilised and have a legal basis. the council, on the other hand, had a different idea, due to the unwillingness of the member states to use the flexibility instrument, which has the consequence of increasing their contributions. and for the reasons i have just given, the committee on budgets has noted the impossibility of reaching an agreement on the 2010 budget.
in writing. for the first time since the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, the european budget is adopted in a single reading. for the first time, this parliament has greater decisionmaking power vis-à-vis the council. this increased strength must, however, be accompanied by a high sense of responsibility and realism imposed by a persistent economic crisis. the committee on budgets has given a clear signal in this respect, by deciding to respect the margins imposed by the current financial framework and by pursuing a policy of rigour based on priorities to boost growth in favour of research, innovation and young people. i welcome the decision of this house to follow the instructions of the committee on budgets and the member states, which are often forced into debt as a result of excessive advances from the community treasury. the union budget must, however, be reconsidered in the light of the new competences resulting from lisbon and the need for own resources, issues which require firmness in the conciliation process, in order to give adequate financial support to an ambitious project such as the eu 2020 strategy.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of the draft budget because i approve of its line and its content. i agree with the reinstatement of the ceilings in relation to the cuts made by the council. i think this vote is extremely important and i welcome the position taken by parliament in asserting the new prerogatives. the new budgetary procedure introduced by the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon enables parliament to assert its weight and powers vis-à-vis the council by advocating a strong and ambitious budget, which is at the same time rigid, in the knowledge that to revive the european union's economy, which has been severely affected by the recent economic and financial crisis, major investments are needed in key areas such as research and technological innovation.
in writing. - mr president, unfortunately in europe the birth rate varies from country to country, often depending not only on the guarantee of protection of rights but also on the social services available to working mothers, such as day nurseries. there is still a lot to be done to reconcile work and family life. the current system of maternity protection in italy is overall in line with the new parameters proposed in the directive, not only as regards the number of weeks of compulsory maternity leave but also as regards the payment of an allowance equal to 100% of the salary for the period of absence. it is significant that the directive clearly introduces paternity leave: the commission has also proposed that the member states should be able to adopt the same rules for the application of the principle of equal treatment for men and women.
in writing. - there is no doubt that many member states still have very low birth rates. the institutions must therefore encourage births by means of an appropriate family support policy. the report by mrs estrela is in that direction and that is why i voted in favour. i believe it is right that maternity rights should be harmonised between the member states (they always take the health of new mothers and newborn babies into account first) in order to avoid discrepancies and a loss of competitiveness vis-à-vis those states which have already adopted advanced measures to protect maternity. in this respect, i welcome the proposal to extend maternity leave to 18 weeks in all eu countries, which is already in force in several member states: in my country, for example, it's 21 and a half weeks. finally, i believe it is essential to guarantee the right to return to the same job or to be assigned an equivalent job.
in writing. - equality between men and women is often a slogan, an empty claim to rights not always accompanied by assumptions of responsibility and sound arguments. this proposal for a directive, on the other hand, strikes the right balance between the biological role of women and the rights which derive from it for those who play it to the full. with demographic issues increasingly an emergency, and the economy requiring ever higher female employment rates, these measures provide a common sense response. the recognition of equality is complete when certain rights are extended to the father, to distribute family responsibilities in the most appropriate way, and flexibility of organization is left to each family.
in writing. − the vote on the legislative resolution amending directive 92/85/eec was conducted not only in support of new and improved measures for the safety and health at work of pregnant workers, workers who have recently given birth or are breastfeeding, but also, more generally, in support of new measures to promote reconciliation between work and family life. although the italian system is more innovative, the increase in maternity leave weeks at european level represents a strong increase in family care for the newborn. the support for paternity leave is also in this direction, although compulsory leave is perhaps not the most appropriate way of pursuing the right objective of greater effective presence of both parents at the most demanding moments for the new family unit and of greater awareness and presence of the father. the support, in addition to extending the rights of adopted children, allows a strengthening, and we hope a simplification, of the adoption process. finally, it is important to note that, with a view to achieving a better balance between work and family life, it is important to have supported the call on the member states to encourage the strengthening of childcare services with childcare facilities for children up to the age of compulsory schooling.
in writing. - mr president, the european union's social agenda sets as one of its priorities the need to promote all policies aimed at promoting the reconciliation of professional, private and family life, whether they are aimed at women or men. a better balance between work and family life is one of the six priority areas of action in the roadmap for equality between women and men for 2006-2010. improving these provisions is therefore an integral part of european policy in response to the recent sharp demographic decline. maternity and paternity are certainly fundamental rights which are indispensable for social balance. it is therefore desirable that the revision of the directive in question should benefit both working women and men who wish to take on family responsibilities. the principle of equal treatment must be respected in order to achieve a better balance between the protection of health and safety. these and other factors convince me to support the requirement, if necessary, to leave member states wide margins of flexibility in setting the rules on leave, but only for reasons of economic sustainability, to cover the additional costs that arise from it.
in writing. i am opposed to the proposal to increase maternity leave to 20 weeks with 100% pay. the adoption of this system would have major consequences for the budgets of states and companies; for france, the additional annual cost would be €1.3 billion, an unbearable financial burden in a time of budgetary constraints. if this is still a good idea, the consequences for women's employment may be negative. this should not be a setback for women. the return to employment of women after pregnancy and the access to employment of young women are likely to be severely affected by this measure. on the contrary, the proposal for a maximum of 18 weeks was a means of social justice. i call for the implementation of innovative ideas on childcare and reconciling private and family life as soon as possible, so that mothers and fathers can play their full role as parents.

in writing. − today's vote encourages working women to become mothers, marking an important step towards increasing protection that will help millions of european women better reconcile their roles as mothers and workers. economic interests did not prevail: today, a path is being set up to meet the needs of new families. the outcome of the vote looks to a society that puts growth, training and education at the centre of political action. i think that the fears that the extension of maternity leave from 14 to 20 weeks with full pay may penalise women are unfounded: it is our duty to protect the most vulnerable workers, guaranteeing their right to stay at home with their children. today's victory in parliament is also a personal satisfaction for the efforts made in person to ensure that every woman who is a midwife does not have to do heavy or dangerous work, by exempting her from overtime and night work. the ball now goes to the member states, from whom i hope the greatest commitment. today's decision by the european parliament shows that it no longer wants women at a crossroads, but only free women who are aware of their role in our society.
in writing. - in an ageing europe, policies that favour women who choose to have children are essential. today, with fragmented legislation, there are too many differences between member states in support for motherhood, which prevent many women from becoming mothers. this directive sets a minimum of 20 weeks of maternity leave, of which at least six weeks are fully paid. it is clear that in countries such as italy this rule is superfluous, as the period of full pay is far beyond the minimum limit set by the directive and the periods of time for women to take time off work for reasons related to childcare are extended until they are eight years old. but for other countries, it means finally laying the groundwork for a dignified motherhood. the proposal also provides that fathers may also have two weeks of paid leave to be able to be close to their wives in the period immediately after childbirth.
in writing. - mr president, compliance with contractual obligations in commercial transactions, whether by public or private administrations, is not only a matter of civility but also of responsibility towards a series of negative conditions which could be detrimental to lending enterprises, especially smes. the fact that these companies can count on being paid on time means that they can enjoy stability, growth, job creation and investment. unfortunately, according to the european commission, late payment is a frequent occurrence in europe, damaging competitiveness. it is mainly the public administrations that create difficulties, often because of a mismanagement of their budgets and cash flows, or because of an overly bureaucratic process of the administrative machinery. sometimes, however, it is decided to operate on the basis of new expenditure prospects, without taking into account commitments already made and to be honoured within the contractual deadlines. i therefore believe that it is necessary to take measures to fill the gaps in the previous directive 35/2000/ec, thus seeking to discourage the phenomenon of late payment by providing for measures that induce debtors not to pay late and for measures that allow creditors to exercise their rights fully and effectively in the event of late payment.
in writing. - mr president, commissioner tajani, ladies and gentlemen, by adopting the new directive on late payment, a measure which represents a concrete support for businesses and in particular small and mediumsized enterprises, the european parliament is making a decisive contribution to the benefit of citizens and the european production system. the revision of the directive establishes certain payment deadlines and appropriate penalties to encourage timely payments within the union, both by public administrations and private individuals. it is estimated that this measure should put some 180 billion euros of liquidity back into circulation in the economy: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to finance the necessary measures. the problem of late payments is particularly acute in italy, where it takes public administrations an average of 128 days to make payments, compared with a european average of 67 days. therefore, the negative effects of late payment in commercial transactions are considerable. i hope that this directive will be transposed into national law as soon as possible, thus removing one of the greatest obstacles to the development of the european internal market.
in writing. - after months of postponement, we have finally reached the vote on the report, which is a real breath of fresh air for the future of our businesses. the problem of late payments is a phenomenon which, especially in italy, has brought tens of thousands of businesses to their knees, costing the italian economic system something like 30 billion euros, according to the calculations made by trade associations. i am not going to go into the details of the national situations, but i am voting for the report, which sets out once and for all certain rules for both public and private operators. the economic crisis has already caused the failure and closure of factories, companies and business activities in dramatic numbers. europe can really help with this measure many productive entities which, because of the crisis, are living in permanent asphyxiation of bank credit, and which may already be navigating in bad waters because of credits to be collected that were late in arriving. when this directive is implemented, at least it will prevent many cases where companies are left to die of credit by other operators, public or private.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because i believe it is of the utmost importance to take all possible measures to strengthen the competitiveness of smes. the fight against late payment in commercial transactions, which is an unacceptable abuse, must be pursued, especially at a time of economic recession such as the one we are experiencing. the negative effects of late payment are considerable, representing a high cost for lending enterprises, reducing cash flows and investment opportunities and undermining the competitiveness of smes. this directive rightly provides for measures to discourage debtors from paying late, measures to enable creditors to exercise their rights and also defines certain and precise rules, such as the moratorium, the compensation for recovery costs and the thirty-day time limit, subject to specific exceptions, for the payment of debts, which oblige and discourage public administrations from engaging in behaviour that may have a negative impact on smes, undermining the credibility of the policies adopted. finally, swift payments are a necessary and preliminary condition for investment, growth and job creation.

in writing. − delayed payments in business-to-business and business-to-government relations are one of the existing obstacles to the resumption of economic growth. the vote in favour of the new directive on combating late payment in commercial transitions is a major innovation which will require adequate preparation, especially by the public sector, both at political and administrative level. at the political level, so that financial and budgetary planning takes account not only of the impact of eu rules on the stability pact but also, now, of the impact of new rules on late payments which, if not properly governed, could have a direct and reflected impact on the room for manoeuvre of governments at various levels. at the administrative level, adequate preparation is required for sound financial management of the public body, starting from the ratio between commitments and expenditure, so that burdens, such as passive interest, which could be significant for public budgets, do not burden the treasury and therefore the population. finally, it is important to pay particular attention and flexibility to certain sectors, including health care, where the public administration has accumulated large arrears in payments due to enterprises for actual goods and services supplied.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of mrs weiler's report because i believe it is essential to protect the creditors of the public administration, which are in most cases small and mediumsized enterprises. this measure will allow the re-circulation of some 180 billion in liquidity: the amount of the total debt owed by the general government to the business system throughout the eu. this is a very important step, as companies will be given the automatic right to demand payment of interest on late payments and to obtain a minimum fixed amount of € 40 as compensation for the costs of recovering the debt. in addition, undertakings will also be able to claim reimbursement of any reasonable costs incurred to that end. i believe that this initiative will serve as an incentive for the eu member states to draw up readiness codes for payments. they will be able to maintain or enforce laws and regulations containing provisions more favourable to creditors than those laid down by the directive.
in writing. - among the many proposals in the small business act, the one on amending directive 2000/35/ec was, in my view, one of the most urgent. late payments in many countries (including certainly italy) have become a practice for the public administration. if the european average is 180 days from the deadline, imagine the peaks of delay and the consequences for the management of a medium-sized enterprise. the paradox is that the same state which demands the timely payment of taxes and duties, imposing penalties and applying fines from the first day of delay, when it is in debt, ignores the commitments. the amendment we are voting for is very important, especially at this time of serious economic difficulties. it will not be able to solve the problem on its own. if the procedures for the recovery of claims against public authorities in the individual member states are not made short and effective, the approved estimates will not have any effect.
in writing. - the report tackles the problem of late payment, a problem which destabilises the market and particularly harms small and medium-sized enterprises, for whom i have a particular concern. my vote in favour should be understood as the hope that a new commercial culture will be born, one more favourable to timely payment, one in which late payment is an unacceptable abuse to the detriment of the customer and a breach of contract rather than a normal practice.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of the weiler report because i believe it is essential to set a ceiling within which companies must be paid. it is a need that in these times of crisis is even more pressing and fundamental. smes, together with entrepreneurs, play a significant role in all our economies and are key generators of employment and income and drivers of innovation and growth. unfortunately, too often in recent years we have seen companies that have a multi-million dollar debt to public bodies, but unfortunately have been forced to close or go bankrupt because of delays in payment. i therefore hope that other factors will be taken into account when the treaty is transposed, such as the relaxation of the obligations imposed on public authorities by the treaty and the gradual reduction of the time limits for payment. this would combine the two requirements and benefit the whole country system. i hope that the directive will be quickly transposed by the member states so that it can be applied as soon as possible. it is a duty on the part of us legislators and a right on the part of the creditors.
in writing. - i congratulate mrs weiler on her excellent work. the european parliament has given the green light to new rules to limit delays in payments by public administrations to their suppliers, most of whom are small and medium-sized enterprises. parliament has decided that public bodies will be required to pay for services or goods purchased within 30 days. if this does not happen, they will have to pay interest on late payments at the rate of 8%. the principle that work must be paid for in a timely manner is a fundamental principle of fairness, but it also plays a crucial role in the soundness of an undertaking, its financial availability and its access to credit and finance. the new directive, which will now have to be transposed into national law within 24 months of its adoption, will therefore benefit the whole european economy.
in writing. - italy is the country where businesses suffer most from late payments by public administrations, with an average of 180 days of payments to suppliers, compared to the european average of 67. this leads, especially for smes, to financial problems, a drastic reduction in investment opportunities and a loss of competitiveness. the directive voted today discourages debtors from paying late and allows creditors to protect their rights effectively against such delays, introducing the right to legal interest caused by late payment even where not specified in the contract and requiring the public administration to pay within a maximum of 60 days from the date of the request for payment, subject to proper performance. the adoption of this directive is a great help to our businesses: one in four businesses is closing down because of problems linked to poor financial liquidity. with the new rules on payments, companies will be competitive in the markets again and there will be no job losses.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, in recent years, late payment has become an increasingly important factor in the financial management of companies. they represent a serious and dangerous problem, which is dragging down the quality of the procurement system, seriously undermining the survival of small businesses and contributing to the loss of competitiveness of the european economy. the statistics are alarming, especially for italy, where the average payment is 186 days, with peaks of 800 at regional level, in the health sector. a real shame, which has often forced the closure of several smes. we are taking a big step forward with this report, setting the ceiling for public-private payments at 60 days. of course, the adoption of the legislation will not magically solve the problem, but it is certainly a starting point for activating a virtuous circle, especially in relation to relations with the public administration. the efficiency and immediacy of the public administration in settling invoices is an important step which will also benefit the european economy. i hope that the member states, and especially italy, will be able to implement the legislation very quickly.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of mrs weiler's report on combating late payment in commercial transactions. business activities are severely hampered by debts or late payments, which often, as a kind of domino effect, cause otherwise solvent businesses to fail. late payment is a frequent occurrence in europe to the detriment of businesses, especially small ones. moreover, in most member states, public authorities are in financial difficulty and are often late in paying. the need therefore emerged to strengthen the legislative measures already in place by committing to combating late payments to support businesses, especially smes, and to establish certain time limits and appropriate penalties for non-compliance.
in writing. - mr president, the eu has demonstrated its commitment to combating poverty in europe in the context of the initiatives it has promoted for 2010, the year of combating poverty and social exclusion and towards the achievement of the united nations millennium development goals. given the gravity of the economic and social crisis and its impact on the increase of poverty and social exclusion, certain vulnerable groups of the population, such as women, children, the elderly and young people, have been most affected by the negative effects of the situation. in this situation, although the minimum income may constitute an adequate system of protection for these categories, it does not take into account the principle of subsidiarity and therefore the fact that this matter falls within the competence of the individual member states. since there are inequalities between wage and social levels in europe, it is difficult to establish a common minimum income threshold. i believe, rather, that it is useful to encourage individual member states to improve policy responses to the fight against poverty by promoting active inclusion, adequate income, access to quality services and a fair distribution of wealth. but above all, to encourage the member states to make better use of the structural funds at their disposal.
in writing. - economic and social cohesion is a fundamental prerequisite for any common policy, in europe as well as in smaller contexts. where interests differ, objectives will also diverge and no common plan can be drawn up. raising the living standards of those below the poverty line is a priority. public resources allocated to this area are undoubtedly a medium-term investment, since, if well distributed, they give rise to growth phenomena which feed themselves. it's always uncertain to make fixed-sum money transfers, unless they're part of a larger incentive discourse. two situations deserve a different speech: the first, of social importance, where a worker is unable to earn enough to live in dignity, because of physical or mental disability or other contingent reasons; the second, of legal and economic importance, concerns the rigidity of the labour market, which does not adequately link productivity and wages, or which does not allow people to work as much as they want or in proportion to what they want to earn in order to lead a decent life. in these two situations the public sector can and must intervene, leaving the other cases to create an incentive to engage and never the other way around.
in writing. − it is now essential to integrate the prevention of and the fight against poverty and social exclusion into other community policies in order to guarantee respect for fundamental human rights, universal access to essential public services, the right to health, education and vocational training. this requires the social sustainability of macroeconomic policies, the necessary reorientation of priorities and monetary policies, including the stability and growth pact, and all policies on competition, the internal market, the budget and taxation. this report deals with the controversial subject of the 'minimum income' as a means of transition from social exclusion to a fully active life. but it stresses the importance of accompanying it with broader policies, which also take into account the needs of other needs: health care, education, training, social services and housing. i voted in favour of this report because i share the idea of the need for a european strategy of coordination. however, i believe that the minimum income is a matter for the individual member states, on the basis of respect for the principle of subsidiarity. it is difficult to establish a minimum threshold in the various member states, where there are large differences in wages and in the cost of living in general.
in writing. − what is contained in the lisbon treaty, what is envisaged in the eu 2020 strategy and what is envisaged in the millennium development goals does not seem to be reflected, even at the forecast level, in the disconcerting reality offered by the number of people who still live in poverty. in europe alone, almost 80 million citizens live in poverty, 19 million of them children. the ambitious policies pursued by the international community to eradicate poverty have too often proved ineffective, difficult to implement or to be seen as mere aid measures. the objectives to be achieved must instead take a more structural approach, assessing specific initiatives, coordinated at european level, which have an impact on income, social services and health care in order to alleviate the burden of a financial crisis that has affected the most vulnerable on the labour market, such as women, especially the elderly, and young people. i believe that the evaluation of european initiatives aimed at establishing a minimum income can be one of the ways of combating poverty, albeit in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity.
in writing. the european union has always proclaimed 'social inclusion' as its founding principle. it is difficult to face the many situations that create marginalization, alienation, abandonment. among these, poverty certainly ranks high. but unlike causes such as disease, antisocial behaviour, race, gender, it is a condition for which civilised countries must organise ordinary means of prevention. the minimum income of citizens is a remedy, not a solution. i share the resolution's call for the commission to place the actions of the member states within a european framework of coordination and to provide for an integrated approach to the minimum income, including health care, education and housing. i would add, however, that i personally call on the commission to give priority to actions to support inclusion in the 'platform for combating poverty and social exclusion' in order to prevent it.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of mrs figueiredo's report. work is the top priority for the population. the solidarity on which the european model of social market economy is based and the coordination of national responses are vital. initiatives by individual states cannot be effective without coordinated action at eu level. it is therefore essential that the european union should have a single strong voice and a common vision, while leaving the choice of the practical application of the measures to the individual member states, in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity. in the social market economy, as recognized and required by the treaty, the public system must implement adjustment measures aimed at speeding up and facilitating the achievement of a balance, with the aim of avoiding difficulties for citizens or of limiting them to a minimum. social policies are needed to protect families, limiting inequalities, and the burden and effects of the crisis. we must improve social protection systems by introducing long-term policies, including in the field of employment, and by providing greater stability for employment while avoiding unsustainable burdens on our national budgets.
in writing. - in a modern society of honest and active citizens, providing a minimum income for the unemployed would be a good thing. in reality, guaranteeing an income to those who do not work leads to a distortion of the world of work. many people would prefer not to seek employment by combining a minimum wage with undercover work or by engaging in petty crime. this negative assumption would certainly affect the less well-prepared sections of the population and particularly non-community families, who are often content to divide small and therefore low-cost areas among themselves. it is clear that the guarantee of widespread welfare would lead the poorest people in the world to try to come to europe because it is certainly better, little but surely, than nothing. for these reasons we are firmly opposed to the report.
in writing. - we voted on a very long, very complicated report, with its own detailed steps and its own architecture. but one thing above all else is not convincing: the real, intimate cause of the economic crisis in which we find ourselves has not been adequately addressed, even though it is mentioned in the recitals to the text. and this is not a contingent cause, but a structural cause, not just an economic one. the financial crisis was born above all from the illusion, cultivated by the elites of finance and world politics, that in the third millennium the economy and the wealth of humanity could be based more on finance than on the production of goods, more on the miraculous creation of products of banking engineering than on what is concretely created, produced, sold, marketed by hundreds and hundreds of millions of business entities in the world. the report does not give due weight to the need, which is almost a matter of economic and political culture, to restore the primacy of the real economy over the virtual one, and is therefore fatally doomed to suggest ways out of the crisis which would not in the end represent a real solution. europe does not need a further concentration of economic power at community level. europe needs enterprise and less bureaucracy. i therefore vote against.
in writing. - the adoption of this complex report is a very important step for the european community, which is crying out for clear answers and quick solutions to overcome this difficult economic crisis. i voted in favour because the text adopted today reflects the principles which have always been the basis of my group's economic policy. i am referring, for example, to the need for greater fiscal consolidation, a strengthening of the stability and growth pact, the completion of the single market. i am convinced that europe needs a profound transformation to double its growth potential and that this can only be achieved through greater coordination of the economic and fiscal policies of the member states. first of all, i think it is necessary to review the financial regulation which has proved not only to be flawed but one of the main causes of the crisis. the eu also has to deal swiftly with a number of challenges, including employment, demography and the pension system. first, policies to support smes, the economic engine and heart of europe, must be implemented, particularly by promoting tax relief and incentives to facilitate access to credit.
in writing. - the crisis has taught us a hard lesson, and will continue to teach us, about the static and dynamic aspects of economic policies. it is our job to take these lessons and leverage them to get back on track. we must avoid the mistakes of the past, recognize phenomena that have not been identified before, but above all go deep into the interrelationships between the real economy and finance, making employment and general welfare immune to shocks of this kind. but the european union must do more: the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the reforms and will continue to monitor the implementation of the reforms. i am very pleased that parliament is reflecting on these issues and is continuing to monitor the situation, provided that these wishes are translated into concrete and effective measures.

in writing. - i would like to thank mr feio for the excellent work he has done in preparing this complex report. i voted in favour because i believe it is of the utmost importance to improve the economic governance of the european union. the financial crisis has highlighted the lack of real political and economic coordination between member states and the ineffectiveness of the various control instruments. it is therefore time for europe to adopt a more robust legislative framework, which takes account of the objectives of the eu 2020 strategy, but also implements more controls on public debt and revenue, tax incentives for smes, the development of the internal market and the integration of labour markets. however, in the light of recent agreements, i do not support the introduction of numerical rules, which might prove too mechanistic and difficult to apply in some member states. we must not forget that the financial crisis was caused by toxic financial products and, before that, excessive private debt (subprime mortgages). in other words, the crisis was caused by imbalances in the private sector and banks, not by the public debt of the states. finally, i agree with recommendation no 3, which aims to strengthen coordination between member states through annual surveillance reports for the euro area.
in writing. − the adoption of the euro was a major step for the eu. and the main risk factor is linked not so much to monetary technical issues, on which the european central bank is doing a very good job, but to economic cohesion and the link with the real economy. the problem has emerged most prominently during the crisis: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament on the subject. the reasoning on these issues cannot and must not be a mere exercise or an excuse for seeking legislative sovereignty over matters which are currently within national competence. it is rather to give coherence and systematicity to economic action in the face of increasingly complex situations, where the monetary challenges are different from the past and require different instruments and objectives, and where the responsibilities on the shoulders of the technicians must be accompanied by continuous and constant vigilance and by political directions based on a thoughtful vision of the future and an eye to solving the problems at hand.
