the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the rapporteur on the committee on development, mr mitchell, has asked me to take his place because he cannot be here today. i thank him for his usual punctuality and for the quality of his proposals, which have received the favourable opinion - i would say unanimously - of the committee on development. i am convinced that the report can be adopted by a large majority, despite what i am going to say and, above all, because of what mr mitchell has done so far. i now come to the report. in 2009, the european commission presented a proposal to amend regulation 1905/2006 establishing a financial instrument for development cooperation. with this proposal, the commission had asked parliament to approve an amendment allowing non-governmental organisations to benefit from tax advantages when operating in developing countries. the request was accepted by us. however, the cooperation and development regulation also contains the implementing rules for the european union's development policy. these rules provide that when the commission is to decide on the granting of funds, it is required to follow the comitology procedures. this means that parliament has the power to examine these proposals for funding and, if the commission exceeds its powers, parliament can adopt resolutions to ask the commission to change the decisions in question. since 2006 alone, parliament has found that in at least 12 cases the commission exceeded its implementing powers, but only in 3 of these cases has the commission actually amended or withdrawn its proposal for a decision. after the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, the committee on development proposed that the procedure for delegated acts provided for in article 290 of the treaty of lisbon be applied. adopting this procedure would mean that parliament would have a more important role at least in the strategic decisions on funding that the european commission has to take. in fact, under the lisbon treaty, in certain well-defined cases parliament can delegate to the commission the power to take strategic decisions. but what might those decisions be? in our view, it is up to the legislator to choose which countries the european union should provide development aid to. there is also the question of the priority areas for funding: education, health, environmental protection, the capacity of good governance or the development of small businesses? and how can we ensure transparency in the management of development aid? these are the choices and the matters in which the european parliament should play a greater role than it has in the past. in these areas it is the legislator who must give precise directions to the executive. and i think that is precisely the direction in which the demands of the european citizens are ultimately heading. i sincerely hope that the greatest possible consensus will be reached on this report by mr mitchell.
i would like to thank mr scholz for the preparation of this report, which establishes a financial instrument for cooperation with industrialized countries, an instrument which should be dealt with by the inta committee because it concerns mainly cooperation with industrialized countries and with emerging countries, and for which there is a certain difference compared to the other instruments. i think it is necessary to emphasize first of all the role of parliament. we have also wasted too much time in a tug of war with the council and the commission over an obvious issue after lisbon. we must defend the centrality of parliament both in terms of delegated acts and executive acts. i would like to stress, secondly, the strategic importance of this whole game and, thirdly, the need to intensify cooperation with developing and emerging countries without taking money away from the poorest countries. we must make an effort, within the union budget, to divert more resources to the poorest countries, bearing in mind that the problems with the emerging countries are more related to rules than to funding. however, innovation must also be supported, but with additional resources and not with the resources of the poorer countries.

the rapporteur. - madam president, mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, many of the european union's major economic and trade partners have long had internal regulations requiring products imported into their territory to bear a designation of origin. in 2005, the european commission presented a regulation to put the european union on an equal footing with these countries by requiring that a number of products imported into the european union be labelled with a designation of origin. this regulation will remedy a situation of disparity which has been experienced so far by european consumers who, compared with citizens of non-eu countries, do not have the right to choose, with full knowledge of the origin of what they buy. it is therefore a violation of a democratic right which presupposes freedom of choice, which in turn, in order to be exercised, presupposes the right to knowledge. the regulation removes the inferiority of european citizens and also restores the legitimate right to reciprocity; this is a regulation which is being called for by many consumer associations and is shared by many business associations. the european production system will never be able to recover if our producers are not placed under the same guarantee conditions as those of other countries where a regulation on the indication of the origin of products is already in force. european producers - who rightly have to comply with many of the obligations imposed by the european union to ensure the quality of products to protect consumers and who, in order to export, are obliged to identify their production with a mark of origin - are now facing unfair competition from producers in third countries who can export their goods to europe, effectively concealing their origin. the european small and medium-sized enterprises, which were voted in favour of a resolution in the last legislature on 5 february 2009 on the problems they face in becoming international, continue to face difficulties today because they face unfair competition from those non-eu producers who can export to europe without the mark of origin and european consumers are deprived of their right to an informed choice. the free market, to be truly free, must be based on fair competition and have clear, shared and enforced rules. that is why the adoption of the regulation will finally remedy the deficit of democracy and fair competition which still exists in europe, especially to the detriment of consumers. the regulation was approved by the european parliament's committee on international trade by a large majority: 19 in favour, 3 against. the european parliament had already expressed its support in the previous legislature by a written declaration adopted by a full majority and, in the current legislature, by a vote on a resolution which received 529 votes in favour out of 593 votes. it is really surprising that today some members who had signed the written declaration and voted in favour of the resolution of november 2009 have tabled an amendment to reject the regulation. i am quite certain that those who oppose this proposal will not want to give european citizens the same rights as chinese citizens.
on behalf of the alde group. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, i would like to thank you for your report. madam president, if you were to go to venice, perhaps with commissioner de gucht, to the rialto bridge and buy a pair of shoes that are purportedly italian, a tie, a typical mask or a glass of murano, you would be in danger of being mocked, as you would find that the product you are buying was not made in italy at all but in some asian country. i believe that the proposal for a regulation under consideration is beginning to put some order into an increasingly confused global market, seeking to protect the consumer - including you, madam president, and commissioner de gucht if you are shopping on the rialto bridge in venice, or elsewhere - european industries that have not relocated (while those that have will be penalized by this regulation) and above all it will correct the asymmetry in the commercial markets, which sees europe as the only large area without a regulation on compulsory origin labelling. it is not a protectionist proposal, and i think it is very balanced. it only concerns a limited number of products, the final consumer product and - as far as my group is concerned - a five-year pilot project because we will support the amendment with the sunset clause. in addition, we have also introduced in the committee, through an amendment of my own, a provision which seeks to avoid any excessive bureaucratic burden on businesses. if the vote tomorrow is satisfactory, it will be a stage victory, not a decisive victory. we will then need the full support of the commission in its relations with the council, a commission which has already been very generous with suggestions and very cooperative and which we thank, which is why we must continue to work together. i am sure that in five years' time we will be satisfied with the result we have achieved.
on behalf of the efd group. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, tomorrow the european parliament will vote on the regulation on origin labelling, according to which as the amendments are now being tabled the origin mark should be applied to final consumer goods and to goods intended for the final consumer. the latter definition could cause a serious chain reaction, since it does not include semi-finished and intermediate products which are made in non-european countries and once they reach europe, with a final and perhaps insignificant processing, could acquire the 'made in' mark. the consumer would not be fully informed of the true origin of the product, while large industries would be encouraged to carry out relocation processes in non-eu countries, multiplying their profits to support themselves exclusively and impoverishing our production districts. for these reasons we have tabled amendments to extend this definition to semi-finished and intermediate products, in order to ensure transparency in the traceability of products imported from third countries, on the model of the italian reguzzoni law, which fully respects the rights of the consumer. ladies and gentlemen, this is really the last opportunity we have to protect the manufacturing sector, in italy as in the rest of europe, which is one of the main drivers of the economy, unlike those few industrial powers, who are concerned with their own interests and not the good of the whole community. the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat illegal immigration, and i am sure that the commission will take the necessary steps to ensure that the community's citizens are not subject to the same treatment as the rest of the citizens of the community. the battle we are waging is not against anyone but for work, for businesses, for our workers and for all european citizens.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, i thank the rapporteur, mrs muscardini, and all the shadow rapporteurs with whom i have been following this extremely important dossier. i hope that tomorrow the european parliament will give the same convinced consent to the legislative resolution as it did in july 2006, with the written declaration of 2008 and with the vote in favour of the 2009 resolution. we are about to adopt a measure which should protect the consumer by informing him of the origin of products for more general use, which restores equality of opportunity in international trade and reciprocity between the european union and its main competitors. it does not add any additional costs to the companies in third countries, which are already obliged to mark these products in all the countries of the world, our competitors and many others, nor does it create any burden on the european distribution system which, indirectly and without any cost to public budgets, favours the return of important products to europe, stops the relocation and contributes to the fight against counterfeiting. it is a set of advantages so obvious that they cannot be stopped by invoking additional measures, because here it is just the case to say that the best is the enemy of the good. we must complete a process which began seven years ago, taking care not only of the interests of our companies - especially in this time of crisis and unemployment - but also of the potential of regulated trade based on reciprocity, consumer protection and correct information, which may find further developments in the field of traceability. but woe betide us if this measure does not receive the favourable vote of this parliament. i would like to thank the commission and all those who will support it, because it is useful for the european citizen and for world trade.

member of the commission. − mr president, i notice there is much support across parliament for the proposal, so i will not go into many of the remarks which have been made because most of them support the commission proposal and the muscardini report on it. let me just say with respect to the rules of origin that this is a very stabilised regime. these rules are very stable indeed and they are well known, because it is on the basis of these rules of origin that customs duties are paid when products come into the european market. in fact, our proposal fully relies on them. there can be no misunderstanding about that. the second remark i would like to make is about an amendment introduced by mrs muscardini, which in fact proposes that this ‘made in’ regulation would be a kind of pilot project that would be evaluated after a four-year period and perhaps changed. i consider this an amendment worth supporting, because i imagine that it will enhance the chances that this proposal has in the council. the reason why this proposal dating back to 2005 is not eu legislation is simply that the council does not buy it. it has refused it until now, but the proposal by mrs muscardini to make a pilot project out of this for a five-year period, with an evaluation after four years, is a very good step in the right direction. that is why the commission can accept the amendment proposed.

consequences of this agreement. as far as i understand it, the current stage of the negotiations involves a disparate treatment of geographical indications and trade marks in favour of the latter, and the intangibility, in contravention of article 22 of the trips agreement, of trade marks using names protected by geographical indications, such as parmesan - but this is only one of many possible cases - which can be freely produced, such as parmesan, by the united states and australia and exported to china or elsewhere, in direct competition with european products, which have as one of their strengths geographical indications themselves and which would be supporting unfair competition without any effective protection by acta. i would like to have a clarification on this point. but parmesan means "from parma", not australian or american, and that's true of every european geographical indication. let us be careful because if in the globalization of the 21st century, in a few years, we lose our geographical indications, it will also be because of the wrong choices today and we will lose a huge part of our identity. in this context, if all this is allowed by acta, the agreement is unacceptable. then there's the internet aspect, which i mentioned earlier: the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to cover the whole of the european union, perhaps it is better to let it go.

in writing. the meissner report is a balanced text, taking account of a number of important factors and issues. maritime policy is one of the most important sources of community revenue. just to give you some figures: the eu's maritime transport sector accounts for 40% of its gross domestic product and 40% of intra-community trade. moreover, 95% of its exports to non-eu countries are transported by sea. the report focuses on a few key points: the commission will also be supporting the development of a european maritime policy, including the establishment of appropriate maritime governance structures at national and regional level; coordinated and cross-border maritime spatial planning; maritime surveillance to protect the member states and the eu; safeguarding the marine environment; developing a strategy for sustainable coastal and island tourism; promoting the already leading european shipbuilding industry and maritime transport to achieve the ambitious goal of 'green shipping'. in view of the above, i could only vote in favour. communication and integration of the various sectors covered by maritime policy must and must be made to 'speak' for a whole range of reasons linked to efficiency, competitiveness and also to respect and protection of the marine environment.
in writing. − while there is no doubt that maritime policy needs to be integrated into the european union, given that maritime activities account for 40% of the eu's gdp, it is also right to regulate maritime activities in a way that takes account of non-eu competitors. too often, the rules on fisheries, tourism, transport and environmental protection in the sector have been developed separately and without taking into account the risks of unfair competition from third countries. for example, extending too strict emission limits to all coastal areas in europe can create distortions of competition. other texts on the subjects discussed have been discussed and approved by parliament and undoubtedly require integrated coordination, such as maritime surveillance, which is essential to control the illicit activities that often occur off the coasts of europe, ranging from the trafficking of counterfeit goods to smuggling, the transport of prohibited substances and illegal fishing.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the report on the integrated maritime policy concerns an important sector of the european economy. maritime activities are an important source of income for the union, both in terms of gdp and in terms of trade, both internal and external. i think it is appropriate to focus on a few issues. firstly, the report states that future strategies in this area will focus on the specificity of the sea basins, and i think it is very important to take account of regional peculiarities as well. the new maritime policy also focuses on the development of safe shipping and offers great opportunities for the future of the european shipping industry. our seas must continue to be a growth engine, and for this reason i think it is essential that the development of an integrated maritime policy ensures greater coherence between the regulations governing the different maritime sectors, and at the same time safeguards the marine environment.
in writing. the european union is based on a system of values with which latin american countries have made significant progress in recent years. such progress certainly merits further incentives under the eu's trade policy. if we add to this the linguistic and cultural links which history has left us, we have the opportunity to contribute as much as possible to the economic and social development of these countries, however fragile their situation may be. it is also useful for both sides to take account of the main factors determining the political developments in these countries and to take steps to avoid any deviations which would harm the states and ourselves. the strengthening of trade relations can only be welcomed, provided that development policies are monitored to continue to provide an incentive for improvement.

likely to limit president obama’s room for manoeuvre even further. we need to make sure that the us does not back-track on its copenhagen commitments and we must encourage them to contribute to a climate change for poor and developing countries. these can proceed without us domestic legislation, as can biological research work on clean technologies. there was also a question on the us visa-waiver programme and the fact that a number of eu member states – bulgaria, cyprus, poland and romania – are still not admitted to this programme. we attach much importance to their admission and we will continue working with our us counterparts on resolving this issue. in relation to the introduction of the esta fee for travellers under the visa-waiver programme, the commission has repeatedly voiced concern that these new requirements are inconsistent with the commitment of the us to facilitate transatlantic mobility and that they constitute an additional burden for european citizens travelling to the us. we need to make sure that work on security issues, such as pnr, goes hand in hand with facilitating transatlantic travel for legitimate travellers. regarding the question on the wikileaks documents, we are unable to comment on the information contained in the leaks at present. however, as a matter of principle, the eu is firmly committed to upholding the absolute prohibition of torture and cruel, inhumane and degrading treatment. this is all we can say at this moment in time. there was a question from ms quisthoudt on the possibility of a free trade agreement with the us. we are not considering this at this moment in time, ms quisthoudt, because, as regards the eu-us trade relationship, an earlier study conducted by dg trade on non-tariff measures shows that non-tariff barriers remain the major obstacle in eu-us trade relations and concludes that the gdp of the eu and the us would increase by about eur 160 billion and exports would grow by 2.1% and 6.1% respectively if half of the non-tariff measures and regulatory differences were removed. in fact, there are not that many tariffs any more between the us and the eu. that said, existing barriers are often very difficult to remove but this is precisely why, in the tec, we are pushing for early and upstream cooperation, for example before we adopt regulations in important areas, in particular emerging markets and new technologies. regarding the tec and what its agenda might be, we are currently working with our us counterparts to fix the final agenda for the next tec meeting, bearing in mind the input from advisers. the main themes we are looking at are innovation and emerging technologies, and strategies for greening our economies and building the transatlantic market place. under these themes we will have opportunities to discuss a wide range of issues including e-health, the interoperability of electronic health records, secure trade, mutual recognition of authorised trade standards and overall approach to regulation, the innovation action partnership and exchange of information on consumer product safety. we will also discuss joint responses to economic challenges. furthermore, at the end of november, as was asked by the committee on the internal market and consumer protection, i will discuss standards. i believe the precise date is 29 november. the last question was on the 100% scanning of inbound container freight. we are concerned about the us requirements that, by july 2012, all us-bound maritime containers will have to be scanned before being placed on a vessel at a foreign port. we believe that this requirement will not bring proven security benefits and will be a barrier to smooth trade. for these reasons the commission does not envisage the implementation of 100% scanning in eu ports. the us homeland security secretary, janet napolitano, has announced plans to push back the july 2012 deadline for 100% scanning by two additional years. the commission is hopeful that this delay will lead the us congress to review its policy and favour a risk-based approach to supply chain security. the main challenges for the eu over the next year suggest many synergies and opportunities for cooperation with the us: dealing with the economic crisis; governance, restoring growth and jobs by accelerating reforms, building an area of freedom, justice and security, and pulling our weight on the global stage. we have a number of important tasks ahead as we look to the forthcoming eu-us summit and beyond. one of them is building a more open and outward-looking eu-us relationship that would take into account the full scope of relations that both the eu and the us are building with emerging powers such as china, india, russia and brazil. on the economy, jobs and growth are at the heart of the discussion. we will compare notes on the g20 results, especially financial and banking reforms and the need to deliver a global trade deal, and look for eu-us added-value there. at the same time we need to focus more on delivering the full potential of the transatlantic market. my aim will be to refocus the tec on a transatlantic agenda for jobs, growth and innovation. with the support of the eu-us senate leaders, i will look to move forward on that at the forthcoming tec meeting on 17 december.
vice-president of the commission. − madam president, after the remarks of my colleague karel de gucht on the general agreement and relations with the united states, let me concentrate on the future umbrella agreement on data protection. it is very clear that we need to share data in order to fight terrorism and organised crime and, at the same time, we need to preserve the rights of citizens to data protection. trying to achieve both in equilibrium will be the content of those negotiations. as i have already told you, on 26 may this year the commission put forward a proposal for a negotiation mandate. we are looking now to the council to have this mandate agreed upon, hopefully at the beginning of december, so that we can start with real negotiations. i absolutely agree with what has been said in this house. we need to concentrate on legal security in an umbrella agreement instead of – and i quote a member of this parliament – ‘fire-fighting on each individual data-sharing agreement’. if we, the united states and europe, manage to set common standards, then those common standards will sooner or later become world standards. we have to show that those standards are built on our values of justice and fundamental rights and of the right to reciprocity, both of which have to be very clearly put on the transatlantic agenda. the question of individuals’ rights in such an agreement has also been raised. what the commission has put on the table would mean the following for our european citizens and for the citizens in the united states: enforceable rights for individuals, such as the right to access personal data that has been collected about them and the right to rectify and erase this data, administrative and judicial redress, regardless of nationality or place of residence, and compensation for any damages suffered. the effective application of these rights would be ensured by the monitoring and controlling of these data protection standards by independent public authorities and, in this context, a non-discrimination clause should also be included to ensure that all personal data is protected regardless of a person’s nationality or place of residence, bearing in mind at all times that we need to strike a balance between rights and security and also, at least in my view, not to allow any discrimination on racial grounds. in order not to allow this, the commission will certainly need the help of parliament. i have heard that you want to establish, or you have already established, specific new bilateral relations between parliament and the united states congress. i think that this will also be very important in order to raise understanding of such data protection agreements on both sides of the atlantic, so here you could be of much help in the course of the negotiations.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, it seems to me natural, as a first step, to thank the negotiators, and in particular mr gauzès, together with the shadow rapporteurs, for the excellent work that has been done on the directive on alternative investment fund managers, finally ensuring that funds have a single rule throughout the european union. these funds are responsible for managing a substantial volume of assets invested in europe and can exert a significant influence on markets. their impact is largely beneficial, but their activities can also contribute to spreading risks throughout the financial system. the new common provisions replace the current 27 different national systems and enhance the opportunities of the single market. alternative funds, regardless of their domicile, therefore have a european passport. in addition, the single european regime will prevent funds from taking advantage of the laws of states offering more favourable regulatory regimes. in the past, this practice has entailed considerable speculative risks for the whole of the european union. i also agree with the introduction of the rules on so-called asset stripping and the ban on short-term short selling, two points which were not included in the european commission's initial proposal. finally, it is essential, in order to avoid distortions of competition, that a third country fund should be able to operate within the european union under the same conditions as eu funds.

on behalf of the efd group. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the volatility of cereal prices is having a serious impact on all sectors of the livestock industry, but also on consumers. the heat, the fires, the drought and the floods - as are happening now in italy - have blocked the export of cereals. to make matters worse, canada has reduced production following heavy rains this summer. not only has climate change affected prices, but speculation on international markets has also. grain producers who are waiting for a price increase wait to see their production and store it, with the consequent depletion of agricultural products. speculation and severe climate change have led to a sharp rise in the price of grain used as animal feed and to a subsequent rise in the price of meat. i believe that timely and targeted action by the commission is essential to deal with the volatility of agricultural prices through innovative market interventions in the new cap. the commission must prevent speculative practices in agriculture in order to preserve the activities of farmers and livestock farmers and to ensure that consumers have genuine products of high quality at fair prices.
the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. i would like to thank mrs garcía in particular for this initiative and would like to draw attention to the particular situation of mountain farming. in many areas of the european union, there are agricultural alternatives to livestock farming, but in the mountainous areas, there are not. if there are no scavengers, then many agricultural areas in the mountainous areas are simply useless and are abandoned. this not only reduces the economic opportunities in the mountain area, but also changes the landscape and ultimately reduces biodiversity. the dairy sector has a very special role to play in this, because it creates economic opportunities and income for livestock farming in the mountain areas and not only in the mountain areas. i therefore believe that we must pay particular attention to three things in the reform of agricultural policy. we must have a cap which takes account of mountain farming, including coupled contributions to mountain farmers. secondly, we need to continue to have a flexible second pillar, in which it is possible to give special support to livestock farms in mountain areas. and thirdly, we need a quality policy which takes special account of products from the mountain areas, including very special labelling, so that the added value of such products from mountain livestock farming can also be obtained on the market.

in writing. - freedom is one of the cornerstones on which this parliament is founded. this value is the foundation on which the european institutions are built, the source of energy which enables the market to give the necessary impetus to a diverse and complex economy, the breath of our citizens who move, for study or work, to the cities of those places which were once places to be reached with a passport and perhaps a visa. its importance is therefore not in question. the issue that this report highlights is rather its relationship to security. the problem is not easily solved. information must be collected, analysed in the right places and care must be taken to avoid misuse. the control of this mechanism must be continuous, constant and must not allow for any leakage. the citizens must not be allowed to feel that they are willing to set aside their freedom, just as they must not be allowed to use it to endanger the security of the people of europe. i think the report offers a good compromise for the balance between the two conflicting principles.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i share the commission's objectives in its communication. the reasons why the use and exchange of pnr data with third countries is necessary and useful for security purposes should be made transparent and understandable. at the same time, it must be demonstrated that there is a full awareness of the implications that such activities may have on privacy and the need for them to be covered by a set of uniform, recognisable and rigorous rules on the protection of personal data, to be enforced also when personal data is transferred to other countries. the use and exchange of pnr data will not only provide greater security for citizens, but will also make their lives and their cross-border movements easier. pnr data can significantly reduce police checks by focusing surveillance only on those for whom factual grounds of genuine risk emerge and by dispensing others from unnecessary checks and inspections.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, despite all the appeals to not let down our guard over the fate of haiti after the earthquake in january, the news of the last few days seems to show that the island has been abandoned by the international community at the most delicate moment, that of reconstruction. the cholera virus is spreading these days, something that few in haiti know about and that everyone ends up attributing a mystical, religious value to. the un peacekeepers are blamed for the spread of the disease. one nepalese soldier on the island was infected, and hundreds of people, including women and children, besieged the peacekeeping headquarters. humanitarian workers are also feeling threatened and many are leaving the country. the tension is very high and much of the rubble from the violent earthquake of january 12 remains in the streets and squares. we heard that there is a lack of water and therefore it is impossible to wash and protect oneself from infection. the vibrator is spreading rapidly and the death toll is rising exponentially. the numbers have been given before, but i want to repeat it: the number of deaths has now reached 1,130, the number of hospitalizations has risen to over 18,000 in a month, but there are thousands more reporting symptoms of the infection every day. any further delay by the international community is no longer possible. the solution must be found immediately, otherwise every further infection will remain on our consciences forever.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, first the epicentre of a terrible earthquake, precisely in the poorest and worst governed part of the american hemisphere, and now cholera in the country with the highest per capita international assistance. what a paradox! it 's not just a terrible combination of bad luck: in haiti, with these streets full of children and tents crammed with garbage, you don't know where to start. the local political class is often greedy and focused on power games rather than taking on the reconstruction and the bureaucratic machine, decimated by the earthquake, has a weak administrative culture and in some cases even came to hinder the receipt of aid. the international organizations are many, often poorly coordinated, and have in fact failed to protect the population. as early as last june, when i visited the country with the european parliament delegation, it was clear that the concentration of displaced camps, unremoved rubble and waste was a sign of the worst-case scenarios. and now the cholera has come. the commission and echo have done their part so far, but now we must redouble our efforts. i believe that haiti now needs not only vigorous rehabilitation but also greater protection at the international political level.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the directive we are discussing is intended to harmonize the content and quality of pharmaceutical information available to all citizens of the union. while reaffirming the right to publicity, the patient's right to information is finally affirmed. we must give all european citizens the same access to information on medicines. the main objective of this directive is to make patients more informed citizens, enabling them to approach medicines in a more conscious way. we all, and the pharmaceutical industry in particular, must have the same objective, namely to disseminate correct and useful information which is equally accessible to all citizens. i consider that the directive has two main points. firstly, by providing the right information, we can give people the opportunity to use medicines appropriately, so that the health benefits are enhanced and the risks of misuse are minimised. secondly, correct and effective information can make citizens more aware of the burden of pharmaceutical expenditure on current expenditure. however, there are some areas where we must be very careful and strict. i am referring above all to the danger of information on medicines becoming hidden advertising. we must prevent the risk that behind apparently scientific information there is in fact a much less noble intention to influence and direct the patient towards the purchase of a medicine. effective tools for controlling information, especially information that the patient can obtain via the internet, are therefore indispensable. in conclusion, i therefore hope that the commission will provide for forms and methods of checking the information in order to ensure that it is correct. these checks should be entrusted to dedicated and independent organisations, so as to have greater guarantees of impartiality.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, this report is of the utmost importance because it will make it possible to harmonize european legislation on access to information on medicinal products and, above all, because it will guarantee patients greater information on prescription medicines. the presence of such information on websites shall be transparent and independent. to ensure this, all information must be checked by the competent national or european authorities to prevent it from becoming a hidden promotion of medicinal products, perhaps by the manufacturing companies. finally, i would urge the same attention to be paid to the information contained in the brochures of prescription medicines. in this respect, i would prefer that the doctors or pharmacists should inform the patients in detail, so that there is all the necessary awareness about the administration of medicines.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, we believe that the regulation is a positive one, since it aims to provide a harmonised regulatory framework for non-promotional information on prescription medicines, which pharmaceutical companies can disclose to the public, while maintaining the prohibition on advertising. this proposal highlights the difference between advertising and information. the provision of information is based on the principles of active research. the main channel of information on medicines must continue to be the doctor. other channels, intended as complementary, must be maintained, and these include magazines and newspapers. the focus has been on the patient's right to information, with the active involvement of organisations representing citizens and in particular patients. our vote is in favour.

on behalf of the efd group. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, we in the committee have taken the opposite view of the proposal for a directive because the rapporteur had radically changed the commission's proposal in a restrictive way, opening up the scope, proposing the phasing out of 33 other substances added to annex iii, including flame retardants, bromates and chlorides, as well as pvc and its additives, restricting the possibilities for exemption and adaptation times, and introducing stringent legislation for nanomaterials. if this choice, which is not backed by sufficient scientific evidence, were to win a favourable vote in the house, it would have caused very serious damage to the economy, with serious repercussions on employment. fortunately, thanks to a series of trilogues in which i participated as a shadow rapporteur, a more than satisfactory compromise was reached, with a commitment to verification and possible revision within three years. another complex topic was the detailed definition of nanomaterials, which was deferred pending a commission proposal. the text, as it has come out of the trilogues, can be signed and voted in favour of.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, in recent years we have seen considerable efforts by the community institutions to make the production, use and disposal of electronic products more environmentally friendly and more environmentally friendly. the rohs directive is one piece of this policy. compliance with directives is undoubtedly a challenge and a burden for companies, but it is also an opportunity. the ability to offer products which are less polluting becomes a very important differentiating factor for our companies, and can be considered a real competitive advantage. companies should not only see the rules and requirements of the directive as punitive obligations, but also as opportunities to improve business processes and product quality. however, some exemptions have become necessary - some because of the current severe economic crisis, others because they will be the subject of a future specific directive. this is the case for nanomaterials, the space and security sectors, fixed installations, transport vehicles and self-propelled machinery, medical equipment for implantation in the human body, photovoltaic panels and equipment for research and development applications. finally, i would like to take this opportunity to call for greater consistency between the rohs directive and the reach regulation, avoiding any risk of confusion and overlap, because companies and operators need clear and certain rules.

in writing. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, according to recent figures, 9.3 million tonnes of electrical and electronic equipment are sold in the european union every year, most of which are large household appliances and computer and telecommunications equipment. as the market expands and innovation cycles shorten, equipment is replaced more frequently, contributing to an increase in the waste stream of electrical and electronic equipment. it is estimated that this waste will reach 12,3 million tonnes by 2020. the rohs directive, adopted in 2003, aimed at phasing out a first set of hazardous substances and has reduced the amount of substances disposed of and potentially released into the environment. the revision of this directive was planned with the aim of introducing stricter rules on the restriction of dangerous substances. i believe that the compromise package, reached after lengthy negotiations between the council and parliament, represents an important step forward in the direction of greater clarity and simplification of the directive. among the regulated aspects, the exclusion from the scope of the directive of all substances which, without any scientific evidence, would have been banned, thus contributing to the harm of the many undertakings operating on the market, is of particular importance.
in writing. dear colleagues, given the high priority of the revision of this directive, it should be borne in mind that its main purpose is to provide for stricter and even more stringent rules on the restriction of the use of dangerous substances. now, i think this compromise package represents a significant step forward towards greater clarity and simplification of the rohs directive. among the many aspects that are being considered in order to be regulated, i would like to emphasize in particular the exclusion from the scope of the directive of all those substances - such as pvc and nanomaterials - which would be subject to a production ban. this, ladies and gentlemen, is not only due to the absence of objective scientific evidence, but also to the detriment of the technological progress connected with the production of these materials. so overall we can be satisfied with the negotiating agreement. on the one hand, this agreement strengthens the protection of the environment by prohibiting substances which are considered dangerous on the basis of reliable scientific evidence; the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the safety of the products concerned is not compromised.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i wish to inform parliament of what has happened to the exhibition 'promoting cultural values through the protection of the cultural heritage of occupied cyprus' which is being held at the committee of the regions from 17 to 26 november. on 17 november, after the opening, the head of the dg communication wolfgang petzold ordered the exhibitors to suspend the exhibition immediately, citing the fact that the panels bore different captions from those agreed. i have had the application for authorization sent to me and i have verified that there is no difference between what is authorized by the same office and what is shown. it also appears that the curator of the exhibition was told by the same unit chief to delete the terms "occupation" and "turkish invasion". i have telephoned the head of the unit several times to clarify what happened, but neither the manager in question nor his staff have agreed to speak to me. within hours of these allegations being made, the exhibition was reopened. ladies and gentlemen, i consider what has happened to the committee of the regions to be a serious violation of the rights of an eu member state.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to inform the members, citizens and associations that we have tabled written declaration 0086/2010 calling for the protection of water as a public good. water is not just a common good, it is a universal human right, and the management of water services as a local public service is the foundation of good governance. these are our guiding principles and they are the same principles that have moved thousands of italian citizens to sign all the requests for referendums to avoid the removal of a primary good from the public sphere. we believe that the initiative is not exclusive to those who have proposed it, because this is a battle that belongs to everyone. in confirmation of this, it should be said that the declaration was put forward together with colleagues from the political groups of the greens, the socialist and democratic friends and the european left and is finding a broad consensus throughout parliament. the aim is to collect at least half the signatures of the members of parliament so that the declaration becomes the official position of the european parliament and can safeguard water as a right and not as a profit.
the debate is closed.
the agenda includes the report by mr ivo belet, on behalf of the committee on culture and education, on public service broadcasting in the digital age: the future of the dual system (2010/2028(ini) (a7-0286/2010)
member of the commission. − madam president, the commission welcomes the european parliament’s report entitled ‘public service broadcasting in the digital era: the future of the dual system’. the report is a well-balanced text as it supports the existing dual system, based on co-existence between public service broadcasters and commercial broadcasters in europe. as the audiovisual media services directive recalls in one of its recitals, this co-existence is a feature that distinguishes the european audiovisual media market from others and the report fully recognises this. the protocol on the system of public broadcasting in the member states, annexed to the eu treaties, recognises the member states’ freedom to define the public service remit to organise public service broadcasting and its funding, as long as such funding does not affect trading conditions and competition in the community. therefore, the member states determine the form and conditions of funding of their public service media so long as eu state aid rules are respected. we agree with the main thrust of the report, i.e. that public broadcasters should be able to use the opportunities offered by digitisation and the diversification of distribution platforms, in line with the principle of technological neutrality. this was acknowledged in the revised communication from the commission of 2009 on the application of state aid rules to public service broadcasting. we have some comments on two elements of the report in particular. first, regarding monitoring the council of europe standards, there is no eu responsibility for the political independence of public service media. furthermore, eu member states cannot give a mandate to the european audiovisual observatory without the agreement of the non-eu members. the commission could not do so either. second, the report suggests that certain member states have failed to take any action in promoting european works in broadcasting. this is not supported by figures from the commission’s recent report on the application of the directive’s provisions. according to that report, broadcasters across europe are doing well overall in terms of the promotion of european programmes. public service broadcasters should be at the forefront of innovation, driving the development of new formats and quality, as regards both the programme itself and technically, if they are to keep up with trends and challenges from elsewhere. it seems that we fully agree on these points and i look forward to cooperating with parliament on these issues within the legal framework provided by the treaties.
the debate is closed. the vote will take place on thursday 25 november 2010. the commission shall be assisted by the committee of the regions.
the agenda includes the report by christian ehler, on behalf of the committee on foreign affairs, on civil-military cooperation and civil-military capacity building (2010/2071 ((ini)) (a7-0308/2010).
member of the commission. − madam president, i will focus on the report, since it is an extremely useful and important report. i would like to thank mr ehrenhauser for his contribution. the report is useful because it rightly focuses on the key element of civil-military cooperation, which is exactly the commission’s priority. it deals with the main points related to the eu’s comprehensive approach in crisis management. the establishment of the european external action service is the exact expression of this priority. the very concept of the service that the high representative is putting in place points in the same direction as the one suggested in the report, in particular through the inclusion of the structures of the common security and defence policy in the external action service. we fully support the development of civilian capabilities in order to have a proper balance between resources. the appropriate modalities for recruitment are now agreed, and appropriate expertise can be brought into the external action service. as everyone knows, this was not possible before. a number of points in the report have been taken into account, and specific actions have been launched. this relates in particular to fostering civil-military synergies, better usability of the eu battle groups, training, financing, and cooperation with key partners, in particular nato and the united nations. we also support the reinforcement of relations between the eu and the united nations. we have already done a lot together. the high representative again met with the un secretary general in lisbon last saturday. the relationship between the eu and nato is an important issue, as was illustrated just yesterday at the nato summit in lisbon. we also favour implementing all practical measures which can reinforce concrete cooperation between the eu and nato and ensure, in particular, cooperation when both are deployed in the same theatre. the commission and the high representative herself are looking forward to working together with the european parliament on this important issue of civil-military cooperation.
the debate is closed. the vote will take place on tuesday 23 november 2010. the commission shall be assisted by the committee of the regions.
on behalf of the ppe group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, in recent weeks severe floods have hit some european countries, bringing the population of the regions concerned to their knees. last week four belgian citizens were killed in the provinces of waals-brabant, oost-vlanderen and henegouwen, on the border with the capital and in the north of the country. authorities say it was the worst flooding in 50 years. in two days, the amount of rain that usually falls in a month has been recorded, so much so that the intervention of the army was necessary to evacuate the most damaged territories. a similar situation exists in the western part of france, where many roads that are impassable to traffic have blocked the transport system. autumn plantings are also blocked by the continuing rainfall that does not allow access to the land. twenty days ago, in my own country, italy, the regions of veneto were also hit hard, with two deaths, friuli-venezia giulia, liguria and calabria, with one death, the province of salerno in campania and tuscany, with three deaths, with dozens of injured people pulled from the mud and rubble and one person still missing in rovigo. the damage amounts to over one billion euros for the most immediate interventions alone, to which must be added the funds needed for structural works. over 4,500 people were displaced, 280 communities and more than 500,000 people were affected, agricultural areas were devastated and 150,000 livestock drowned. i would like to emphasize two points. the first is the exceptional mobilization of the aid machine and the world of solidarity, which, with thousands of volunteers, supported the affected populations in the first emergency phase. they must receive the thanks and applause of our institution. the second aspect is related to the long-term effects that this catastrophe will trigger. the european fabric of production is characterized by small and mediumsized enterprises which have lost everything: machinery, equipment, processing materials. the same is true of the thousands of farms whose plantations have been destroyed, but also of tractors, machinery and seeds rendered useless by mud, flooded stables and farms, and drowned thousands of cattle and chickens. these companies, which were already struggling with the economic crisis, are now doomed to fail. the floods will eventually destroy the productive system, leading to unemployment and impoverishment in these areas. it is therefore urgent that europe does its part by giving the governments of the countries concerned assurances that they are prepared to mobilise the solidarity fund. even in the absence of the strict criteria for the activation of the fund and even without the approval of the 2011 budget, we must give an immediate response to our fellow citizens who are still experiencing the effects of such a great tragedy and who have the right to feel the closeness of this parliament and the concrete support of the european union.
on behalf of the efd group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, on behalf of my group i would like to express our solidarity with all the citizens affected by the floods. however, i would like to speak about my region, a region of 5 million inhabitants where 500,000 people have been affected by flooding, with 131 municipalities affected, 7,000 people displaced, 140 km2 flooded, 3 hospitals and health facilities evacuated, 2 deaths. agriculture was damaged and 23% of the venetian enterprise system was affected by the flood. so you can imagine the scale of this catastrophe. europe must do more. europe must mobilise the solidarity fund and we know that if the budget is not adopted the fund cannot be mobilised. but europe, in addition to talking about grand strategies, development plans and fantastic planning, should invest more in research and prevention of hydrogeological risk, promote responsible land use planning, encourage the use and study of early warning systems. it should invest more in water protection, because our rivers are at risk and continue to endanger the health of our citizens. so i really hope that europe, for once, will respond and make itself heard, since it is often accused of being distant from our citizens.
the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, today we are called upon to vote on a package of aid for the netherlands, which has called for the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund for a total amount of eur 10.5 million. this internal transfer of funds to the union budget will continue in the normal way. however, the next requests for aid, the number of which is constantly increasing, risk being blocked due to the non-approval of the 2011 budget. if the twelfths system were to come into force in january, it would not be possible to make the transfers and the necessary payments. in this particular period of economic difficulties for the whole of europe, parliament called for a high degree of responsibility on the part of the member states, which had created resistance in the council to the adoption of an austere budget in line with the prerogatives of the lisbon treaty.
the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, thanks to the change of agenda approved yesterday by this house, i am here to express my first and foremost satisfaction that the juri committee has unanimously approved the draft report we are now voting on. it is important that the construction of the european legal area should be supported by such a broad consensus in parliament. the stockholm programme is a deeply personal reflection of the very nature of the process of building a people's europe, not just of political forces or institutional representation. it is intended to solve the problems of life for europeans by creating a genuine and unified common market in labour, goods and services, a business activity without internal frontiers and without bureaucratic obstacles, and to strengthen the common basis of the law of inheritance, contracts, consumers, timeliness of payments, the family, minors and more. it will also be the task and merit of the judiciary, national magistrates, lawyers, accountants and workers in the individual states to make europe, to interpret the law that unites our continent. our past is marked by different judicial and legal traditions common law and civil law with differences between french or german codes and sometimes distant histories. we respect national prerogatives and the principle of subsidiarity, but we also recognize that to make europe - and fortunately the path is now being taken - we need a gradual convergence based on a great constitutional tradition of fundamental rights, which is the symbol of europe. mr president, the action plan we are about to adopt aims to build, strengthen, extend and disseminate a solid european legal culture, a european legal mentality. i recommend that we vote for it.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, this report examines the annual report and the work carried out during the year. the economic and financial and, increasingly, political actions are still largely dominated by the international financial crisis. the events in greece and other eurozone countries have, of course, complex causes. the problems are largely of internal origin, being the result of the lack of internal structural reforms. there is no doubt that european monetary union has not worked the way it was designed. the principles of the stability and growth pact have not always been respected and what initially appeared to be minor breaches have, over time, proved to have seriously undermined the pact as a whole. we must therefore learn the right lesson from this situation. the european monetary union must be rebalanced, financial markets must be made more transparent and crises better managed, and public confidence must be fundamentally rebuilt. this is a huge challenge, but it is also an opportunity which we must seize.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the commission's proposal to exempt the introduction and relocation of closed aquaculture installations from the requirement of authorization could not but be accompanied by a stricter definition of the requirements which these installations must meet. that is why i gave my full support to mr ferreira's report. however, i would like to take this opportunity to point out the lack of adequate support for scientific research and technological development in the field of native species husbandry. increased support in this area is crucial for the sustainable development of european aquaculture. only in this way can we diversify food production and supply, guaranteeing improved quality and greater environmental safety.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the single market is one of the pillars of the european union. it is true that, on equal terms, firms can produce and sell their products and services without public support, but not all sectors and not all territories are on equal terms. it is therefore right, as is the case today, to correct economic disadvantages and to allow those productive entities to exist, to remain on the market and to maintain employment levels, as for example in sulcis, where 500 families would have been without work, without income, without dignity. it is important to remember that when we talk about coal we are talking about areas which have no alternative to mining and which must be allowed to adopt production technologies which are competitive, compatible with the free market and with the environment. logically, the postponement of public support to 2018 must be an imperative for institutions and companies to act immediately to achieve technological, financial and environmental compatibility conditions in line with the challenges ahead.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the quality of the work done by the joint parliamentary assembly of the european parliament has made it a key player in north-south cooperation throughout the world. strengthening the parliamentary dimension of cooperation has proved essential in order to ensure the sound use of funds, the satisfaction of the needs of the population and the achievement of the millennium development goals on health and education. the european commission has for some time been putting national and regional policy papers under the parliamentary scrutiny of both the european parliament and the national parliaments. i voted in favour of this report because i want to support the work done so far by our assembly, which now has an even more important role in the supervision of the negotiations for the economic partnership agreements. in 2009, the european commission, together with the acp, put forward proposals for the second revision of the partnership agreement and i hope that its survival and evolution as a key institution in this process of cooperation and democratization in the rest of the world can be ensured.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, first of all i would like to congratulate my colleague, mrs joly, on her report. we live in a world today where human history seems to be traveling on separate tracks. there are continents where the day is marked by innovation, technology and an objective well-being, and others where people spend hours, from dawn to dusk, in the desperate search for the minimum means of survival. in 2009, the joint parliamentary assembly worked actively to ensure that the many proposals could be translated into concrete commitments and targets to be achieved. the european union has demonstrated its firm resolve to take timely, targeted and coordinated action in support of the most affected countries, in particular the poorest and most vulnerable. the 20th acp-eu plenary session will be held in kinshasa on 1 december, during which an important report on the millennium development goals will be discussed. i will do my utmost, as rapporteur and as vice-president of the assembly, to ensure that all the measures adopted do not become mere slogans but become concrete commitments to continue the journey towards a more equitable world and above all a world without poverty.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the stockholm programme, adopted by the european council in december last year, aims to create a european area of freedom, security and justice, to be achieved in the next five years, capable of guaranteeing citizens the enjoyment of all their fundamental rights. the ultimate objective of eu law must therefore be to facilitate mobility and to ensure that citizens themselves can establish a european judicial area as quickly as possible. the action plan proposed by the european commission includes a whole series of measures, drawing on the new instruments made available by the lisbon treaty, to reconcile the needs of citizens in the single market with the different judicial traditions of the member states. i voted in favour of this report because, given the necessary premises, it calls on the member states to commit themselves actively to its implementation, emphasizing those areas which should be considered as priorities, such as civil matters, mutual recognition of acts and judgments, the common framework, debtors' assets and common judicial training. i would like to stress once again my conviction that the european parliament must be involved in this process of harmonization after a careful examination of the existing legislation at national level. today, the harmonisation of legislation and the respective scope of civil and criminal law on many issues is interrelated and has become an integral part of the discussions in international trade negotiations because it raises a number of legal issues that are still unresolved.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of the mobilisation of the european solidarity fund. i believe that it is a valuable instrument which enables the european union to show its solidarity with the people of regions affected by natural disasters by providing financial support to help them to restore normal living conditions quickly. the request approved in today's vote was submitted by ireland, in reference to heavy rainfall which caused severe flooding in november 2009. these floods have caused serious damage to the agricultural sector, residential and business properties, the road network and other infrastructure. the irish authorities estimated the total direct damage caused by the disaster at eur 520,9 million. since these are below the threshold provided for in the regulation, the commission examined the application on the basis of the so-called 'extraordinary regional disaster' criterion, according to which a region affected by an extraordinary disaster, mainly of natural origin, which has affected the majority of the population, with profound and lasting repercussions on the living conditions and economic stability of the region itself, may benefit from the fund's assistance. finally, i would add that the fund has been mobilised for a total amount of eur 13 022 500.

in writing. - i congratulate the rapporteur and colleague david casa on the preparation of this report which allows us to return to a fundamental issue such as vat and tax harmonization. i agree with the rapporteur that the current vat system, partly because of its increased complexity, is not keeping pace with the development of the internal market and is putting businesses and smes at a disadvantage, greatly affecting their competitiveness. moreover, the current tax legislation has many weaknesses that can be exploited by tax evaders to their illicit advantage. i therefore support the commission's proposal for a delay in the creation of a common vat system in order to give businesses the necessary legal certainty, but at the same time i urge the commission to conclude its analysis as soon as possible by drawing up, with the involvement of this house, a green paper on the revision of the vat system.
in writing. the report extends the transitional arrangements introduced by council directive 92/77/eec, which introduced a system of minimum rates of vat, stipulating that the standard rate could not be lower than 15%. since no final system of tax harmonisation has yet been established in the union, it is now common practice to set minimum rates of indirect taxation. in the field of vat, this avoids the increasing divergence between the normal rates applied in the member states leading to structural imbalances and distortions of competition. the difference between the normal rates applied currently ranges between 15% and 25% and is sufficient to ensure the proper functioning of the internal market. the extension allows businesses to have the necessary legal certainty, but also to make further assessments as to the appropriate level of the standard vat rate across the eu. the commission is also urged to publish a green paper on a new vat strategy in the near future and to launch consultations on future tax harmonization. i am voting in favour of tax harmonization, which will lead to a single vat rate throughout the union.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of the report by mr casa, whom i congratulate on the work he has done and the cooperation he has had within the econ committee. the report proposes to extend for a further five years the current obligation for the countries of the union to apply the minimum standard vat rate of 15%. the report, in addition to stressing the importance of a minimum standard rate, goes further and stresses the need to plan a new vat strategy, as the current system, with its complexity not only in terms of tariffs, is not keeping pace with the development of the internal market. as mario monti also pointed out in his report on the relaunch of the single market, without a uniform tax system and with a different cost of living in the various member states, situations could arise that are contrary to the spirit of the single market. this puts european companies, and especially smes, at a disadvantage. moreover, the european value added tax system, as conceived and implemented by the member states, is often subject to cross-border fraud that costs billions of euros in tax revenue.

in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of the resolution. experience gained in the baltic sea using a discard system shows that this system works properly and is feasible for certain fish species. species which give rise to by-catches may have a low market value, may be completely unfit for human consumption or may be illegal to land. the basis for the sustainable exploitation of fish stocks is thus laid without the need to lower the level of marketing standards. in order to effectively prevent by-catches and limit discards of juvenile and undersized fish, it is of key importance that the fishing industry is encouraged to use more selective gear and not to fish in areas where large quantities of undersized fish and non-target fish are present. in addition, variable rest periods adapted to the reproductive cycles of fish should be introduced. the climate in the baltic sea is changing and different fish species are adapting to it, which means that their migration and reproduction cycles are also changing. in the light of these considerations, it appears necessary to revise the protected areas.

in writing. − the introduction of exotic species is one of the main elements of ecosystem disturbance and, together with the destruction of natural habitats, is one of the major contributors to the loss of biodiversity worldwide. the introduction of exotic species into european coastal seas and inland waters is in many cases due to 'aquaculture and restocking practices'. the simplification of the procedure for introducing exotic species into aquaculture should be matched by a strict definition of the requirements that closed aquaculture facilities will be required to comply with and the necessary supervision of the facilities, so as to ensure that all technical requirements proposed by the specialists are duly kept and complied with. the sustainable development of european aquaculture requires robust support for scientific research and technological development in the field of farming of native species, so as to allow diversification of production and supply of food and an improvement of its quality, while ensuring greater environmental safety. i therefore hope that strong encouragement will be given in this area.

in writing. - i abstained in the final vote on the berlinguer resolution because amendment no 2 was rejected, which is very important in order to remove possible misinterpretations of paragraph 40. it says that parliament 'strongly supports plans to allow mutual recognition of the effects of civil status acts'. the expression might suggest an obligation to recognise, for example, a union between persons of the same sex registered in a member state where such a union is permitted, throughout the european union. in fact, a distinction must be drawn between the effects of the legal act performed (in this case, the marriage) and the effects of the act of registration. the latter gives full faith to what is documented (for example that a same-sex marriage has been contracted in the netherlands) and this public faith is the effect of the civil status act. but the effects of the registered act are something else and their recognition (e.g. the survivor's pension) is not allowed in the state which does not recognise them. the question of family law is a matter of national identity and cannot be affected by community law. a possible different interpretation has led me to choose abstention.
