member of the commission. − i am strongly committed to the fight against child abuse and specifically child sexual abuse. on 29 march 2010 the commission adopted a proposal for a directive on child sexual abuse and exploitation and child pornography. this ambitious text covers prosecution of offenders, protection of victims and prevention of offences. to take account of risks brought about by technological developments, the proposal introduces in particular new criminal offences such as grooming, viewing child pornography without downloading files, online sexual abuse or advertising the possibility to abuse children, for example, through internet forums. special investigative tools should be made available, such as undercover operations for the police to infiltrate sex offender circles, and special investigative units should analyse child pornography material to identify child victims. member states should also put in place national systems to block access to internet pages containing child pornography and undertake actions to remove the content at source. we have looked carefully at the european parliament declaration of 23 june 2010, and i would be interested to know about the honourable member’s proposal for an early warning system. i have also taken note of the proposal to extend the scope of the data retention directive in order to retain data about searches made by users for child pornography material and child sex abuse content uploaded on the internet or messages used to groom children online. the data retention directive obliges communication and network service providers to retain traffic and location data and data about subscribers. it does not extend to information about content. content can be obtained and stored in the context of criminal investigations by means of the instrument known as lawful interception. lawful interception is solely governed by national law and differs across member states, but in general it can be used only if a law enforcement authority has indications that a specific criminal activity is being committed and requires further investigation. this investigative tool lies outside of the scope of the data retention directive. lawful interception occurs in the context of a criminal investigation which supposes the existence of a suspect. the data retention directive, on the contrary, obliges operators to retain certain categories of data irrespective of whether the data holders are suspect or not. extending the data retention directive to huge volumes of personal and content-related data such as internet searches for different key words in different languages, content uploaded, messages exchanged and the elements necessary to identify all users would have to withstand a necessity and proportionality case which has not yet been made. such an extension would apply to content uploaded by everyone on every platform, at any given time and on every topic. the proposal put forward by the honourable member raises serious concerns about its compliance with the principle of proportionality, even if its purpose is legitimate and deserves our full attention. the commission believes that its recent proposal for a directive would be a more suitable instrument to achieve our common objective of protecting children from child sex offenders.

in writing. mr president, the energy efficiency action plan is not a competition, where you set the bar and the constraints, but the beginning of a cultural path, a key objective of european policy designed to influence the behaviour of individuals and businesses. it is a path that is facilitated not by rigid constraints that generate costs that are difficult to sustain for both citizens and businesses, but by concrete incentives and that is concretized by energy infrastructure, changing urban development, products, packaging and transport. i would remind you that energy efficiency is considered the most cost-effective method of managing greenhouse gas and other emissions from energy production. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any evidence that the measures in question are imputable to the state. i therefore believe that it is essential not only to focus investment in this area but also to ensure that the european instruments available are effectively implemented and strengthened.

on ever better regulation at community level. the proposal, as the rapporteur has pointed out, will repeal eight obsolete directives covering six categories of legal metrology instruments, on the grounds that the instruments covered by the directive are now obsolete and that trade in them is declining. in addition, there are no barriers to trade in substitute products, which are technically more advanced and fall outside the scope of the directives. in the future, member states may wish to have national rules, but this will not create new barriers to trade as there are already international rules which fully cover these old instruments, as well as the majority of the more advanced substitute products. the world trade organisation agreement on technical barriers to trade requires member states to base their legislation on these international standards. the treaty on european union also requires member states to recognise each other's equivalent products legally marketed in another member state. the commission therefore welcomes the compromise at first reading between parliament and the council, which provides for the repeal of one directive by july 2011 and the other seven directives by december 2015. finally, the commission reiterates the joint statement of the three institutions and declares its willingness to re-examine the arguments in favour of harmonisation put forward during the legislative process. as indicated, we will report on these issues by the end of april next year and, if appropriate, submit the legislative proposal in accordance with the principles of smart legislation.
on behalf of the ppe group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i fully support the position expressed by the rapporteur on the commission proposal to repeal eight directives in the field of metrology. in particular, i welcome the proposal on whether member states should be given sufficient time to assess the possible consequences of repeal in the context of the review of the mid directive on measuring instruments. while i share the general objectives of better regulation and simplification, which are also promoted by the lisbon strategy, i believe it is absolutely important to give the member states the time they need to ensure that the repeal of the repealed directives does not lead to legal uncertainty. this would help to allay the concerns expressed by the various member states that they would not have a reasonable time to deal with the regulatory vacuum that would result from repeal. this is a good compromise between the commission's position, which is in favour of abrogating the directives outright and opposed to new regulation of the matter in the framework of the mid directive, and the critical positions initially adopted by the member states in relation to this proposal.
on behalf of the efd group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we support the report on metrology. it is a very technical text which has been awaiting a vote in plenary for months. the report, which was not opposed by the committee responsible, was rejected last march and dragged on for so long because of the need to reach agreement in the council among the 27 member states on the correlation tables. the real problem is that the european commission has not yet put forward the proposal for a directive on measuring instruments, which should replace the obsolete ones we are now deleting and regulate the matter once and for all. i would like to criticise the commission for having decided to scrap the obsolete directives without having already submitted the proposal for a revision of the measuring instruments directive at the same time. this behaviour is unjustifiable and far from the needs of businesses and citizens. at the same time, i would like to criticise the excessive fears of those who believe that the law of the member states is not able to take over during the vacatio. fortunately, european companies have a system of international rules in this area which goes beyond the union's rules. so the fears of catastrophes in the vacuum of the directive are unfounded. the companies are filling in the gaps of the legislators with their own trade organizations, with their own skills, with the rules they have set themselves to create a dynamic and balanced market. let us remember our companies which are still operating in our territory with great difficulty. we must not continue to squeeze them with taxes, bureaucracy and absurd demands. sometimes parliament's work proceeds in a hurry. common sense and the desire to reach agreements with the other european institutions go beyond political divisions.
vice-president of the commission. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, never has the debate in plenary on the safety of toys in the european union been more timely this year, especially in the light of recent events in which countries such as belgium have withdrawn several models of puzzle carpet from the market because of a concentration of formamide, a chemical classified as carcinogenic, mutagenic and toxic to reproduction, in doses considered dangerous to children's health; the commission has also been asked to provide information on the situation in the community, and to provide information on the situation in the member states. we are waiting for the national authorities to notify us of the measures taken and will then immediately evaluate the data provided through our scientific committees. if these checks confirm, on the basis of scientific data, that such a concentration of formamide does indeed represent a risk to the health of children, we will take all the necessary measures to amend the provisions of the directive to that effect by means of comitology measures. the directive - and i want to reassure mr harbour - provides for this mechanism, which allows it to be constantly updated in the light of new scientific data. the commission, for example, has already made such changes for certain chemicals - as mr weisgerber has mentioned - such as lead and cadmium, so that their values are in line with the latest scientific information. these amendments will be examined under the regulatory procedure with scrutiny and parliament will therefore be fully associated with this work. but beyond the mechanisms provided for by the comitology procedure - and i am addressing myself to mr rühle - i am personally committed to keeping you constantly informed of the progress of work on these two substances. as regards the other specific issues at the heart of the question, i would start with the scientific committee on health and environmental risks, which refers to a study carried out by the joint research centre to evaluate the method used in laboratories to detect traces of heavy metals such as lead in toys. these analyses shall be carried out in accordance with en71-3. according to the study, 40 laboratories participated in the evaluation, 15 of which are bodies notified by the member states as being competent to assess the conformity of toys within the meaning of the directive. only 3 out of 40 laboratories misinterpreted the test results. the results of these studies were communicated by the commission to the member states which had notified the names of the laboratories and to the laboratories themselves, inviting them to take appropriate measures. the study was also submitted to the european committee for standardisation for consideration in the ongoing revision of en71-3, which aims to establish a new standard by the deadline for the application of the new provisions on chemicals, i.e. 2013. as regards the new toy directive, adopted in may 2009, it is based on a new legislative framework for the marketing of products and provides for increased market surveillance. member states are required to put in place the necessary tools to ensure that only safe products are available to the european consumer. this obligation concerns both the strengthening of border controls and the efficiency of the inspection services in monitoring products already on the european market. finally, if member states find irregularities in toys, it is important that they immediately notify other countries of this information through rapex, the community's rapid alert and information system. mr harbour, the commission is cooperating closely with the chinese authorities, particularly with regard to the safety of toys. european and chinese experts in the field meet regularly to exchange information on applicable legislation and rules and administrative practices. the personnel of the chinese authorities responsible for controls are trained to improve product quality controls. as regards the limits on chemicals, mr buşoi, it is true that a method based on migration is scientifically preferable, since it is based on the real risk to which the child is exposed. but setting migration limits involves assessing risk and exposure to risk and also admitting the existence of permissible daily intakes for calculating those limits. since there are a considerable number of chemicals over a thousand and not enough information is available on all of them, this method is impossible to implement at the present stage of scientific knowledge. that said, the directive already provides for migration-based limits for certain chemicals for which scientific data are available and allows, again thanks to comitology, the possibility of introducing migration-based limits in the future in the event that additional scientific data are available for other new substances. mr rühle, as regards compounds, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, these substances can be found in various consumer articles and not only in toys. as a result, the possibility of taking specific measures is currently being tested under the wider reach regulation, and this method seems to be the most consistent and effective. toys intended for children under three years of age are subject to stricter rules. children under this age are more vulnerable and need more protection. in case of doubt as to the age for which a toy is intended, the manufacturer must apply the strictest standards. however, it does not seem justified to subject all toys to the same restrictions as those intended for younger children. the risk exposure and the use made of it are not the same. in addition, it would lead to the outright ban of certain categories of toys intended for older children and for which no risks or accidents have been recorded. this approach would be disproportionate and would be contrary to the objective of better lawmaking. the new directive also prohibits the use of substances classified as cmrs, but it was decided in this very house that a total ban without any possibility of derogation would be neither justifiable nor realistic. but if the substance does not present a health risk, for example because it is inaccessible, it cannot be banned. the assessment shall be made on a case-by-case basis on the basis of the scientific information available for each substance. more stringent limits may be adopted through comitology to ensure an adequate level of safety. the commission will not fail to propose this whenever a real risk and precise data make it appropriate. as you know, the new directive will apply to economic operators from july next year. the obligations for chemicals will apply from july 2013. the commission considers that the implementation of the new rules by all those concerned - member states and economic operators - and the incorporation of the necessary adaptations to scientific developments are a priority. in particular, member states have already met twice to discuss changes to certain chemical obligations, in october 2009 and in september this year. a further meeting is planned for april next year to conclude the work. a group of chemical experts was also set up to guide the commission and met last november with good results in defining the issues to be addressed and the options to be suggested. another meeting is scheduled for january 2011. mr harbour, on the subject of market surveillance, i will be brief in my reply to give you the answers you have requested.

in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the global financial crisis has shown the need to set up a mechanism to regulate and supervise the credit rating agencies, which are partly responsible for the crisis. to this end, regulation (ec) no 1060/2009 on credit rating agencies was adopted in 2009. that regulation has enabled the establishment at european level of a system for the registration and supervision of credit rating agencies that publish credit ratings in use in the european union. it also lays down the conditions for the use in the european union of credit ratings issued by third-country agencies, applying a dual system of credit rating equivalence and endorsement. i therefore vote in favour of the rapporteur, mr jean-paul gauzes, who proposes that the focus be on the introduction of esma into the system of supervision of agencies and the definition of its new tasks and powers. it is essential that esma is able to exercise its powers from the outset to ensure effective supervision of credit rating agencies operating in the european union as well as of third-country credit rating agencies authorised to issue credit ratings in the eu.
in writing. - repealing european directives is essentially leaving a regulatory vacuum in the community system, but modernising a system such as the metrology directives is certainly a step towards a wider and more modern common system. that is why i voted in favour of the report which repeals the eight council directives on metrology. the principle shared by the council and the commission is, however, a delicate balance because each member state will have to rely on the mutual recognition of national legislation, avoiding creating problems for industry which relies on metrology provisions, until the revision of the measuring instruments directive which will harmonise the legislation on metrology at european level is approved.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i agree with the rapporteur, mrs anja weisgerber, who welcomes the general objective of improving regulation. however, with regard to the proposal under consideration it is not clear which is the best option. in its impact assessment, the commission concludes that the examination of the various options for the eight directives in the field of metrology (abrogation tout court, repeal subject to certain conditions, no action) does not reveal a 'preferred option'. however, in order to improve regulation, the commission prefers the abrogation of all directives (and relies on the mutual recognition of national legislation) to harmonization (i.e. new regulation of the matter under the measuring instruments directive). i would like to reiterate, and i agree with the rapporteur, that she believes that more time should be given to the member states to assess whether the repeal of the directives will lead to a situation of legal uncertainty which will require harmonisation of the rules at european level.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i welcome the report by mr lamassoure and mr gurmai on the citizens' initiative. the basic rules for the operation of the european people's initiative, as provided for in the treaty of lisbon, were approved and even facilitated by this vote. a 'citizens' committee' composed of people from at least seven member states will be able to register an initiative and start collecting the necessary one million signatures, on paper or online, after the commission's eligibility check. it is an example of participatory democracy with very positive potential, where citizens are involved in the first place and join our work in a sense. the joint work of the two co-rapporteurs has shown that good work and the interests of citizens can overcome ideological divisions; the epp group is always proactive, open to dialogue and cooperation, but at the same time anchored in solid and indispensable values.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the european citizens' legislative initiative is a fundamental element in the process of building a europe based on the rights of its citizens. strict eligibility criteria, accessible and simplified procedures and the representativeness of the member states are the key elements of an instrument which restores the primacy of the value of democratic participation. in line with the union's values, the lisbon treaty gives at least one million citizens representing at least one quarter of the member states a genuine opportunity to have a real say in shaping the rules in line with the expectations of the european people. we hope that this instrument will give a boost to the prerogatives of the citizen and that we can soon reach a moment of positive verification of the results obtained and, where necessary, the necessary corrections in the interest of the citizen, to ensure further flexibility and agility to this truly innovative project. to integrate the union based on the euro with the union based on the right to citizenship of the european people.
in writing. - the text in question fully meets my expectations, particularly on three points. firstly, the minimum age for supporting a legislative initiative has been set at 18 (the minimum age for voting in the ep elections), in line with the rules for participation in direct democracy instruments such as the referendum. secondly, the need to require identity documents from resident european citizens who wish to sign declarations of support, in order to be able to carry out the checks provided for in the regulation in compliance with the legislation in force. finally, there is the need to provide for a period of 12 months for the application of the regulation after its entry into force, in order to enable the competent national administrations - many of which are faced with such an instrument for the first time - to prepare all the necessary legislative, administrative and financial measures.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i support the initiative of the rapporteurs, mr gurmai and mr lamassoure, that the organisers of the european citizens' initiative should meet in a citizens' committee composed of representatives from different member states. this will ensure that the issues identified are truly european and will also have the advantage of facilitating the collection of signatures from the very beginning. i share the rapporteur's view that the european citizens' initiative is a new instrument of participatory democracy on a continental scale. as a result, this regulation may not be perfect and practice may present new challenges for european policy-makers. i therefore agree with the rapporteurs that the commission should report every three years on the implementation of the regulation and, if necessary, propose a revision.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the report on the european citizens' initiative was voted on in plenary today. this initiative was introduced by the treaty of lisbon in article 11 with the aim of giving citizens the same powers of political initiative as those already enjoyed by the council of ministers and the european parliament. the ice is a new instrument of participatory democracy on a continental scale. on 31 march 2010, the commission presented its proposal for a regulation and on 14 june 2010 the council adopted the general approach on ice. the european parliament's committee on constitutional affairs adopted its report in november, where a negotiating mandate was foreseen. the trilogue of 30 november reached agreement on a number of amendments. the main points of the agreement concern the merging of registration and admissibility, the number of signatures to be received from at least one quarter of the member states, the creation of a citizens' committee; minimum age to support the initiative; the online collection system.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, today's vote is the first example of democratic participation in europe. the european people's initiative is one of the most innovative provisions of the lisbon treaty, a first step towards direct democracy. the initiative is a tool that allows citizens, with the submission of one million signatures, 0.2% of the union's population, to propose to the european commission to submit a legislative proposal on any issue they consider to be of interest to them. environmental and social issues and disasters caused by the financial crisis are among the most sensitive issues that can mobilise citizens to ask the eu to legislate on these issues.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the commission's work programme for 2011 calls for a further community spirit and greater courage in tackling the eu's main political and institutional issues, especially in the light of and in line with the entry into force of the lisbon treaty. the issues to be addressed include: 1. greater respect for the role of the european parliament in formulating proposals, taking due account of the positions it has adopted in its own-initiative opinions and proposals; 2. closer and more balanced interinstitutional cooperation both on budgetary matters and on the financial perspective; 3. greater courage in formulating proposals for the efficient use of community resources which will enable binding objectives and concrete benchmarks to be achieved; 4. effective and efficient community governance of the economy and finance, and financial participation by workers in the success of the enterprise, which allow for more widespread, balanced and participatory economic and social development. although the commission's 2011 programme contains only part of the above-mentioned calls, i still believe it is necessary to support it.

in writing. − the basis of democracy and of any rule of law is the protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms. with the adoption of the lisbon treaty last year, the charter of fundamental rights of the european union has become legally binding, outlining a new european legal framework in which the universal values expressed in the charter finally become concrete rights. i voted in favour of the gál report precisely because it approves the effective application of fundamental rights in the european union after lisbon. this is not only an internal step of the eu, but also an external position for the safeguarding and protection of human rights, for the promotion of peace and for the welfare of citizens, in a climate where the law guarantees serenity, security and justice.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of this report on the effect of advertising on consumer behaviour. in view of the influence of advertising on consumers and the economy, action is urgently needed to prevent certain unfair advertising practices from influencing and shaping commercial choices. the spread of new communication systems, such as the internet, requires even more attention to consumers and in particular to the most vulnerable segments of society, such as children and adolescents. our task is to counter the spread of false and misleading information but, above all, certain practices, such as spam in emails, which invade the privacy of users and their privacy. i agree with the rapporteur when he asks that action be concentrated on the suppression of misrepresentation through the extension of the existing directive. in this sense, i believe that the measure voted on today strikes the right balance between freedom of expression and consumer protection.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the evolution of the media and the development of the internet have contributed to the spread of forms of hidden advertising messages and unfair advertising practices that often invade the private sphere of consumers. it is essential to reflect carefully on the consequences this may have on the most vulnerable groups who must be protected from harmful and uncontrolled advertising. we must not forget that advertising sometimes conveys social stereotypes linked, for example, to an uninhibited conception of sexuality and violence or inappropriate messages that can adversely affect the behaviour of children and adolescents who are susceptible to influence and who do not yet have the necessary critical attitude. it is therefore necessary to update the existing legislation in this area and to ensure better implementation and interpretation of the unfair commercial practices directive. finally, i would like to stress that it is essential that consumers are properly informed about the use and processing of the data collected, especially if they are asked to provide the data in exchange for price reductions and other promotional offers. to this end, it would be useful to promote effective information campaigns on consumer rights in this area and thus try to compensate for the lack of knowledge of the problems related to the use of personal data.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, the impact of advertising on consumers is often enormous and can lead to unfair commercial practices. my decision to vote in favour of the report is a consequence of the use made of advertising in the market. it is a tool for the internal market, a lubricant for economic activities and consumers, but above all it is an important economic sector. of course, the negative aspects of advertising must also be considered: unfair practices, encroachment on public and private space, influencing the most vulnerable people, creation of potential barriers to market entry, distortion of the internal market. it is therefore important to strengthen european cooperation in the fight against unfair practices in advertising through a process of co-regulation which can improve the effectiveness and applicability of measures. i also believe that it is essential to protect the most vulnerable groups and to strengthen education and information by increasing the transparency of advertising. it would be highly appropriate to launch information campaigns on consumer rights through the use of educational tools.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i share the rapporteur, mr philippe juvin, in his view that it is important to strengthen european cooperation in the fight against unfair practices in online advertising, as demonstrated by the success of the so-called 'sweep' (systematic and simultaneous checks of internet sites by member states), which are currently limited to three areas: airline tickets, ringtones for mobile phones and electronic devices. i agree with the rapporteur that we should broaden the scope and regularity of the regulation and encourage co-regulation, which brings together the various parties concerned with legislative developments, thus improving the effectiveness and applicability of the measures.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i congratulate mr juvin on his excellent work. with the unfair commercial practices directive of 2005 failing to provide the right legal framework to combat misleading and aggressive advertising, a number of new and more persuasive forms of advertising are developing through the internet. the resolution allows european consumers to be better informed about new forms of intrusive advertising on the internet, also calls for greater protection for vulnerable consumers and underlines the role of advertising in promoting positive behaviour patterns. i am particularly concerned about the trivialization of behavioural advertising and the development of intrusive advertising practices, such as reading the content of e-mails, the use of social networks and geolocation and the repetition of advertising targeting, as they represent an infringement of consumers' privacy. i therefore ask the commission to introduce an obligation to include the term 'behavioural advertising' in such online advertising in a clearly legible way.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the andrikienė report as a whole is an excellent report, on which the socialist and democratic group has worked very hard and provided us with valuable information. human rights have been one of the founding principles of the european union since its inception and their respect is an essential point which the european parliament must promote every day. a broader understanding of human and fundamental rights, globalisation and the change in our society require a new and different vision that goes beyond the canons hitherto adopted. it is therefore essential to guarantee, among other things, equitable access to natural resources as a fundamental right of every individual. climate change will cause a huge number of refugees to flee the poorest areas of the world in the coming years, and it is our duty to begin to take account of these potential migration flows, so that we can create appropriate policies that allow us to guarantee respect for the dignity of these people. the term 'climate refugee' is not yet recognised in international law. of course, our commitment to combating desertification as an adaptation to climate change remains. these are the issues which i have tried to include in the text of the report so that a serious debate can be opened on them.

rapporteur. − madam president, the report that we considered today has been approved virtually unanimously by the committee on foreign affairs of this parliament. it is the result of one year’s work by a team which i led and is based on extensive consultations in kabul and brussels. this report is an attempt to explain a paradox: why has so little been achieved in afghanistan, in spite of nine years of international involvement? since 2001, military operations inside that country have cost more than eur 300 billion and several thousand human lives, and at least another eur 40 billion have been spent on the civilian side: in total, more than 30 times the current afghan gdp. in spite of this huge effort, afghanistan is still the number one producer of narcotic drugs. it is still one of the poorest countries in the world, where – for the majority of the afghan population – life is short, brutal and nasty, as it was in our continent five centuries ago. there are more victims of maternal mortality alone in afghanistan than the war: over 20 000 a year as against 2 300. the answer to this paradox is not simple. the opium problem and the strength of the insurgency must be taken into account, along with the belief in the illusion of a quick military victory, which dominated the early years of the international presence. moreover, the legitimacy of the central government has been overestimated, as has the efficiency of international aid in the reconstruction of the country. this report does not try to simplify all these matters. it accepts the challenge in its full dimension, and this document is an attempt to suggest new directions for our policies. the report approaches the subject from a european standpoint. this means that the afghan crisis is considered from an angle that does not simply mirror the american perspective on it. european values and principles matter. they influence the way the afghan problem is seen by european citizens, and they do not believe in a military solution in principle, because more than 65 years ago we abandoned the idea that war and occupation of foreign lands is good solution. today’s eu is built on an aversion to war, and this report reflects this feeling. on the specific issue of afghanistan, eu citizens strongly support a civilian approach as an alternative to the use of force. our approach is not naive; it is not, as has been said, venus’s softness against mars’s strength. it is instead the power of reason, of human solidarity, applied to a crisis like the afghan one that cannot be approached with a simplistic solution and mentality. this report proposes a strategy that does not exclude the limited use of coercive means. the security of the people of afghanistan from terrorists and criminal attacks is a prerequisite for development, and this parliament believes that the combination of peace-keeping interventions, multilateral diplomacy, domestic peace negotiations, effective poverty reduction measures, the establishment of democratic institutions and the protection of women’s rights are the pillars of a new, winning strategy in afghanistan as elsewhere. i hope that the strategy which is outlined here will be implemented carefully by the new system, and i take this opportunity to invite baroness ashton to join parliament in this endeavour.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i share the rapporteur's view that the enormous problems which remain in afghanistan today require a new approach, that is, a different definition of priorities than has been followed so far. i also welcome the fact that afghan president karzai has set the target of 2014 as the beginning of the period when only the afghan national security forces will conduct the military operations of the various provinces, as well as the commitment of the afghan government to gradually come to the exercise of full authority over its security. but this does not mean that the international community has abandoned the afghan cause. the cooperation with afghanistan must be strengthened in all its aspects, first of all we must promote investment in the economy because it would really mean investing in the stability of the country. this must be done in the right way, namely by establishing a model of cooperation based on inclusive dialogue between social realities and local institutions. but the main issue, as the report rightly states, is that there can be no stability or peace in afghanistan unless the state first ensures the safety of its citizens and takes responsibility. in this connection, i would ask the rapporteur to consider whether it is possible, perhaps by means of an oral amendment, to change the use of drones on the ground, that is to say, in an operational way, in the sense that one thing is to say 'the use of drones is prohibited', another is to say 'let us limit the use of this technological instrumentation as much as possible' so as not to affect the civilian population. let us meet, i believe the rapporteur has the sensitivity and the means to do so. we would be happy to support him in that.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i too join in the memory of richard holbrook. i am sure that if this report had been the responsibility of my group, the approach would have been very different from that of mr arlacchi, whom i also thank for the passion with which he has followed the afghanistan dossier for some time. it is a report which today, thanks also to the many qualifying amendments tabled by our political group, appears to be less ideological and certainly able to recognize the critical points that have been identified in these nine years, but also to recognize the positives and the most effective lines of development to be followed in order to contribute to a full re-appropriation of sovereignty by the afghan authorities. it is true that a military response alone cannot be sufficient, but we must emphasize once again that significant military successes have been achieved in recent months - we think of the operations in the areas of almando and kandahar - and that greater force against the insurgents is an indispensable prerequisite for bringing the taliban formations that we would like to bring to the negotiating table to a more peaceful council. this military commitment, and with it the sacrifice of thousands of young soldiers of the isaf contingent - among them many europeans, also many boys from my country - we must claim it with pride, because it is not only a military commitment but also a commitment to reconstruction: we are bringing schools, bridges and civil works to those unfortunate lands that serve the development of this tormented land. in this sense, despite the compromises reached, i believe that there are still some critical points in the report, in particular the one already mentioned concerning the use of drones. i think it is a serious mistake to uncritically deprive ourselves of the possibility of using this instrument which is proving very useful, especially in certain areas of the north-east of the country where it is more difficult to find and defeat the taliban militias. i hope that the rapporteur will reconsider this, otherwise i shall join my group in voting against the report.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, with the adoption of several amendments, we agree with mr arlacchi's report and with the priorities which have been highlighted in the report for the future development of afghanistan, in particular a system of transparency of financial aid, the training of the internal police forces and the fight against drug trafficking and the coordination of international aid, which are the essential points of a political and military strategy which has been further strengthened. it is important to stress once again the need to ensure control and stabilization of the territory, so that the taliban's activities are weakened, in order to give life to the peace process. i would like to conclude by stressing the contribution made by the epp group to reaching a consensus on the text. finally, i would like to pay tribute to the action and sacrifice of the soldiers of the multinational isaf contingent for their presence on the ground in defence of freedom and the local populations.

mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, with tomorrow's vote on mr szájer's report we will be launching one of the new instruments - the instrument of implementing acts - contained in the lisbon treaty. this will make it possible to simplify the old comitology system. this measure will ensure greater transparency during the adoption of acts by regulating the way in which member states monitor the exercise of the powers conferred on the commission. the fundamental importance of the regulation has complicated the legislative process, both at interinstitutional level and within parliament, where, however, thanks to the involvement - albeit belatedly - of all the committees, i hope that the proposal will be adopted at first reading. i therefore congratulate the rapporteur on having succeeded in achieving the priority objectives for the european parliament: i refer to the guarantees of alignment of the current comitology procedures with the new procedure, the right of scrutiny by parliament and the council, the creation of an appeal committee chaired by the commission and the inclusion of a review clause which will make it possible to assess the efficiency of the procedure. let me make a final comment on what has been the last obstacle to the negotiations: the inclusion of the common commercial policy in the scope of the future regulation. although the final agreement allows for a transitional period of 18 months for the application of the simple majority voting system for the adoption of anti-dumping measures, measures will be adopted by qualified majority thereafter. i am convinced that this solution, the result of a difficult compromise, meets the needs of both industry and the community executive, by avoiding dangerous politicization of technical decisions.

author of the book. - mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, today is an important opportunity to discuss a strategic issue, namely the protection of animal welfare in agriculture. as from 1 january 2012, the deadlines laid down in directive 74/99, laying down minimum standards for the protection of hens, namely the abolition of conventional battery cages as a breeding system for egg production, will come into force. this method of housing will be banned in favour of systems of rearing which ensure greater welfare of the animals. i have a vivid memory, mr president, of the agriculture council of the european union on 19 july 1999: i am glad that the commission has taken the initiative to put forward a proposal for a directive on the protection of animals during transport. now, one year after the irrevocable entry into force of the new legislation, the data indicate that european producers are proceeding with the adaptation of their production system, but not without encountering difficulties. what is needed is a concrete commitment by the commission to safeguard animal welfare, to protect producers who have brought their farming systems into line with directive 74/99 and, at the same time, to ensure that the transition to the new legislation is effectively ensured by avoiding distortions of competition on the market. that is why i and my colleagues in the european parliament have considered it appropriate to include this important subject on the agenda of the committee on agriculture, which i have the honour of chairing. the commission has been working hard in recent months, with the participation of all the parliamentary groups, and this has led to the oral question of 28 october, which raises three important questions for the commission: firstly, information on the implementation of the new legislation within the member states; secondly, measures to be taken in the member states to ensure that the deadlines laid down in the directive are met, if necessary by meeting those undertakings which show a real willingness to comply; finally, measures and guarantees to avert crises on the egg market in the coming years and to avoid unfair competition from third countries which are not obliged to comply with the european union directive on the european internal market. these are the questions to which we expect concrete and definitive answers from the commission. finally, we ask the commissioner to ensure that a more transparent market is created, based on the concept of the so-called reciprocity of rules, in order to promote the prospect of greater international convergence of the animal welfare standards applied by the european union. attention to this issue, which we have discussed several times in committee since the beginning of the legislature, is crucial to preventing european efforts - our efforts, commissioner - on animal welfare from being frustrated by a market which is incapable of recognising the social values embedded in foodstuffs. it is necessary to reduce the distortive effects of the possibility for producers outside the system of community rules to translate the lower constraints on them into greater competitive advantages. the adoption of the motion for a resolution on the welfare of laying hens which we are voting on this morning can be a first and important contribution in this direction.

in writing. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, this annual report is intended to reaffirm the european parliament's strong determination and its long-term efforts to defend human rights and democracy in the world through the development of an increasingly integrated and effective european policy, capable of ensuring greater coherence and uniformity in all areas of intervention, both through bilateral relations with third countries and through support for civil society organisations active at local and international level. we stress in particular the importance of conducting a comprehensive assessment of the human rights aspects of the european neighbourhood policy (enp), which will examine in particular the coherence and effectiveness of existing mechanisms, such as action plans, progress reports, human rights dialogues and the decision-making process for enhanced relations with non-eu countries. we want to give greater visibility to the european union's future accession to the european convention on human rights, which is an opportunity to demonstrate its commitment to the defence of human rights inside and outside its borders, and we therefore invite all member states to offer their support, to make citizens commit themselves to this.
in writing. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the report on human rights in the world in 2009 and the european union's policy on the matter is a very important tool for strengthening the role of the european external action service in human rights policy. these have always been the hallmark of the european union in the world. i agree with the rapporteur when she stresses that freedom of religion and belief is, among all human rights, a primary and fundamental right that must be respected, and that the conditionality regarding respect for human rights, provided for in bilateral agreements with non-eu countries, must be able to be imposed with greater force and effectiveness. it is therefore right to call on the high representative to integrate freedom of religion or belief into eu human rights policy and to make a thorough assessment of the situation of freedom of religion or belief in the eu's annual human rights report. i shall vote in favour of the andrikiene report.
in writing. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i congratulate mrs andrikienè on her excellent work. the parliament's annual report on human rights - this year covering 2009 - is a reference point for all those interested in the subject. this is even more important, because it is the first since the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, which gives the eu greater powers in foreign policy. the greatest hope for human rights is the implementation of the lisbon treaty in foreign policy: the external action service shall reflect the priorities and the spirit of the treaty. one of the priorities of a coherent foreign policy should be the promotion of democracy and human rights. finally, i know that parliament's annual report on human rights does not just provide a long list of problems, it also suggests solutions. we have seen the abolition of the death penalty in some countries, progress on violence against women, on the protection of children, on the fight against torture, on the protection of human rights activists, on the promotion of democracy and religious freedom, and so on.
in writing. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of the andrikiene report because i think it is necessary to stress once again that respect for human rights is the mirror of modern society. all human beings are born free and equal, and it is our clear duty to do everything possible to ensure that this opportunity is valued throughout the world. although the eu's external policy has made important progress in recent years, there is still a long way to go before a shared and coherent policy for the promotion of human rights is adopted. firstly, the council and the commission must improve the european union's capacity to respond rapidly to breaches in third countries. the european union's firm condemnation of the death penalty is a starting point for the daily struggle to win and reassert human rights. in this connection, mr president, i would like to conclude by recalling what mahatma gandhi said: 'the protection of human rights is the necessary prerequisite for peace', and this should never be forgotten.
in writing. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, this report is perhaps the best compromise that can be reached today on the new european strategy in afghanistan, thanks in part to the many qualifying amendments tabled by the epp, which have made it less ideological and more pragmatic, capable of recognising the critical points of the nine years of mission in afghanistan, but also of identifying the positives and the lines of development to make the presence of the international community more effective and to encourage the transition towards a full re-appropriation of sovereignty by the afghan authorities. it is true that a military response alone cannot be sufficient. but it is an indispensable prerequisite for weakening the taliban formations, forcing them to sever all ties with al qaeda and thus to sit down at the negotiating table. the first is that the commission has not yet taken a decision on the use of drones in the border areas with pakistan. enhance the commitment in eupol to continue training a police force capable of managing public order and step up the training of magistrates and administrative officials, in order to foster the strengthening of afghan institutions, reduce corruption and build the conditions for the return of afghanistan to afghans.
in writing. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the report on a new strategy for afghanistan is to be regarded as a positive one overall and i therefore vote in favour. the enormous problems that remain in afghanistan today, each of a different nature and all of extraordinary importance for the future of the middle eastern country, require to be addressed according to a new logic, with a different definition of priorities than what has been done so far. the primary issue, as it is correctly stated in the report we are going to vote on, is that 'there can be no stability or peace in afghanistan unless the state first ensures the safety of its citizens and takes responsibility'. in this connection, i hope that the rapporteur will reconsider the part where he talks about the use of drones, perhaps through an oral amendment.
in writing. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to congratulate mr arlacchi. the report adopted today proposes to articulate the new eu strategy for afghanistan around four key factors: full support for the peace negotiations between the karzai government and the taliban and other insurgent groups; a major training plan for the afghan police; the elimination of opium cultivation; the european union is also calling for the immediate release of the hostages and the immediate release of the hostages. as for the last point, it is noted that international aid to afghanistan ends up in bribes, forms of 'legalized corruption' and robberies of all kinds, and often finances the enemy. since 2002, the eu alone has paid the beleaguered country €8 billion and yet infant mortality has risen, literacy levels have fallen and the incidence of those living below the poverty line has increased by 130% in the last six years alone. to address the lack of coordination and transparency among international donors, the eu is invited to establish a centralised database of all eu aid and to allocate more funds directly to concrete projects in partnership with afghan institutions.
in writing. the compromise reached allows the commercial policy, including trade defence instruments, to be included in the overall comitology framework. this approach is entirely consistent with the spirit and the letter of the lisbon treaty. in particular, i fully share the need to strengthen the decision-making and implementation process by giving the commission the appropriate tools in the common interest of the eu, the member states and all economic operators. i support the principle that the commission should adopt definitive anti-dumping and anti-subsidy measures and that member states should vote by qualified majority.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, i repeat what i said yesterday in the debate and i am very pleased that amendment no 12 has been adopted, although i would have included an even more direct reference. new and innovative instruments must be found to finance the crisis mechanism. the issue of eurobonds would allow the anti-crisis facility to be financed on the market by drawing on foreign capital and investors, without any burden on national budgets. a mechanism based solely on the contribution per quota, in the form of mere provisioning of reserves, would impose a heavy burden on the states which would have to find means or capital to be deposited without, however, bringing any return or return. in a situation like the present, where on the one hand we are asking the states to implement strict budgetary policies to reduce deficits and debt and on the other hand we are asking for contributions to the anti-crisis fund, there is a real risk of collapse.
in writing. - i think it is appropriate that the commission has come to parliament today to report on the ban on the use of unmodified cages for laying hens which will come into force from january 2012. the implementation data are not very encouraging and therefore very severe action is needed against member states that have been lax in taking action in time. the banning of these cages has been known since 1999, and the member states that have subsequently joined were fully aware that they had to take steps in this direction according to precise timetables. a postponement is not acceptable. the deadlines must be respected to give credibility to the european union's action. the treaty requires the eu to set its policies with the welfare of animals as sentient beings in mind. let us not always hide behind the problem of competitiveness, which should not be seen as a question of quantity and price but above all of quality, environmental sustainability and also ethics. conscious and critical consumption must be the basis of a new economic model, which the eu must promote. the commission should therefore proceed swiftly and decisively to implement directive 74/99, which protects animals and consumers.
in writing. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, as of january 2012 the ban on keeping laying hens in traditional cages will come into force and we are alarmed by the risk that many businesses will not be able to do so. we are also concerned about possible shortages in supply and price increases for eggs, as eggs from farms which do not comply with directive 1999/74/ec will not be marketed. i voted in favour of the resolution because it is not possible to get an extension, but we have supported countries such as spain and portugal in activating an instrument to ensure a 'soft' transition for companies that have started to change their farming systems but will not complete the process before the deadline. it is not my intention to harm animal welfare and ask for an extension, but just to highlight some of the cornerstones that need to be emphasized. first, in the interests of reciprocity, the european commission is asked to implement a control system to monitor the quality of eggs imported into the eu and to ensure full compliance with european rules and standards. the member states are then urged to include measures in their rural development programmes to support the laying hens sector at this difficult stage.
in writing. − directive 1999/74 states that from 1 january 2012 conventional cages will no longer be used. european farmers will have to choose between converting their production to enriched cages (with more capacity, to allow for greater animal welfare), or raising laying hens on land, outdoors or in organic systems. according to recent surveys, 30% of farms in europe are still in traditional cages, and there are real difficulties in adapting to the new system within the time limits laid down by the directive. this is the case in italy, for example. the european commission, as well as the agriculture council of 22 february, has decided that no derogation is foreseen in the application of the ban. but an amendment to the resolution has provided an alternative solution for those producers who have already begun to replace their farming systems with new cages. that is why i voted in favour.
